# Operation catalog — @goliathdata/sdk

625 operations across 29 domains — small enough to read whole. One line each:

`operationId` (type, required scope) [flags] — what it does

Full detail per operation (variables, call example, gateway notes, response shape): `operations/<domain>/<operationId>.md`.

## account

- `clearIntakeAssignment` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Delete an owner's intake assignment for good (its people, teams, employees, workflows and rotation place); a line then falls back to the org default, and an ORG clear deletes that default, so a line with none of its own assigns nobody. owner is { kind, id }: ORG (the org id, the default), LINE (a phone line), META_PAGE (a Page id) or WORKFLOW (an EVENT workflow group). A LINE or ORG owner reads true whether or not one existed; a META_PAGE or WORKFLOW owner reads false when there was none or it is not the key org's. Admins only.
- `disconnectCallTools` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect CallTools: revokes the organization's CallTools key and the webhook automations Goliath created there, so dispositions stop syncing. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectDialer` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect a campaign dialer, provider ENZO or READYMODE, with EVERY campaign the organization linked to it (listIntegrations shows them); their calls stop syncing. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectDirectMail` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect one direct-mail provider connection by connectionId (from listIntegrations directMailConnectionQuery.list). New workflow mail sends through it are refused; mail already submitted to the provider is NOT cancelled and may still be delivered. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectFacebookLeadAds` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect Facebook Lead Ads for the key owner's own Facebook account. Goliath's access is always removed; unsubscribing the Pages and deauthorizing the app at Facebook are best-effort, so read the result: pagesDisconnected is how many Pages were unsubscribed, and deauthorized false means the user should remove the app in their Facebook settings themselves. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectPhoneEnrichmentProvider` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect a phone-enrichment provider by providerKey (provider.key from listIntegrations phoneEnrichmentQuery.providers, e.g. Trestle); phone checks through it stop. Returns its new connectionStatus. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectSlack` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect the organization's Slack workspace (the Integrations page's Slack Disconnect). Slack notifications stop. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `disconnectSmrtPhone` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Disconnect the smrtPhone dialer for the organization; its calls stop syncing. Connecting again needs the customer's own login in the app (getIntegrationSetupUrls), so confirm with the user first. Organization admins only.
- `getIntegrationSetupUrls` (query, READ) — In-app settings page URLs where a human connects an email account (Google/Microsoft) or sets up Twilio phone numbers for calling/SMS. Those setup flows are NOT available through this API — when a user asks for email or phone/Twilio integration, send them the matching link to complete it in the Goliath app.
- `getLineIntakeAssignments` (query, READ) — Each phone line's own intake assignment (who gets the contacts its inbound traffic creates); null when the line follows the org default (getPhoneRouting's defaultInboundIntakePolicy).
- `getMetaPageIntakeAssignments` (query, ADMIN) — Each Facebook Page's own intake assignment (who gets the contacts its Lead Ads create), through the key owner's own Facebook sign-in as listIntegrations reads the Pages; null for a Page nobody has configured. Only the Pages that sign-in reaches: [] when the key owner has not connected Facebook, which does not mean no Page is routed (the admin who connected it sees them). Admins only.
- `getMyCapabilities` (query, READ) — The key owner's own permissions — CHECK THIS BEFORE OFFERING OR ATTEMPTING A GATED ACTION, or saying why one is unavailable. Returns the capabilities they HOLD; one missing from the list is one they do NOT have. Seven are opt-IN, off unless a team admin granted them: VIEW_ALL_CONTACTS (without it the user sees only contacts assigned to them or their teams, the usual real answer to "why can't I see this contact"), VIEW_ALL_DEALS, VIEW_ALL_PHONES (call and text FROM any team number), CONTRACTS_VIEW and CONTRACTS_MANAGE (where a contract surface enforces them), VIEW_ORGANIZATION_SETTINGS (the organization's settings pages) and CAN_MANAGE_SPENDING (seats, numbers, the plan, invites). Eleven are opt-OUT, on unless a team admin revoked them: CAN_SKIPTRACE, CAN_EXPORT, CAN_WORKFLOW, and VIEW_TEAM_DIRECTORY (knowing anyone else is in the organization — without it no teammate names are shown, the real answer to "why is this note signed Team member"), and the app sections CAN_USE_AUTOMATIONS (workflow operations too), CAN_USE_FILES, CAN_USE_MARKETPLACE, CAN_USE_API_KEYS, CAN_USE_COMPUTER (where computer use is on), VIEW_TEAM_CALENDARS (teammates' calendars), and VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS (reading teammates' calls and texts; email only from mailboxes their owner shares). Roles are only Admin (holds them all) and Member (their own set). An EMPTY list means none held; a NULL/absent list means the lookup failed and you know nothing — never read either as the other, nor tell a user they lack a permission on a failed read. When one is missing, say so plainly and name the remedy (a team admin can turn it on) rather than attempting it and relaying the refusal, or guessing the record does not exist. Never promise the app will refuse an act their role does not allow: say what it does and let the approval card or the operation's own answer speak to permission.
- `getMyProfile` (query, READ) — Fetch the key owner's own profile — id, name, email, phone number (personal, via updateMyProfile; lines: listCommunicationChannels), profile picture URL — plus WHO THEY ARE IN THE ORGANIZATION and WHICH CLOCK THEY READ ON. organizationRole is their role (ADMIN | MEMBER): every ADMIN-scoped operation requires the key owner to be an ADMIN, so CHECK THIS BEFORE attempting one and, when it is not ADMIN, say that a team admin has to do it instead of relaying a refusal. organizationMembershipStatus is ACTIVE or SUSPENDED. organization carries the org's id, name and its own timezone (null = never set, NOT UTC). timezone is the zone the key owner CHOSE (null = never chosen, again not UTC); resolvedTimezone is the zone their times are ACTUALLY rendered on after the fallbacks (their availability schedule, then the organization's) — use resolvedTimezone whenever you state or interpret a time for them, and never assume UTC from a null. Permissions are a separate read: getMyCapabilities. Read it before updateMyProfile.
- `getOrganizationAreasOfOperation` (query, READ) — The organization's markets: `regions` and drawn `polygons`; null until set.
- `getOrganizationSettings` (query, READ) — Your organization's profile and org-wide settings in one read: name, booking-link `slug`, `websiteUrl`, `timezone` (null = never set, not UTC), `alwaysExcludeDncTexts` (texts skip National DNC numbers), `aiCoOwnedLineHeadStartSeconds`, `textReplyLinePolicy` and `callLinePolicy` (which line a text or a manual dial defaults to), `inboxDefaultView`, `suggestionAudience`, `meetingNotetakerEnabled`, `outboundPause` (null = sending is on; else when and by whom everything was paused), `leadRouting.assigneeUserIds` (who gets new skip-traced leads; empty = nobody).
- `getWorkflowIntakeAssignment` (query, READ) — One EVENT workflow's intake assignment (who owns a contact its find/create step creates); assignmentPolicy null when it has none, workflowGroup null when the id is not one of the org's workflows.
- `listDirectMailLetters` (query, READ) — The letters on contacts you can see (Automations → Letters), newest first: `totalCount`, then a page (`limit` default 50, `offset`) of contactName, campaignLabel, workflowName, mode, status (QUEUED, SUBMITTED, MAILED, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED, RETURNED, CANCELED, FAILED…), requestedAt, mailedAt, deliveredAt. Narrow with `statuses`, `modes` (LIVE; a TEST account mails and bills nothing) or `search` (a contact or workflow name). The read for "did my letters go out", "how did the last mailer do" and "did anyone answer the mail": totalCount 0 with no narrowing means no letter on a contact you can see was ever mailed (an account setup's test letter is not listed), so say that plainly and never guess. Answers show as the contact's own text, call or email afterwards, and QR scans as the `physicalMail` contact filter.
- `listIntegrations` (query, ADMIN) — Every integration on the app's Integrations page and whether it is CONNECTED, in one read: currentUser.connectedEmailIntegrations (the key owner's own Google/Microsoft mailboxes; email is per person, so a teammate's mailbox is not here), oauthQuery.slackIntegrationStatus, Facebook Lead Ads through the key owner's own Facebook account (oauthQuery.listFacebookPages: Lead Ads is CONNECTED only when a Page has connected: true, the way the card reads it; facebookAccountConnected is just the account sign-in, and a null page list means Facebook did not answer), organizationQuery.getOrganization callTools / smrtPhone / enzo / readyMode (the dialers; a connected Enzo or ReadyMode lists its campaigns), directMailConnectionQuery.list (Lob, PostGrid, OLC: state ACTIVE | PENDING_VERIFICATION | DISCONNECTED, authHealth; rows outlive a disconnect, so an empty list means no account was ever connected), and phoneEnrichmentQuery.providers (phone enrichment such as Trestle: connectionStatus ACTIVE | NOT_CONNECTED | REVOKED | UNVERIFIED). Zapier, incoming webhooks and API keys are not listed. To connect anything, send the user the link from getIntegrationSetupUrls: connecting needs their own login. Organization admins only.
- `renameOrganization` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Rename the organization. The new name is carried into the AI employees' instructions, the voice agents and the onboarding drip. Organization admins only.
- `setIntakeAssignment` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Replace who gets the contacts an owner's inbound traffic creates: assigneeUserIds (in order; 2+ rotate), participants, teams, tags, AI employees attached (agentAssigneeIds) and workflows fired (workflowGroupIds). owner is { kind, id }: ORG (the org id, the default), LINE (a phone line), META_PAGE (a Page id) or WORKFLOW (an EVENT workflow group). Send the whole policy (read it first: getPhoneRouting, getLineIntakeAssignments, getMetaPageIntakeAssignments, getWorkflowIntakeAssignment). A WORKFLOW owner takes no AI employees or workflows: send both []. Admins only.
- `setMyTimezone` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the key owner's own time zone (an IANA id such as "America/Chicago"); null or omitted CLEARS it, so their times fall back to the organization's zone (`resolvedTimezone` says which zone applies now).
- `setOrganizationAiLineHeadStart` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — How long, in seconds (0 to 3600), a person sharing a line with an AI employee gets to answer a new text before the AI replies. Null clears it (no head start). Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationCallLinePolicy` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Which line a manual dial to a contact defaults to: ASK_BEFORE_DIALING (ask when the contact last called on another line), USER_PRIMARY_LINE (the caller's own line) or LAST_CALL_LINE (the contact's last line, which widens who may dial from a line). Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationInboxDefaultView` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — What the inbox shows before a person chooses: INDIVIDUAL (their own lines) or TEAM (every line, for members who may view all phones; it grants no one that permission). Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationLeadRouting` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Who gets the new leads a property-signal skip trace creates: active members' user ids (listTeammates). One person gets every lead, two or more split them evenly, an empty list sends them to nobody. Replaces what was set; setup no longer changes it after this. Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationOutboundPause` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — "Pause everything": `paused: true` stops every automated outbound message (workflow texts and emails, AI employee texts, emails and calls, drips, mail) until it is turned off; queued work waits and nothing is cancelled. A person's own sends still go out. `paused: false` resumes. Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationSlug` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Set the organization's booking-link slug: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen, at most 100 characters. A taken or malformed slug is refused; the old slug keeps resolving as an alias. Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationTextDncSkip` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Turn "Always skip National DNC numbers when texting" on or off. On, every workflow text step and AI employee text skips numbers on the National Do Not Call registry, whatever the step says. Calls and exports are not affected. Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationTextReplyLinePolicy` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Which line a contact's text composer opens on: USER_PRIMARY_LINE (the sender's own line) or LAST_THREAD_LINE (the line the contact last talked to, which widens who may text from a line). Organization admins only.
- `setOrganizationTimezone` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Set the organization's own clock: an IANA zone the product schedules in ("America/Chicago"; EST, CST, MST, AZ, PST and HST are accepted and normalized). Null clears it. New schedules start from it; stored ones are not rewritten. Organization admins only.
- `setSuggestionAudience` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Set who contact suggestion cards go to: WHOLE_TEAM or POINT_PERSON. Organization admins only.
- `updateMyProfile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update the key owner's own profile. All three of firstName, lastName, and phoneNumber are required together (send the current values for the ones you're not changing — read them with getMyProfile); an EMPTY phoneNumber clears the number. Two more fields are OPTIONAL and PARTIAL: profilePictureUrl (an https URL to the new picture) and howDidYouHearAboutUs (free text) — omit either and the stored value is left untouched, send it to set it. The phone number is normalized and must be unique across users; email is not editable here (parity with the app). Returns the updated profile including profilePictureUrl, so quote what came back rather than assuming the picture took.
- `updateOrganizationAreasOfOperation` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Replace the organization's markets: `{version: 1, regions, polygons, updatedAt}`, a region `{kind: "county"|"city"|"zip", fips|cityId|zip, label}` (searchCounties/searchCities). Send back all you keep of getOrganizationAreasOfOperation, polygons too. An added market can buy phone numbers once the number plan buys: confirm first. Admins only.

## appointments

- `checkAvailability` (query, READ) — Live conflict check for a proposed slot: run it BEFORE createAppointment, and before moving a time with updateAppointment. Pass userIds, startDate, endDate (end after start). WHOSE CALENDARS: everyone in the appointment's userIds (teammates from listTeammates; a partner-org participant listAppointments shows on a shared appointment is accepted too) PLUS the key owner (getMyProfile): they organize, and the provider event lands on THEIR calendar whenever they are in userIds or userIds names zero or two-plus teammates, so a check without them misses the organizer's own conflicts. The one exception: userIds naming exactly ONE teammate and not the key owner puts the event on that teammate's calendar, so check that teammate alone. That exception is for CREATE only: on an updateAppointment reschedule ALWAYS include the key owner (update-time sync runs as them; a missing event created with createCalendarEvent: true lands on their calendar). When rescheduling, pass the RESULTING set: the appointment's FULL existing participant list (listAppointments) minus anyone you are removing, plus anyone you are adding, never only the additions; apply the organizer rule, and set excludeAppointmentId to the appointment being moved so it does not collide with itself. Known gap when the new window overlaps the old one and the key owner organizes without being a participant: the appointment's own Google/Microsoft mirror can show as a GOOGLE/MICROSOFT conflict on the key owner at the OLD time. Treat that row as AMBIGUOUS, never as harmless: busy ranges are merged, so a real event may hide behind the mirror; say so and have the user confirm against their calendar before booking over it. userIds are de-duplicated server-side and capped at 100 distinct participants. It reads Goliath appointments (source LOCAL) AND each participant's CONNECTED Google/Microsoft calendar live (GOOGLE/MICROSOFT), which listAppointments cannot. Returns available plus every overlapping conflicts row: start, end, source, and for a Goliath row its appointmentId and title; an external title is null unless the key owner may read that calendar (null = 'busy'). available: true means NOTHING WAS FOUND, never that the time is proven free: an unconnected calendar cannot be checked, and a provider outage degrades SILENTLY to no external conflicts, with no flag. Report 'no conflicts found on the calendars Goliath can see', name who was checked, and never promise the slot is free. A conflict is information, not a refusal: double-booking is allowed, so show it and let the user decide.
- `createAppointment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create an appointment: title, timezone, startDate, endDate; optional location, description, contactIds (accessible to the key owner), participant userIds (listTeammates), appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId (listAppointmentReminders; null = no texts to contacts, but participants' 15-minute alert still follows their notification settings; this API applies no org default, so to give it the default pass the isGlobal one's id). By default it is ALSO created on a connected Google/Microsoft calendar, which is what invites the participants and linked contacts as guests: the key owner's, EXCEPT when userIds names exactly one teammate and not the key owner, then that teammate's, as organizer. createCalendarEvent: false keeps it inside Goliath. ALWAYS read calendarSync before telling anyone it is booked: SYNCED = the event exists and guests were invited, the only state where an invite went out (else say it was recorded, not sent); NOT_REQUESTED = Goliath-only; SKIPPED_NO_ACCESS = no connected calendar could be written; SKIPPED_WRITE_BLOCKED = a provider was reachable but deliberately not written; FAILED = the provider errored and the calendar may be stale. Confirm first: title, day, time, zone, participants, contacts and, with a calendar event, whose calendar (it invites them). Double-booking is allowed and nothing here warns, so run checkAvailability FIRST over the same window with every userId plus the key owner (getMyProfile; unless userIds is exactly one teammate without the key owner: then that teammate, the organizer, alone) and show its conflicts. listAppointments is NOT a conflict check: it sees ONLY Goliath appointments. A connected calendar's event lands there only when it already maps to a Goliath appointment, is an out-of-office blocker, or has an attendee whose email matches a CRM contact; everything else (a busy event whose attendees are not contacts, a free/transparent event, any calendar never connected) is never ingested and is invisible here, and a MEMBER key sees only its own rows. So a clear listAppointments window means the GOLIATH calendar looks clear, never that the time is free; even after a clean checkAvailability, say no conflicts were found rather than that the slot is free.
- `createAppointmentReminder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A reminder TEXTS REAL CONTACTS automatically. Before calling, show the user every step's exact message and timing and wait for them to confirm that copy; never invent or reword it and send it unseen. Messages may use {{merge fields}} (the APPOINTMENT keys under MERGE FIELDS in updateWorkflowGraph's description); a step with a field an appointment cannot fill is NOT sent for it, so keep to fields every appointment has. Create a reminder: one SMS to the appointment's linked contacts per step, each sent amountBefore + unitBefore (MINUTES | HOURS | DAYS; amountBefore > 0) before its start, e.g. steps: [{message, amountBefore: 30, unitBefore: MINUTES}] for "30 minutes before". isGlobal: true makes it the org default, replacing any prior one. The org DEFAULT reminder ("Run for every appointment") is attached automatically to booking-page and AI-employee bookings and preselected in the app's appointment form; NOT to appointments created through this API (pass its id as appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId on createAppointment) nor to existing ones (updateAppointment attaches it). With none flagged and exactly ONE reminder, that one is the default anyway. So the org's FIRST reminder texts new bookings even without isGlobal; any other without it is a preset that sends for nothing until attached. listAppointmentReminders first: when one with the same timing exists, offer to make it the default (setDefaultAppointmentReminder) or edit it rather than add a duplicate.
- `deleteAppointment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete an appointment by id (from listAppointments). Also removes the synced calendar event, if any. The appointment must belong to your organization.
- `deleteAppointmentReminder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a reminder by appointmentReminderId. Its scheduled texts stop and it leaves the list and the appointment form; appointments carrying it do not block the delete, their upcoming texts just stop. If it was the default the org has none, unless exactly one reminder remains, which then is. Refused only when something else names its workflow: then pass getDeletionImpact's dependencyResolution (targetKind WORKFLOW_GROUP, targetId = this id). Confirm with the user first: it stops texts their contacts expect.
- `getMyAvailabilitySchedule` (query, READ) — The key owner's saved availability schedule: timezone, weeklyHours, dateOverrides; null if never saved: booking then uses Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00 in a fallback zone (America/New_York, or a booking form's creator's), so start a change from those hours and confirm the zone with them. Read it before setMyAvailabilitySchedule. "weeklyHours" and "dateOverrides" are raw JSON with a FIXED shape, and this text is their only documentation. "weeklyHours": one day rule per bookable weekday, { "day": 0-6 with Sunday = 0 through Saturday = 6, "intervals": [ { "start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM" } ] }; a weekday with no entry is not bookable. "dateOverrides" (optional): exceptions that REPLACE that day's weekly hours, a single date { "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "intervals": [...] } or a span { "startDate": "YYYY-MM-DD", "endDate": "YYYY-MM-DD", "intervals": [...] }; either may add "repeat": "monthly" (same day-of-month) or "repeat": "yearly" (same month/day); omit "repeat" for a one-off. "intervals": [] means UNAVAILABLE for that date or span (PTO, holidays, "block me off"). "reason": "away" is set by Away until; keep it as is. The write REJECTS the whole save (nothing stored) when: "weeklyHours" is empty (block a whole week with a "dateOverrides" span instead); a time is not strict 24-hour "HH:MM" ("9:00" and "5pm" are invalid); an interval's "end" is not after its "start"; intervals in one day or override overlap (touching, 09:00-12:00 then 12:00-17:00, is fine); a date is not a real calendar date; a span's "startDate" equals its "endDate" (write a single "date"); or a one-off span's "endDate" is an earlier calendar date than its "startDate". A one-off span may cross a month or year end with the dates in full ("2026-12-20" to "2027-01-02") — do NOT add "repeat" to make a one-time absence span the year end, that makes it recur every year. Only a RECURRING span may have an "endDate" that reads earlier than its "startDate" ("12-29" to "01-02" every year), which is how it wraps. Example of a complete valid payload: {"timezone":"America/Chicago","weeklyHours":[{"day":1,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"12:00"},{"start":"13:00","end":"17:00"}]},{"day":3,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"17:00"}]},{"day":5,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"15:00"}]}],"dateOverrides":[{"date":"2026-12-24","intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"12:00"}]},{"startDate":"2026-11-23","endDate":"2026-11-27","intervals":[],"repeat":"yearly"}]}
- `listAppointmentReminders` (query, READ) — The organization's appointment reminders: each with its `steps` (one SMS each, its message and amountBefore + unitBefore lead time, longest lead first) and isGlobal (true on the flagged default). The org DEFAULT reminder ("Run for every appointment") is attached automatically to booking-page and AI-employee bookings and preselected in the app's appointment form; NOT to appointments created through this API (pass its id as appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId on createAppointment) nor to existing ones (updateAppointment attaches it). With none flagged and exactly ONE reminder, that one is the default anyway. Attach one by passing its id as appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId to createAppointment/updateAppointment (the responses echo it under that name).
- `listAppointments` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — List appointments: org-wide for a team-admin key, the key owner's own otherwise (MEMBER keys always only their own, whatever the filters). Optional participants (listTeammates userIds, same-org), startDate/endDate, completed, searchTerm. Each row has times, location, linked contacts and participants. PAGING: this operation IS cursor-paginated, so "show me the rest" is answerable here. When canFetchNext is true, re-call with the SAME filters and cursor set to the LAST row's id to get the rows after it; repeat until canFetchNext is false. Forward only — there is no backwards page, so to revisit earlier rows restart from the top. Keep every filter identical between pages; changing one restarts the walk. total is the unpaged match count for the filters, so nothing is silently truncated. A LIST, not a conflict check: it sees only what Goliath recorded as an appointment; checkAvailability says whether a slot is actually free.
- `setDefaultAppointmentReminder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Turn "Run for every appointment" on or off for one reminder (appointmentReminderId), its messages and timing untouched. isGlobal: true makes it the org default and clears any previous one (an org has at most one); false clears it on this one. The org DEFAULT reminder ("Run for every appointment") is attached automatically to booking-page and AI-employee bookings and preselected in the app's appointment form; NOT to appointments created through this API (pass its id as appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId on createAppointment) nor to existing ones (updateAppointment attaches it). With none flagged and exactly ONE reminder, that one is the default anyway. Confirm with the user before switching it on: from then on every booking texts its contacts this reminder's copy.

Only a RECURRING span may have an "endDate" that reads earlier than its "startDate" ("12-29" to "01-02" every year), which is how it wraps. Example of a complete valid payload: {"timezone":"America/Chicago","weeklyHours":[{"day":1,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"12:00"},{"start":"13:00","end":"17:00"}]},{"day":3,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"17:00"}]},{"day":5,"intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"15:00"}]}],"dateOverrides":[{"date":"2026-12-24","intervals":[{"start":"09:00","end":"12:00"}]},{"startDate":"2026-11-23","endDate":"2026-11-27","intervals":[],"repeat":"yearly"}]}
- `updateAppointment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update an appointment by id (listAppointments): title, times, location, description, outcome; addUserIds/removeUserIds, addContactIds/removeContactIds; switch or clear the reminder with appointmentReminderWorkflowGroupId (omit = unchanged, null = clear). Only passed fields change. It must belong to your organization. Before moving startDate/endDate, run checkAvailability over the NEW window with the RESULTING participants (the FULL existing participants from listAppointments, minus any removeUserIds plus any addUserIds, never just the additions) plus the key owner (getMyProfile), ALWAYS on an update, with no single-teammate exception here: update-time sync runs as the key owner, and a missing event created with createCalendarEvent: true lands on THEIR calendar. Set excludeAppointmentId to this appointment and show conflicts. If the windows overlap and the key owner organizes without being a participant, the appointment's own mirror can appear as a conflict at the OLD time: treat it as AMBIGUOUS (merged busy ranges can hide a real event), tell the user, and let them confirm against their calendar. The edit is pushed to the external event when there is one. With none, createCalendarEvent: true creates it (how an appointment whose sync never landed reaches a calendar), on the key owner's calendar with them as organizer; it is opt-in, since a missing event may mean it was deliberately kept in Goliath, so only ask for it when that is the right host. Read calendarSync as on createAppointment: only SYNCED means the calendar matches; a reschedule that comes back SKIPPED_NO_ACCESS or FAILED left guests' calendars at the OLD time: say so instead of reporting it moved.
- `updateAppointmentReminder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A reminder TEXTS REAL CONTACTS automatically. Before calling, show the user every step's exact message and timing and wait for them to confirm that copy; never invent or reword it and send it unseen. Messages may use {{merge fields}} (the APPOINTMENT keys under MERGE FIELDS in updateWorkflowGraph's description); a step with a field an appointment cannot fill is NOT sent for it, so keep to fields every appointment has. Edit a reminder by appointmentReminderId (listAppointmentReminders). steps REPLACES the whole set: send every step to keep, with its message and timing. A step left out stops sending (booked appointments included), a kept step's scheduled texts take the edit, and a NEW step reaches only appointments booked after the edit. isGlobal: omit to leave the default untouched, true to make this the default, false to stop it being one. Only the default: setDefaultAppointmentReminder.

## askGoliath

- `answerAgentQuestions` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Answer the questions the latest reply ended on (a question or an approval) as the key owner's click would: `answers` maps each question id to a label, a list of labels, free text, or {"other": "text"}. Returns the turn (getAgentTurn). Waits up to `waitSeconds` (0-25, default 25) for the reply; poll getAgentTurn after. `confirmSends`: an approval card for a text or email carries its `draft`; trust decides if it asks.
- `cancelAgentTurn` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Stop the reply to one message (`conversationId`, `turnId`); changes it already made stay made.
- `getAgentTurn` (query, WRITE) — One message sent to Ask Goliath (`conversationId`, `turnId`): `status` RUNNING, WAITING_FOR_CALLER (answer `questions` with answerAgentQuestions), COMPLETED (a card only Goliath answers is `inAppCard`), FAILED (`error`) or CANCELLED, and the `reply` so far. `waitSeconds` (0-25) holds until the reply finishes. Ask Goliath acts as the key owner, as in the app. Needs a WRITE key.
- `listAgentConversations` (query, WRITE) [max limit 50] — The key owner's own Ask Goliath chats, newest first, with `appName` (the key that last talked in it). Continue one with sendAgentMessage. Needs a WRITE key.
- `prepareAgentConversation` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A voice assistant warming Ask Goliath up while the person is still speaking, before startAgentConversation with `spoken`. Opens no chat.
- `sendAgentMessage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Send a `message` in one of the key owner's chats (`conversationId`), as if they typed it. Returns the turn (getAgentTurn). Waits up to `waitSeconds` (0-25, default 25) for the reply; poll getAgentTurn after. `confirmSends`: an approval card for a text or email carries its `draft`; trust decides if it asks.
- `startAgentConversation` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Start a new Ask Goliath chat as the key owner with its first `message`; it shows in their chat list as "via" this key's name. Returns the turn (getAgentTurn). Waits up to `waitSeconds` (0-25, default 25) for the reply; poll getAgentTurn after. `confirmSends`: an approval card for a text or email carries its `draft`; trust decides if it asks.
- `submitFeedback` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Send our team a BUG report, FEATURE_REQUEST or QUESTION as the key owner: a one-line `title`, the `message` (10+ characters) and optional `details`. It lands on our board (added to the organization's open card for the same problem, when there is one); keep the returned `ticket` name to refer to it.

## automationMap

- `getAutomationMap` (query, READ) — Your organization's Automations Map. When there is none, this read draws it from the organization's workflows and AI employees (no agent turn) and saves it; null when there is nothing to draw. `story` (a MapStory: journeys, steps, edges and each step's detail, as JSON), `refStates` (each workflow or AI employee a step stands for, with its state now: on, off or draft, and its setup as label/value `facts`), and `changedSince` (records saved after this version: the Map may be out of date until the Automations chat redraws it). `story` null means the current version cannot be read. `pageId` and `version` are what the version ops take.
- `getAutomationMapVersion` (query, READ) — One earlier version of the Map (`pageId`, `version`), with the `story` it was written with.
- `listAutomationMapVersions` (query, READ) — The Map's version history, newest first (`pageId` from getAutomationMap): each version's number, note, when, who, and `bySession` (Ask Goliath wrote it rather than a person).
- `restoreAutomationMapVersion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put an earlier Map version back, as the Map's Versions menu does: it is copied forward as the new current version, so nothing is lost and the step can be undone the same way. Changes the drawing only, never a workflow or AI employee.

## billing

- `checkBillingAction` (query, READ) — The check the app runs before a skip trace, export or email verification of `count` records. Read `state` and `reason` first: a BLOCKED org (payment needed) shows 0 whatever it holds. For those three, `unitsAvailable` is what the action can spend, unused plan allowance (none during a trial) PLUS wallet credits (bought or granted): what answers "how many skip traces are left". For other actions it is not credits (null, or seat slots for an invite). It checks the org, not the person: skip traces still need an admin. `willTriggerAutoRecharge.chargeCents` is a card charge: say so and get a yes first; when null, mention no card. Read-only.
- `getAddOnPrices` (query, READ) — The monthly price of one extra seat, in cents, live from Stripe. Quote it, then hand over getSeatsPurchaseUrl.
- `getAiCreditUsage` (query, READ) — Why the AI employees stopped, and what AI use costs: burn over a trailing window (`windowDays` 1..90, default 30), `balanceCredits`, `outOfCredits`, `planAllowance`. THIS IS THE ONLY OPERATION THAT REPORTS THE AI PAYWALL. `outOfCredits: true` is a CONFIRMED paywall. `outOfCredits: false` is NOT proof the agents are running: the flag is deliberately narrower than the predicate that actually refuses work (AiAgentBillingGateService.isOutOfCredits), which omits its usage-history condition. TREAT `balanceCredits <= 0` AS THE STOP-CONDITION and `outOfCredits` as the confirmation. `lowOnCredits` warns (still working); give `lowCreditThresholdCredits`. `balanceCredits` can be NEGATIVE, normally. COST: `creditsConsumed` is window burn, never a bill. `planAllowance` is this period: `usedThisPeriod` of `includedCredits` is in the plan; past it, or in a trial (`lockedDuringTrial`), use draws `purchasedBalance` (bought or granted). 1 credit = 1 cent of AI cost. What used them: `aiCreditUsageBySource`; name causes only from it. To buy: getCreditsPurchaseUrl.
- `getBillingSummary` (query, ADMIN) — Read the organization's plan, subscription lifecycle, seat utilization, feature limits and credit balances. Read-only. LIFECYCLE: answer "when does our trial end" and "are we set to cancel" from the dates, never from `status` alone — `status: TRIALING` is paired with `trialEnds`, and `cancelAt` is the scheduled cancel-at-period-end (null when nothing is scheduled). A deferred downgrade is the `pendingPlanCode` / `pendingPlanIsAnnual` / `pendingPlanEffectiveAt` trio (null when none): until `pendingPlanEffectiveAt` the org is STILL on `planType`, so report the current plan and the change date. `isGrandfathered`: a legacy price, so `currentUnitAmountCents` (the core plan) can differ from the published one. SEATS: compare `extraSeats.seatsUsed` against `extraSeats.seatsCap` DIRECTLY, which is already TOTAL capacity; never add `extraSeatQuantity` (the seats paid extra for, already inside it). Open seats = it − `seatsUsed` − live non-permanent invites (listTeamInvites `isAlive`, not `isPermanent`), min 0. `featureLimits.seatsCap` is a DIFFERENT number: plan-included seats only. `extraSeats.unusedPaidSeats` null means UNKNOWN, never zero. CREDITS: `creditLedger.unitBalance` is only the PURCHASED balance, so 0 there is not "none left". For what is left read `planUsage`, one row per credit type (AI_CREDITS and SMS_CREDITS included): plan `planCap`, `usedThisPeriod`, `planRemaining`, `purchasedBalance`, and `available` (spendable now; quote it), `periodResetsAt`, `planCreditsLocked` (only purchased credits spend). Before a skip trace, export or verification: checkBillingAction. 1 SMS credit = 1 outbound text segment; inbound is free. AI burn, sources, paywall: getAiCreditUsage (READ).
- `getCreditPrices` (query, READ) — Fixed credit packs for EVERY credit type. Quote `packs` (credit type, code, units, whole-pack price in cents); skip a pack whose `available` is false. AI Agent Credits: 1 credit = 1 cent of AI cost. Texting Credits: 1 credit = 1 outbound text segment; inbound texts are free. No credit pays for mail: the provider bills the org’s own account at rates Goliath cannot see; never quote a price or range. The agent cannot buy: hand over getCreditsPurchaseUrl.
- `getCreditsPurchaseUrl` (query, READ) — The in-app Billing > Credits page URL where a human buys credits. The agent cannot buy: send this link when a balance is low or the AI paywall is hit.
- `getCreditUsageByType` (query, ADMIN) — What used the credits this billing period, per credit type: `series[].totalUnits` for AI_CREDITS, SMS_CREDITS (outbound text segments), CALLING_MINUTES, SKIPTRACE, EMAIL_VERIFICATION and EXPORT_PROPERTIES, the Billing page usage chart's own figures (each day's use, charges less that day's refunds, summed). Pass timeZone (getMyProfile.resolvedTimezone) so the days fall as the person's chart draws them; omitted, they are UTC days. A refund that lands a day after its charge is not netted, so a total can exceed getBillingSummary's `planUsage.usedThisPeriod`; quote this one as what used the credits, that one as what is left. Null before a first billing period. AI use is not split further (no per-employee figure). Read-only. Admin only: a Member is told a workspace admin sees it.
- `getPhoneNumbersPurchaseUrl` (query, READ) — The in-app Team & Phones page URL where a human registers and buys phone numbers. The agent cannot buy numbers.
- `getPlanCatalog` (query, READ) — Every plan on sale: monthly and annual (whole-year) price, and what each includes per month. Quote *Formatted; never divide *Cents. Current plan: getBillingSummary; plans change on Billing & Plans.
- `getSeatsPurchaseUrl` (query, READ) — The in-app Billing page URL where a human buys extra seats. The agent cannot buy. Decide "at cap" from getBillingSummary's `extraSeats.seatsUsed` vs `extraSeats.seatsCap` (total, purchased seats included), never the plan-only `featureLimits.seatsCap`. Price: getAddOnPrices.

## bulkTasks

- `getBulkTask` (query, READ) — Status of an async bulk task by the bulkTaskId an async op returned (addPropertiesToList and the like): status (CREATED = queued, PROCESSING = being applied, COMPLETED, FAILED = the change was NOT applied), progress (processedItemCount of estimatedItemCount) and a best-effort ETA (secondsRemaining; null = no estimate, not an error; status is authoritative). Null for an id not in your workspace. Poll every 3-5 seconds.

## callLists

- `addCallListContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add contacts to the end of a call list, so they are called after everyone already on it. Needs you to have built the list or be an admin. Contacts already on the list, including ones removed earlier (`alreadyOnListCount`), ones its own rules cannot call (`cannotCallCount`) and ones past the 10,000 cap (`truncatedCount`) are left off and counted. At most 10,000 ids per call. Refused on an ENDED list.
- `createCallList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Build a call list from contact ids, dialed in the order given (duplicates collapse). Every contact must be one you can open, or the whole build is refused. Collect the ids with filterContacts, ANDing in the condition {id: "dnc", fieldId: "doNotContact", value: false} (an OR root goes under a new AND root beside it; leave it out only when the person asked to override do-not-contact), so the count on your yes card leaves them out; a result cut short hides some rows’ flags, so never say none are do-not-contact from one. Optional build rules, frozen onto the list: maxNumbersPerContact (default 3), includeRelatives (default false), overrideDnc and overrideLitigator (default false; turning either on dials people who asked not to be called or are a litigation risk, so ask the person first), reachedTagId (a contact tag applied to everyone the run reaches). visibilityScope is USER (only you, the default) or ORG (your whole team). Pass buildAttemptKey (any unique string) and resend it unchanged on a retry so a lost response never builds a second list. A list nobody in the org can dial from (no calling line) is refused. Contacts the list cannot call (no number, do-not-contact, litigator) are left off and counted in cannotCallCount; truncatedCount counts contacts past the 10,000 cap. Returns the new list with its dialPath.
- `createCallListFromContactFilter` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Build a call list from a saved CONTACT filter (`filterId` from listContactFilters): the contacts it matches for you right now, in the filter's order, up to 10,000. The list is a snapshot; it does not follow later changes to the filter. Before the yes, count it with countContacts on a new AND root holding the filter's own tree (the root getFilter returns) and {id: "dnc", fieldId: "doNotContact", value: false} (without that condition when the person asked to override do-not-contact), and say do-not-contact people are left off. Optional build rules, frozen onto the list: maxNumbersPerContact (default 3), includeRelatives (default false), overrideDnc and overrideLitigator (default false; turning either on dials people who asked not to be called or are a litigation risk, so ask the person first), reachedTagId (a contact tag applied to everyone the run reaches). visibilityScope is USER (only you, the default) or ORG (your whole team). Pass buildAttemptKey (any unique string) and resend it unchanged on a retry so a lost response never builds a second list. A list nobody in the org can dial from (no calling line) is refused. Contacts the list cannot call (no number, do-not-contact, litigator) are left off and counted in cannotCallCount; truncatedCount counts contacts past the 10,000 cap. Returns the new list with its dialPath.
- `deleteCallList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a call list: it disappears from Call lists for everyone. The calls already made stay on each contact's history. Cannot be undone in the app, so confirm with the person first; prefer endCallList to keep a finished list. Needs you to have built the list or be an admin.
- `endCallList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Archive a call list: it moves to ENDED, stays readable with its outcomes, and can no longer be dialed or edited. Needs you to have built the list or be an admin. Refused with a CONFLICT while `lockedByUser` shows someone dialing it: end it once their run stops.
- `getCallList` (query, READ) — One call list with its progress, plus one page of its contacts in dial order: each slot's `position`, `status` (PENDING = still to call, IN_PROGRESS = being dialed, COMPLETED, SKIPPED with `skipReason`), the outcome (`disposition`), numbers tried and the contact. `limit` defaults to 50 (max 200); pass the returned `nextFromPosition` as `fromPosition` for the next page, and `statuses` to see only some slots. A list that is gone, or private to someone else, is refused with an error (NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN), not returned empty.
- `getCallListDialLink` (query, READ) — The in-app link that opens a call list in the dialer, where a person presses Start: `dialPath` is a path inside the app (`/contacts?callListId=…`). Show it to the person as a button (open_url with that path). Calls are always placed by a person in the app, never through the API. `lockedByUser` says who is dialing it right now, if anyone; an ENDED list cannot be dialed again.
- `listCallLists` (query, READ) — The call lists you can open: your own and the ones shared with your team, newest first (at most 50). Narrow with `status` (ACTIVE, PAUSED, ENDED) and with `mine` / `orgVisible` (set either and the pair is exact). Each list has its progress (`counts`: total, pending, completed, skipped, dials placed and outcomes), its frozen build rules, who built it, who is dialing it right now (`lockedByUser`, null when free) and `dialPath`, the in-app path that opens it in the dialer.
- `removeCallListContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take contacts off a call list before they are called: their slots close as skipped by hand (`skipReason` USER), so the list keeps its record. A contact being dialed right now, already called, or up next for a rep working the list stays as it is and counts in `notRemovedCount`. A removed contact keeps its slot (and its place toward the 10,000 cap) and cannot be added back to the same list. Needs you to have built the list or be an admin. Refused on an ENDED list.
- `renameCallList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a call list. Needs you to have built the list or be an admin.

## communications

- `clearChannelSuppression` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Lift an organization-wide opt-out (suppressChannel's undo): the value can be texted, called or emailed again on that `medium`, on every contact carrying it. Only on the person's own word: an opt-out is the recipient's, and lifting it without their consent breaks the law the opt-out exists for. Idempotent; a value that is not suppressed is a no-op. Returns organizationId, normalizedValue, medium.
- `clearContactDoNotContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take one contact off Do Not Contact, as the contact page's toggle does, so texts, calls, emails and workflows reach them again. Only when the contact asked to be contacted again. A value-level opt-out on one of their numbers or addresses stays until clearChannelSuppression lifts it. Returns the contact's id and doNotContact.
- `deleteVoicemailTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a voicemail drop. It leaves the dialer at once and nothing restores it: the person records it again.
- `getCallWorkspaceSettings` (query, READ) — The dialer's settings (Settings → Calls): auto-advance, the after-call actions in order, callCardFieldIds (contact custom fields shown on the call card) and callerIdTableColumnId; plus a person's voicemail drops (userId, default the key owner).
- `getMeetingTranscript` (query, READ) [max limit 300] — The full speaker-by-speaker transcript behind a meeting-summary note, as a PAGEABLE window of ordered { speaker, text } utterances. When the Goliath notetaker attends a meeting, the summary lands as an AI note on each meeting contact and the complete transcript is archived separately — this operation reads that archive. Pass the noteId of the meeting-summary note (from getContact notes[] or a NOTE entry in listContactActivities). Use it whenever the summary is not enough — extracting commitments, action items, exact quotes, pricing figures, or who-said-what. PAGE THE WHOLE MEETING before concluding: a full page (as many utterances as you asked for) means more remain — request again with offset advanced by the count you received until a short page arrives. Action items cluster near the END of a meeting, so an unpaged first window is exactly the wrong place to stop. Returns null (not an error) when the note is not a meeting-summary note, the note is hidden from the caller, or no archive exists; a null on a random note means "this note has no meeting transcript", not a failure. The meeting notetaker is feature-flag gated per org — where the flag is off this operation is refused, which also means no workspace has summary notes to point at it. Quote selectively rather than echoing whole pages back to the user.
- `getSendConsentAttestation` (query, READ) — Whether the organization's send consent attestation stands: an org admin's one-time statement that every contact the organization texts or emails through the developer API consented. Every operation that messages a contact (sendText, sendEmail, accepting a card that sends, a contract's emails to its signers) is refused (403 send_consent_not_attested) until `attested` is true; `attestedAt` and `attestedByUserId` say when and who. Set it with setSendConsentAttestation (ADMIN).
- `getSendingLimits` (query, READ) — How much can we text and email today? Per line, brand (team) and mailbox: used / cap / remaining today (text segments; null cap = no limit; a mailbox also meters recipients, and the tighter of its two binds), a line's last-7-day volume, and the sending queue. Read-only. Count only lines with canSendSms and not isBurned. textingReadiness is the org's texting registration: canText, and reason when not (NO_REGISTRATION = none filed; MANAGED_* = Goliath-managed registration in review or failed; BYO_* = their own Twilio account). Read it first for a registration question; never fill in or submit one for them.
- `getTextingRegistrationStatus` (query, READ) — The organization's A2P 10DLC texting registration, STATUS ONLY: each brand (`status`, `statusLabel`, `useCaseLabel`) and its sending campaigns (`sendReady` true = approved and able to text; `rejectionReasons` when a carrier refused it). Read-only: registering, resubmitting or retrying happens in the Goliath app (Settings → Phone → Registration). For whether the org can text at all right now, listCommunicationChannels' textingReadiness.
- `listCommunicationChannels` (query, READ) — What can I send from? All the organization's phone lines (each with its user and canSendSms) and your mailboxes; your lines have user.id = currentUser.id. "My number" to text from or give a teammate is one of these, not getMyProfile.phoneNumber. canSendSms is line setup only: while organization.textingReadiness.canText is false nothing texts, so never say a line can text; say what its reason value says to do. myDisconnectedMailboxes lost connection (disconnectedAt): say disconnected, reconnect; never no mailbox.
- `listMeetingSummaries` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — The organization's notetaker calls created after `after`, in any status, oldest first: each call's status (COMPLETED and FAILED are terminal), summary note id and text (null when the key owner may not read it), who sent the notetaker, the appointment title, and the meeting contacts with the contacts connected to each. At most 50 per page; advance `after` to the last `startedAt`. Read a call transcript with getMeetingTranscript(noteId).
- `renameVoicemailTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a voicemail drop (templateId from getCallWorkspaceSettings).
- `renderContentTemplate` (query, READ) — Render a content template against a contact: collapse [a|b] spintax and substitute merge fields — the CONTACT vocabulary updateWorkflowGraph lists ({{firstName}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{userFirstName}}, …), matched exactly and case-sensitively. Returns the rendered subject/body plus missingVariables — every token that did NOT render, whether it had no value for this contact or could not render at all because contactId was omitted (contact tokens then remain as literal {{...}} text AND are listed as missing). Inspect missingVariables (empty = fully rendered). Send with sendText / sendEmail (behind the organization’s send consent attestation). Pass spintaxSeed for a deterministic variant. Omitting contactId previews spintax and user tokens only — never send a no-contact render of a template with contact tokens.
- `reorderAfterCallActions` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Order the after-call actions the dialer offers: items list every kind once with its displayOrder. Admins only.
- `reorderVoicemailTemplates` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the order of a person's voicemail drops: items are { id, displayOrder } for that userId.
- `sendEmail` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Send an email as the key owner through their connected Gmail/Outlook mailbox. NEEDS THE ORGANIZATION'S SEND CONSENT ATTESTATION, like sendText: refused with 403 send_consent_not_attested until an org admin attests (setSendConsentAttestation), and with 403 outbound_paused while the org has paused everything. IMPORTANT: bodyHtml is the authored content, not necessarily the complete delivered Gmail body — appendSignature defaults to true, so Goliath appends the sending mailbox's default signature when one is available: on Gmail its synced/default Gmail signature, on Outlook the first signature the owner keeps in Goliath for that mailbox (unless they default to no signature). Set appendSignature to false when bodyHtml must be the complete email with nothing appended. fromClientId + fromEmail identify the sending mailbox — get them from listCommunicationChannels. contactId (optional) attaches the email to that contact timeline; a Do-Not-Contact-blocked contactId returns a GraphQL error (the one failure that is not ok:false) and releases any Idempotency-Key for a corrected retry. On any other failure ok is false and failureReason + failureMessage explain why (NO_CONNECTED_MAILBOX, INVALID_SENDER, MAILBOX_MISSING_SEND_SCOPE, or PROVIDER_SEND_FAILED). No attachments or threading in v1.
- `sendText` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Send an SMS to a phone number (E.164, e.g. +13235550100; an unparseable number is rejected up front with INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER) as the key owner. NEEDS THE ORGANIZATION'S SEND CONSENT ATTESTATION: until an org admin attests once that every contact the organization messages through the API consented (setSendConsentAttestation; read it with getSendConsentAttestation), this is refused with 403 send_consent_not_attested, and while the org has paused everything it is refused with 403 outbound_paused. Runs the checks the app's composer runs: opt-out and Do-Not-Contact guard, A2P active-campaign gate, send throttles and daily caps, find-or-create contact from the number, and conversation + activity logging. A 200 response is NOT delivery — check status: FAILED or SKIPPED means the message never reached the contact (errorCode/errorMessage say why) even though the row is returned without a GraphQL error. Omit fromPhoneLineId to use your assigned line; sending from another user's assigned line requires the VIEW_ALL_PHONES capability (org-shared bulk lines are usable by any org member without it; another organization's line is never usable). Call listCommunicationChannels first and pick a line whose canSendSms is true.
- `setCallCardFields` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace the contact custom fields shown on the call card (at most 8, in order). Admins only. Send the whole list.
- `setCallerIdTableColumn` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the PHONE_LINE Workflow Table column the dialer reads each contact's outbound caller ID from (listWorkflowTables), or null to stop. Admins only.
- `setSendConsentAttestation` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Attest (`attested: true`) or withdraw (`false`) the organization's send consent: the org admin who owns this key states, once for the whole organization, that every contact it texts or emails through the developer API consented to be contacted. It opens the operations that message contacts (sendText, sendEmail, and accepting a card that sends, a contract's emails to its signers) to the organization's developer-API keys; it replaces no check — every send still runs opt-out, Do Not Contact and A2P registration, and Pause everything still holds them. Only on the admin's own word: never attest for them. ADMIN scope; the key owner must currently be an org admin. Returns attested, attestedAt, attestedByUserId.
- `suppressChannel` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Value-level opt-out: block a phone number or email address for your organization on one medium (SMS, VOICE or EMAIL). Keyed on the normalized VALUE, not a contact: every contact carrying it, now and later, is blocked on send. SMS/VOICE take a phone in any format, EMAIL an address; an unparseable one is rejected (INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER / INVALID_INPUT). Idempotent. Blocks only the medium named (send VOICE too for calls). A person in the app clears it, or a developer-API key with clearChannelSuppression. Returns organizationId, normalizedValue, medium.
- `updateCallOutcome` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Record or correct a call's outcome (disposition) and its note (at most 280 characters), as the dialer's outcome gate does. By callSid, or by contactId for the key owner's latest outbound call to that contact. Sends nothing.

## contactImports

- `authorContactImportMapping` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Bring an import from startContactImport to a ready mapping when it was not ready yet (transformerAuthoringState IN_PROGRESS, or hasAuthoredTransformer false). It returns at once when the mapping already exists. Same result fields as startContactImport. Nothing is imported.
- `confirmContactImport` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Import every row of the spreadsheet as contacts: the step the Import page’s Import button runs. Rows that match an existing contact update it instead of duplicating it. Every import puts its contacts on its own list, “Contacts from <file name>”; tagName adds a second list of that name (optional; a list, not a tag), so pass it only for a list the person named or picked, never one you made from the file’s name. attestationAccepted records that the person affirmed they have a lawful basis to contact everyone on the list; the import is refused without it, so pass true only on their yes (in a chat, their yes on the import task’s approval card, which shows the attestation). reviveArchivedMatches (default true) restores archived contacts the file matches. optOutTagName is the tag the mapping puts on the file’s opt-outs (a DNC column or tag, for example "DNC"): when the import finishes, every contact it imported that carries that tag is marked Do Not Contact, as part of the import, so nothing waits on it to mark them; omit it when the file marks nobody. Only after the person has seen the preview and said yes to importing this file, with this list. It starts a background task and returns at once; the chat that started it is told when it finishes, so never wait on it.
- `getContactImport` (query, READ) — The status of an import: status (CREATED and AUTHORING_TRANSFORMER = not confirmed yet, PENDING_PROCESSING and PROCESSING = importing, COMPLETED, FAILED, NOT_ENOUGH_BALANCE), totalRows, the contacts produced so far (producedRecordsCount), a best-effort estimatedRemainingTimeInSeconds (it runs high early in an import, so never promise a time from it: the chat that started the import is told when it finishes), the upload’s own list (contactTag, named for the file; not the list the person chose), and the results report: created, matched (an existing contact updated, or one an earlier row of this same file made), duplicateRowCount (rows that repeat an earlier row of this file), mergedAfterImportCount (the duplicate rows whose new contact was merged into an earlier row’s after the import; the rest of the duplicates count as matched, so contacts they already had = matched - (duplicateRowCount - mergedAfterImportCount)), restored (an archived match brought back), skipped and failed rows, and processedRowCount. One read answers "how is it going". For an import this chat started, the chat is told when it finishes, so a code task never polls it; for one started elsewhere (Files, another chat), poll every 10 to 30 seconds.
- `getContactImportRowFindings` (query, READ) — The rows of an import whose phone the import cannot store (not a full US number): they come in without that phone. unstorablePhoneRowIndexes are 0-based, so row N is index + 1; checkedRows is how many of the file’s first rows were checked (up to 100): past them nothing was checked, so say so. Null when the check could not run. Read it once for the finish report (W20 BP14).
- `previewContactImport` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — The first rows of an import as the contacts they will become, in the app’s own fields: name, phones, emails, property addresses, mailing addresses, tags, lists, deals, and custom fields (every custom field of the workspace is listed; the ones with values are the ones this row fills). contactTransformerRowCount is the number of rows the import will read. A row with error set and no contact will be skipped. contactTransformerRowFindings names the rows to tell the person about before they approve the import: a likely repeat of an earlier row (the same name and a shared phone or email, or for a nameless row a shared phone or email; the import usually merges it into that contact, so say it likely will, never that it will) and a row with no name (it lands under its phone or email), with 0-based row indexes, over the file’s first checkedRows rows; null means the check did not run, so never say the file has no repeats. limit is 1 to 10 (default 8). Show these rows to the person as a table, one row per contact, a column per field that any row fills, and say how many rows the file has. Read only; nothing is imported.
- `reviseContactImportMapping` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change how an import maps the spreadsheet’s columns, in plain words: message is the change the person asked for (for example "the Owner 2 column is a second contact name, not a note" or "put the Lead Source column in the Source custom field"). Re-runs the import mapper, which takes up to a few minutes; read the result again with previewContactImport. Nothing is imported.
- `startContactImport` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Start importing contacts from a spreadsheet the person attached to the chat. Pass artifactId, the shelf id the chat names for the file (`[shelf id …]`). It creates the same upload the Import page creates (it shows on the Files page) and runs the import mapper on it, which takes up to a few minutes, then returns the import (its id is the fileProcessingTaskId every other contactImports operation takes), the file row count (totalRows) and its columns with example values (csvSample). Nothing is imported yet. transformerAuthoringState COMPLETED with hasAuthoredTransformer true means the mapping is ready: read it with previewContactImport. IN_PROGRESS means another mapping run on this upload is still going: wait a little and call authorContactImportMapping. Only .csv, .xlsx and .xls files can be imported (spreadsheets are stored as CSV). Call it once per file and keep the id; a second call for a file whose import is not confirmed yet returns that same import.

## contacts

- `acceptContactSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Accept a contact's suggestion card as written: a reply card SENDS its text or email to the contact; another card applies its action. Only when the person asks for THIS card by name, by its suggestionId; when their trust for the card's kind asks first, the write says how to ask. Leave `senderUserId` out: it names a customer reply's sender and is refused on any other card; Ask Goliath sends only as the person. In Ask Goliath `acceptPairedActions` is refused (accept each paired card on its own); over HTTP it also accepts them, and `replyInThread` answers in the email thread.
- `acceptEditedContactSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Accept a text or email reply card with the person's own words (`text`) in place of the draft; it SENDS. Only when the person asks for THIS card by name, by its suggestionId; when their trust for the card's kind asks first, the write says how to ask. Leave `senderUserId` out: it names a customer reply's sender and is refused on any other card; Ask Goliath sends only as the person. In Ask Goliath `acceptPairedActions` is refused (accept each paired card on its own); over HTTP it also accepts them, and `replyInThread` answers in the email thread.
- `addContactCustomFieldOption` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add one option to a contact DROPDOWN field (listContactCustomFields). Never drops an option; a label already there (any case) is kept as-is.
- `addContactExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add a titled URL to a contact's Links card (getContactConnections externalLinks): a web address, or an app path starting with / (it becomes the app's own URL). Never for a Library file or page: those go on the contact's files with fileLibraryItemsOnContact.
- `addContactNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add a text note to a contact, synchronously (getContact returns it at once). The response is the OWNING CONTACT, not the note (`id` and `name` are the contact's), so report the name it gives back, never the name you searched for. They differ more often than they look: contactId usually comes from a findContacts search, which ranks and can return a near match for a name with no exact one. A run that wrote to the top row and told the user the note landed on the searched name has reported a record it did not touch, which nothing downstream catches. If the echoed name is not the contact the user named, say so and offer to move the note. Returns no noteId: re-read getContact notes[] for one (see editContactNote).
- `addContactsToList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add contacts to one or more LISTS (segments) by list id (searchContactTags `lists` / createContactList): the selection-wide form of updateContact’s addToListIds; removeContactsFromList is the twin. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask; an immediate read-back will not show the change. A contact already on the list is skipped, not failed, so re-running is harmless. LIST ids only: a free-form tag or custom-field id is refused at the gateway (the underlying worker would silently drop it and complete having changed nothing). POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND: list membership publishes the same tags-changed event tags do, so a CONTACT workflow triggered on this list can start a run and send. Check the org’s workflows or confirm with the user before a large selection.
- `addContactTags` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add tags to contacts: existing ones by `tagIds` (searchContactTags), new ones by exact name in `newTagNames`, created as this runs, never createContactTag first. removeContactTags is the twin. Async bulk job: poll `bulkTaskId` with getBulkTask; a read-back right away will NOT show it. POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND: a CONTACT workflow whose trigger names a tag starts a run that can text or email; on a large selection check first (listWorkflows { status: ACTIVE, triggerType: [MATCH, MUTATION] }, then their graph `triggers`).
- `archiveContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Archive (soft-delete) contacts by id. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask. Archived contacts drop out of the CRM but are recoverable: unarchiveContacts restores them (bulk), updateContact(isArchived: false) one. Nothing is destroyed: notes, activities, tags and deals survive and come back with the contact.
- `assignContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Assign a teammate to contacts (get userId from listTeammates). role defaults to POINT_PERSON; pass PARTICIPANT for a secondary assignment. The removal twin is unassignContact. Async bulk job — returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask.
- `changeNotePinned` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pin (isPinned true) or unpin a note (getContact notes[]); any teammate may. A pin notifies the contact's teammates.
- `clearContactPhoto` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove a contact's photo; the image stays on the contact.
- `commentOnSuggestionCard` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Comment on a suggestion card ("too pushy"). Nothing on the card changes and nothing is sent; the employee reads it when it drafts its next card. submissionKey: a new one per comment (1 to 100 characters), resent unchanged on a retry.
- `contactListUsage` (query, READ) — EVERY list in ONE call, import uploads ("Contacts from … .csv", kind UPLOAD) and exports included, emptiest first: contactCount (unarchived you see), orgActiveContactCount / orgArchivedContactCount and isEmpty (no unarchived contact in the org; null unless you can view all contacts). onlyEmpty and kinds narrow it. Use instead of a countContacts per list. Tags are contactTagUsage.
- `contactTagUsage` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Free-form tags, least-used first: contactCount (visible, unarchived), orgContactCount (org, +archived; null w/o view-all: 0 proves nothing), dependents. maxContactCount 0 = unused (view-all). filterTree: MATCHING contacts per tag, carried tags first, no org count/dependents. Never countContacts per tag; getDeletionImpact before deleting.
- `controlContactsWorkflowRuns` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PAUSE or RESUME the workflow runs of contacts (optional workflowGroupIds narrows it). RESUME restarts only runs someone paused by hand on a workflow version still active; other runs are skipped. A bulk task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). The person approves it on a card.
- `convertSubContactToLinkedRelationship` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Promote a relative (getContactConnections subContacts id) to its own contact, linked back as a related person; returns the link with `linkedContactId`. linkToExisting: true links the org's existing contact for the same person instead, and is refused when there is none.
- `countContacts` (query, READ) — The number of active contacts visible to you, in one call: the total the Contacts page shows (archived and hidden contacts excluded). Use it for any count-shaped question; never page through findContacts to count. With no arguments it is the total VISIBLE TO THE KEY OWNER, the org-wide total only for an owner holding VIEW_ALL_CONTACTS (applied with or without a filterTree), so never report it as the organization's total unless you know the owner sees every contact. Takes an optional filterTree (saveFilter's DSL), never filterId: a saved filter's count is filterContacts' `total` with its filterId. NEVER save a filter to measure one. A status word ("called", "hot", "dead") can name the org's own tags: searchContactTags for it before you count by an activity or system field alone, and count each reading you find. A count is the answer, 0 included: never re-derive it by paging. Archived contacts are excluded, so 0 means no ACTIVE match. To see how a condition treats empty values, run filterContacts once.
- `countRecords` (query, READ) — Count records grouped by any field in ONE call: tasks per contact or per teammate, mine vs others, contacts by source, deals by stage. Use it instead of paging a list op or a code task to tally. `spec` = {from, groupBy (up to 6), measures, where (equality; an array = any of; null = unset), orderBy [{by, dir}], limit (default 500), since/until (ISO, "now", "-30d")}. Values match exactly: statuses are UPPERCASE (tasks: UPCOMING, OVERDUE = past due now, earlier today included, COMPLETED; open tasks = completed false). Counts only what the caller may see. Contacts per TAG are contactTagUsage, one call; contacts.owners groups by the whole owner set, not per owner. Answers {ok, result: {rows, truncated}} or {ok: false, error}. Models: contacts (group: owners, source, doNotContact, lastActivityType, archived, stage, buyer, buyerStatus; measures: count, replied; time createdAt) · tasks (group: contactId, contactName, assigneeId, assignee, mine, completed, status; measures: count, rows; time dueAt) · deals (group: pipelineId, pipeline, stageId, stage, outcome, archived, workflowId, employeeId, teammateId, origin, assignees; measures: count, valueCents; time createdAt) · pipeline (group: pipelineId, pipeline, stageId, stage, stageOrder, outcome; measures: deals, valueCents, openDeals, openValueCents) · appointments (group: completed, cancelled, workflowId, employeeId, teammateId; measures: count; time startAt) · leads (group: source; measures: count; time at) · properties (group: contactId, contactName, relation, zipCode, state, propertyType, bedrooms, ownerOccupied, countyFips, county, ownedSince, ownerPropertyCount, wrongLink, archived; measures: count, properties, contacts, avgEstimatedValue, medianEstimatedValue)
- `createContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a contact; needs sellerFirstName, sellerLastName, and type (LISTING | INVESTMENT | BUYER | UNDETERMINED); phones/emails optional. Search findContacts by the name and each phone/email first: a match is a same-person-or-new question for the user BEFORE creating.
- `createContactCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create an org-wide contact custom-field DEFINITION (name + type: TEXT | NUMBER | DOLLAR | DATE | LINK | DROPDOWN; `options` required for DROPDOWN; `allowMultiple` optional), synchronously. Returns the org custom-field catalog: find the new id by name (or listContactCustomFields), then write values via addCustomFieldValues (createContact) / updateCustomFieldValues (updateContact). A defaultValue fills every contact lacking a value, archived too, and stays if later changed; nothing counts them: ask first.
- `createContactFromProperty` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Create a CRM contact from a property (id/esId). It runs skip-trace enrichment on the property and CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT (plan allowance first except in a trial, then real money; checkBillingAction): ADMIN scope, and the key owner must be a team admin. Returns the property with its linked contacts, the new one included.
- `createContactList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create an org-wide contact list (segment), synchronously. Returns the org list catalog: find the new id by the name you gave (or searchContactTags). Fix a name with renameContactList; fill it with addContactsToList.
- `createContactTag` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create an org-wide free-form contact tag, synchronously. Returns the org tag catalog: find the new id by the name you gave (or searchContactTags). To fix a name use renameContactTag, never a second tag.
- `createNoteReply` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Reply to a note (getContact notes[]) as the key owner; AI employees cannot. Notifies the thread, by text too (a hidden note's: Goliath staff only). Returns the replies: find yours by author and createdAt.
- `decideContactSuggestionsInBulk` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Accept or dismiss many cards at once (`verb` ACCEPT or DISMISS, `suggestionIds` at most 500): each runs as its own Accept or Dismiss would, so an ACCEPT can send a reply per card. An id the key owner may not act on is dropped from the plan, not reported. `dismissReason` for a DISMISS. `rowDecisions` answers one card's own question for an ACCEPT ({ suggestionId, decisions }). Returns planned, applied, refused, truncated (only the first `planned` ran: call again) and unresolvedIds. An ACCEPT whose answer spends credits is refused (the app's costed bulk accept). Behind the send consent attestation and Pause everything, a DISMISS too.
- `decideSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Accept or dismiss any card in the suggestion feed — a contact's, an AI employee's or an account card — by its id (`verb` ACCEPT or DISMISS), the same door Work through uses. DISMISS takes `reason` and optionally `note` (their words). An account card's ACCEPT runs only the actions named in `selectedProposalKeys`; a card with a question of its own takes its answer in `decisions`. Accepting a reply sends it, under every gate the app's Accept runs; an account card's accept needs an org admin. Only on the person's word. Behind the send consent attestation and Pause everything, a DISMISS too. Returns id, kind, status.
- `deleteContactCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Permanently delete a contact custom-field DEFINITION (id from listContactCustomFields). DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: every value recorded on every contact for it is deleted, NOT moved to another field. Prefer updateContactCustomField when the field is merely wrong rather than unwanted. Call getDeletionImpact first (targetKind CONTACT_CUSTOM_FIELD, targetId the field id): it reports how many contacts hold a value and which filters/workflows reference the field, and returns the impactVersion to hand back as dependencyResolution.impactVersion (with an empty `replacements` array when it reports no replacementRequirements). A required replacement redirects those filters/workflows to another field; it does not carry contact values over. The impactVersion goes stale if anything changes in between: re-read the impact and retry rather than reuse an old one. System-defined fields (e.g. Buyer/Seller) cannot be deleted. Confirm with the user before calling.
- `deleteContactFilter` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY delete a saved CONTACT filter by id (from listContactFilters): no archive, no undo. Returns true when a row was deleted; a foreign or unknown id is rejected, and a property or deal filter id is refused with nothing deleted. WHOSE FILTER IS IT: listContactFilters returns `userId`, the owner. A TEAMMATE'S shared filter is deletable when the key owner is an org admin, so check `userId` against getMyProfile (`currentUser.id`) first and say whose it is.
