A teammate's PRIVATE filter is refused outright. If the filter is merely wrong rather than unwanted, updateFilter (properties domain; it edits contact filters too) fixes it in place.
- `deleteContactLists` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete contact lists by id (from createContactList), dropping their membership. IRREVERSIBLE: prefer renameContactList when only the name is wrong, and removeContactsFromList when the list should just not hold those contacts; this is for retiring the list. A list referenced by filters/workflows needs a dependencyResolution from getDeletionImpact (targetKind CONTACT_LIST); an unreferenced one needs none.
- `deleteContactNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY delete a note (by noteId): it leaves the contact's timeline with NO undo, so ALWAYS show its text and get their yes; a card counts. When only the wording is wrong use editContactNote, which is reversible. noteIds come from getContact (notes[]) or a NOTE entry in listContactActivities. One note per call; no bulk delete. Returns the owning contact with its REMAINING notes (the deleted one gone), so confirm the removal and show what is left rather than assert it worked. You can only delete a note you authored (or any note, if the key owner is a team admin); a note whose `author.kind` is AI is someone else's, so a NON-ADMIN key is refused on one.
- `deleteContactTags` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete free-form contact tags by id (from createContactTag), removing them from every contact. IRREVERSIBLE and org-wide: prefer renameContactTag when the name is merely wrong, and removeContactTags when the tag should only come off some contacts; this is for retiring the tag itself. Free-form tag ids only (custom fields, lists and system-defined rows are rejected). A single-tag delete needs a dependencyResolution from getDeletionImpact (targetKind CONTACT_TAG): its impactVersion plus any replacements. A multi-tag delete accepts only tags with no dependencies; delete a depended-on tag on its own.
- `deleteNoteReply` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a reply for good. Same authorship rule as editContactNote. Returns the replies left.
- `dismissContactSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Dismiss a suggestion card with the reason the person gave (NOT_RELEVANT, WRONG_TONE, WRONG_FACTS, ALREADY_DONE, OTHER, …). Recorded through the API, not as feedback heard from a person.
- `duplicateContactsByRep` (query, READ) — findDuplicateContactGroups tallied per assigned rep (point person) in ONE call: per rep, groupCount (groups holding one of their contacts) and contactCount; userId null = unassigned. totalGroups, truncated (past 500 groups).
- `editContactNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rewrite an existing note's body (by noteId). REVERSIBLE: the note keeps its id and timeline position, so a wrong edit can be edited again, and no permission is needed when the user asked for a correction. Pass the FULL replacement body: it replaces the text, it does not append. noteIds come from getContact (notes[]) or a NOTE entry's note payload in listContactActivities; addContactNote returns none, so re-read the contact for the note you just wrote. The response echoes the saved body and updatedAt plus the owning contact (id + name): quote the corrected text back rather than assume it took. Only a note the key owner wrote, unless they are a team admin; a note whose `author.kind` is AI is someone else's, so a NON-ADMIN key is refused on one: check the author before offering to correct a note.
- `editNoteReply` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace a reply's body (replyId from getContact notes[].replies); echoes the saved body. Same authorship rule as editContactNote.
- `enrichContact` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Skip-trace a contact to discover phone numbers and emails. CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT (plan allowance first except in a trial, then real money; checkBillingAction) — requires the ADMIN scope, and the key owner must be a team admin.
- `filterContacts` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Run a contact filter and paginate the matches with limit/offset. Returns a page of contacts (name, tags, phones, emails, `doNotContact`, reason, date, linked `properties`: no getContact per row) plus total and hasMore. Pass EITHER filterId (a saved filter from listContactFilters) OR filterTree (saveFilter's filter-tree DSL; conditions key `fieldId`, not `field`) to run an UNSAVED tree: same path and totals, nothing saved. filterTree verifies a filter before creating it and settles what a condition does (fetch a record with no value for the field and see whether the tree returns it). NEVER save a filter to measure one; save only the one asked for. Sort with sort: { field, direction } (`ASC` / `DESC`); field is a CLOSED vocabulary: `NAME` (A–Z), `SELLER_INTENT_SCORE`, `LAST_COMMUNICATION`, `LAST_ACTIVITY`, `DIAL_ATTEMPTS` (org-wide dials), `MY_LAST_CALL`, `MY_LAST_TEXT`, `LAST_UPDATED`, `CREATED_AT`, `TASK_HIGHLIGHT`, `AUCTION_DATE` (earliest upcoming auction; none sort last). Any other field is silently IGNORED. `participants`: its assignees (REVOKED: no longer assigned).
- `findContactDataProblems` (query, READ) — Contact data problems in ONE call, never contact by contact: EMAIL_NOT_LOWERCASE, NAME_EMPTY, NAME_ONE_WORD (a first or last name missing; which is unknown), PHONE_NOT_NORMALIZED (not the 10-digit form phones are stored in; well-formed numbers are shown formatted, never stored so). Each: count of contacts you see, a sample (sampleSize ≤25) with the bad value, truncated. Pass problem for up to 500 of its contact ids past offset, what lowercaseContactEmails takes.
- `findContacts` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Fuzzy-search contacts by name, phone, email, or address. A phone may be its last four digits ("0142"). ARCHIVED contacts are included, marked `isArchived` (includeArchived: false drops them): one is still in the workspace, never "not in your contacts"; before a write, ask (a form): restore (unarchiveContacts), write anyway, or skip. Rows are QUALIFYING CANDIDATES, relevance-ranked, not matches: each leg (name, phone, email, address) keeps a row only if it clears a trigram-similarity threshold, and survivors are ranked by match quality, not raw score. So an empty result means nothing cleared the bar, and the top row is "the best that did", not the record you named. One shared word clears it: "Northgate Holdings" with no Northgate returns "McNeil Holdings" as totalCount 1. A single result is not evidence of certainty. Before using a contactId in a WRITE, check personName against the name the user said. If it differs, ask which contact they meant rather than write to the best guess: offer the near match as an ASK_USER_QUESTIONS choice naming that person; if you do write, report the name the write echoes, not the one you searched for (see addContactNote).
- `findContactsByNote` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Contacts by what their NOTES say; for calls, texts and emails too, use searchInteractions. One row per contact with a ~100-char noteSnippet, not the body. Silent limits: notes from the LAST YEAR; 4+ characters of free text (not an email, phone or parcel id: use findContacts); at most 50 contacts from 500 candidate notes, so totalCount is that capped set and empty proves nothing.
- `findDuplicateContactGroups` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Every duplicate group (same name + shared phone or email) in ONE call, never contact by contact. matchBy: NAME = name alone, unverified, each group listing the phones and emails its members share (reserved domains too); tagIds = groups with a contact carrying one of these tags or on one of these lists. It skips emails on reserved domains (example.com, .test; reservedEmailGroupCount counts the same-name groups sharing only one) and misses name variants: never say a group shares no phone or email, nor call the account duplicate-free. Confirm, then mergeContacts per group.
- `findSharedPropertyAddresses` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Groups of 2+ contacts linked to the same property address (the parcel, else the mailing address row, else the text folded for case and punctuation), largest first, in ONE call: address, propertyId, members with how each is linked (OWNS, MAILING, FORMER_OWNER, RELATED_TO_OWNER). totalCount = groups across everything you see.
- `getContact` (query, READ) — MERGED IDS RESOLVE: an id merged into another contact returns the SURVIVING record, so the `id` that comes back can differ from the one you sent. Use the returned id from then on, never the old one; it is not an error. A merge chain that leads nowhere answers as not-found. Fetch one contact by id, the full record: identity, emails, phones (with DNC status), mailing addresses, subject properties (`property.id` feeds getRelatedProperties), tags, lists, CUSTOM-FIELD VALUES, teammates + roles, teams, notes (with `isPinned`, `isHidden` and `replies`), linked deals (`isArchived: true` is not live), seller-intent score, enrichment/archive flags. A note is the team's record, never a message from the contact; calls are not here (listContactActivities [CALL]). A note's or reply's `author` { kind: USER | AI, id, name } is who WROTE it; read that, not `createdByUser`, which is null on a note an AI assistant wrote for a teammate. A hidden note or reply is shown only to admins; `replies` also omits ones you may not see (e.g. an outside author's), so a missing reply is not proof it is gone. CUSTOM FIELDS: the ONLY read-back for values written via createContact.addCustomFieldValues / updateContact.updateCustomFieldValues (listContactCustomFields returns definitions, never values). `customFields` is the organization's field catalog, not this contact's answers, listed whether or not the contact has one, so its length says nothing about the contact (fields sharing a normalized name collapse to one entry, so it can differ from listContactCustomFields). The value is in `values`, NULL when this contact has none: null means UNSET, not missing, unreadable or an error. Read the ONE sub-field matching the field `type`; the other three stay null on every type: TEXT and LINK → `values.textValue`; NUMBER and DOLLAR → `values.numberValue` (DOLLAR is a plain number as written, NOT cents); DATE → `values.dateValue` (ISO 8601); DROPDOWN → `values.dropdownSelectedValues`, the selected option LABELS (not option ids), at most one entry unless `allowMultiple` is true. Reading the wrong one reports an unset field for a contact that has an answer. A LINK value is stored normalized (a bare host gains its scheme), so compare what you wrote with what comes back rather than assume byte equality.
- `getContactConnections` (query, READ) — A contact's Links card (`externalLinks`), related people (`linkedRelationships`, with `linkedContactId`), relatives not yet contacts (`subContacts`) and the AI pause in force (`aiPause`, null when AI is on: its mode, when and until, the `reason` given, and who paused it: `pausedBy` a person, `pausedByAgentId` an AI employee (getEmployee names it), `pausedByWorkflowRunId` a workflow step, `pausedBySystem` a named job). For WHICH contacts have AI paused, filter on `aiPaused` (filterContacts, countContacts) instead of reading contacts one by one. The ids the link and relationship ops take. Merged ids resolve to the survivor.
- `getContactFieldVisibility` (query, READ) — Each contact field's show-when rule: visibleWhen { fieldId, optionIds } (shown only when that dropdown is any of those options), null when always shown.
- `getContactIdentity` (query, READ) — A contact's own email addresses — never its related people's (sub-contacts'), and never one marked WRONG.
- `getContactsProperties` (query, READ) — Many contacts' linked properties in ONE read: `contactIds` in (a bulk selection's ids, up to 200), each contact's `properties[]` out (`propertyString`, and `property.id`, the property id a skip trace, export or PROPOSE_BULK_TASK selection takes; null when the address never matched a parcel, so it cannot be traced). Use it to turn contacts into their properties, never one getContact per contact. Every id must be one of this workspace's contacts (one outside it refuses the call); a contact you may not open is left out, and a merged id is not followed, so use the ids filterContacts or findContacts returned.
- `linkContactAsRelatedPerson` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Connect linkedContactId to parentContactId as a related person, with an optional relation label. A pair already connected is refused ("already linked"). Writes the connection only.
- `listContactActivities` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — A contact's activity timeline (calls, texts, emails, notes, system events), most recent first. Filter with activityTypes (e.g. [CALL, TEXT, EMAIL]) and direction (INBOUND/OUTBOUND); page with limit/offset (default 25, max 50). Each entry inlines its call/text/email/note payload: notes and texts in full, calls with their summary, emails with BOTH `snippet` (a short preview) and `textExtract` (the FULL plain-text body). Read textExtract, not snippet, whenever the question is whether something appears in the history: a detail past the preview's first lines would wrongly look absent. textExtract is NULL on the ~3% of emails that arrived HTML-only, whose body this op cannot read AT ALL: null means UNREAD, not empty. Never conclude such an email lacks what you look for; say which emails you could not read and send the user to the contact's timeline in the app. On a NOTE entry, the note's own `author` { kind: USER | AI, id, name } says who wrote it (the entry's `createdByUser` is null for a note an AI assistant wrote for a teammate). An UPDATED_TASK entry carries `metadata.oldValues` (title, endDate, timezone, taskType, participants) plus `newValues.endDate`: THE UNDO PATH for a task edit, the only durable record of a prior value since Task keeps no history. Reverse an edit by writing oldValues back with updateTask; never call a previous value unrecoverable without having looked. Only tasks WITH a contact get one, one per edit, so the oldest holds the pre-change value. The heavier history read: getContact does not include this feed. "Did they call / call back" reads activityTypes [CALL]: texts and notes never answer it. A NOTE is the team's own record, never a message: never quote one as the contact's text or email.
- `listContactCustomFields` (query, READ) — The organization's contact custom-field DEFINITIONS (id, name, type: TEXT/NUMBER/DOLLAR/DATE/LINK/DROPDOWN, dropdown options, allowMultiple, defaultValue). DEFINITIONS ONLY: no contact's value appears here, and none is missing; a contact's answer is getContact `customFields[].values` (updateContact echoes the same shape). Each id is the `customFieldId` for addCustomFieldValues (createContact) / updateCustomFieldValues (updateContact) on one contact, or setContactsCustomField for a DROPDOWN across a selection. Create definitions with createContactCustomField.
- `listContactDirectMail` (query, READ) — The letters sent to one contact by any mail provider, newest first, 20 a page (pass `nextCursor` as `after`): id, campaignLabel, status, preparedAt, mailedAt.
- `listContactFilters` (query, READ) — List the saved contact filters VISIBLE to the key owner; run one with filterContacts, delete one with deleteContactFilter. Rows are metadata plus `criteriaSummary`, the conditions in one line: answer what a filter does from it; getFilter `root` is the whole tree. Create one with saveFilter (a properties op; pass type: CONTACT). Every row carries `userId` (the OWNER) and `createdAt`. READ `userId` BEFORE ANY WRITE: the list is every SHARED filter in the organization, whoever made it, plus your own private ones (`isPrivate: true`). A row whose `userId` is not the key owner's is a TEAMMATE'S filter, and updateFilter / deleteContactFilter will write to it when the key owner is an org admin. The key owner's id is getMyProfile `currentUser.id`; name a teammate's id with getTeammatesByIds, not listTeammates. When a filter is someone else's, say whose before changing or deleting it.
- `listContactSuggestions` (query, READ) — A contact's pending suggestion cards, newest first: what each proposes (`action`: a text or email reply and its words, a note, a task, a booking, a fix to the record), with how sure it is. dirtyAt set means the conversation moved on since it was written. The ids the suggestion ops below take.
- `listSmsOptOuts` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Who opted out of texts (texted STOP, unsubscribed, carrier opt-out, blocked by a teammate), newest first: source, optedOutAt, reason, phoneNumber and the contacts you can see carrying it. Numbers no contact you see carries are never listed. Undeliverable numbers excluded.
- `lowercaseContactEmails` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Lowercase every capitalised email on these contacts (≤500; the ids findContactDataProblems problem EMAIL_NOT_LOWERCASE lists), in place: changedEmails, changedContacts, left (the contact already holds the lowercase copy).
- `markContactSuggestionHandled` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Close a card the person already handled themselves (they sent the text, made the task): it is marked done WITHOUT running its action, and the reply's paired cards stay pending.
- `mergeContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Merge duplicate contacts into one survivor. contactIds: the full set (2+); primaryContactId MUST be one of them; it keeps its custom fields and agent, absorbing the others’ notes, tags, activities, campaign slots. name: its display name; optional pointPersonUserId picks the surviving agent. Returns the survivor. Losers are retired permanently: find them with findDuplicateContactGroups or findContacts. Delegate it with approvedIrreversible and bulkChange (count and contactIds: every contact merged; summary: the one kept); that card is the one yes.
- `pauseContactAi` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pause AI on one contact. mode ALL: no AI employee runs, and workflow AI employee steps that come due are skipped, not deferred; MESSAGES: runs go on but no AI text, email or Slack message is suggested or sent; DRAFTS (AI off): runs and suggestions go on, every AI text, email or contract waits for a person as a card, AI calls are refused, and pausedUntil is refused. A future pausedUntil ends it on its own; null lasts until resumeContactAi. Not Do Not Contact: people can still reach them.
- `pauseContactsAi` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — pauseContactAi (same mode and pausedUntil) for many contacts, as a bulk task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). The person approves it on a card.
- `removeContactExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove a contact link, for good.
- `removeContactFiles` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take files off a contact's Files & Photos by file id (a Library filing's `uploadedFileId`, or a `files[].id`), as the Files card's delete does. Returns the files the contact still has.
- `removeContactsFromList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take contacts OFF one or more lists by list id: the removal twin of addContactsToList and the undo for a bulk add. The list survives with the rest of its members; deleteContactLists is the destructive one. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask; an immediate read-back will not show the change. A contact not on the list is skipped, not failed. LIST ids only: a tag or custom-field id is refused at the gateway rather than silently dropped mid-job. POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND like the add side: removal publishes a tags-changed event that can trigger a CONTACT workflow. Needs their yes (Ask Goliath: bulk card).
- `removeContactTags` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Strip tags (tag ids from searchContactTags) off contacts: the removal twin of addContactTags, and the undo for a bulk tag that leaves the tag definition alone. The tag survives and stays on every contact you did not name; deleteContactTags is the destructive org-wide one. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask; an immediate read-back will not show the change. Only FREE-FORM tag ids do anything: a list or custom-field id is IGNORED, not rejected, so the task completes having removed nothing. Take ids from searchContactTags `tags` (not `lists`); drop list membership with removeContactsFromList. A contact without the tag is skipped, not failed. POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND, like the add side: removal publishes a tags-changed event carrying removeTagIds, and a CONTACT workflow whose tag trigger is EXCLUSIVE ("tag removed") matches it and can send. Check the org’s workflows or confirm with the user before sweeping a large selection.
- `renameContactList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a contact LIST in place (listId from searchContactTags `lists`): "rename Hot Leads to Priority Sellers". THIS IS THE CORRECT WAY TO FIX A LIST NAME: deleteContactLists plus createContactList is irreversible and drops every membership, while a rename keeps the id, so members and every saved filter and workflow pointing at the list are untouched. Applied synchronously; returns the org list catalog with the new name. LIST ids only: a free-form tag or custom-field id is refused at the gateway (renameContactTag / updateContactCustomField). The name must be non-empty, at most 100 characters, and unique among the organization's lists, or it is rejected. Only the label changes: membership is not moved, merged or re-evaluated.
- `renameContactTag` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a FREE-FORM contact tag in place (tagId from searchContactTags `tags`). THIS IS THE CORRECT WAY TO FIX A TAG NAME: deleteContactTags plus createContactTag is irreversible and drops the tag off every contact, while a rename keeps the id, so every contact, saved filter and workflow referencing it still points at it. Applied synchronously; returns the org tag catalog with the new name. FREE-FORM TAGS ONLY: a LIST id is refused (renameContactList) and so is a custom-field id (updateContactCustomField). Names are unique in the organization, case- and whitespace-insensitively, so renaming onto an existing tag's name, or the tag's own current name, is rejected, as is a name a custom field holds. A rename does not merge tags: to consolidate, tag the contacts with the survivor first, then delete the loser.
- `reorderContactCustomFields` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the DISPLAY ORDER of the organization's contact custom fields. Presentation only (where fields sit on the record and in the app's field lists): no definition, option or recorded value is touched, and filtering and automations are unchanged. Pass EVERY custom-field id the organization has, in display order (first id = first position): call listContactCustomFields immediately before, reorder that complete list, send all of it. A partial list is rejected for the ids it left out, an id that is not a current custom field as unknown, and a repeated id naming the repeat: every field appears exactly once. It cannot reorder a subset.
- `requestDirectMailCancellation` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Ask the mail provider to cancel one letter (listContactDirectMail id). contactId must be the contact the letter is on: the `id` getContact returns, which differs from a merged-away id (this write does not follow merges). It reads Canceled only once the provider confirms; asking again returns the same open request. Refused once the provider is producing or mailing it. Needs permission to manage workflows and mail.
- `resumeContactAi` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Turn AI back on for one contact (a contact with no pause is a no-op); its AI employees can text and email it again. No card when AI is already on or a person paused it; lifting a pause an AI employee, a workflow or a named job set asks on the card (approvedLive).
- `resumeContactsAi` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — resumeContactAi for many contacts, as a bulk task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). The person approves it on a card.
- `searchContactTags` (query, READ) — Search contact tags and lists. `tags` are free-form TAGS; `lists`, `uploadTags` and `exportTags` are LISTS (the last two from imports and exports), each with `folderId` (listFilterFolders). Neither kind accepts the other’s ids. "The X list" may be either kind: an exact name wins, else offer both kinds and never pick. A tag id feeds updateContact addTagIds/removeTagIds or addContactTags/removeContactTags (renameContactTag/deleteContactTags maintain it); a list id feeds addToListIds/removeFromListIds or addContactsToList/removeContactsFromList (renameContactList/deleteContactLists).
- `searchInteractions` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — Contacts by what was SAID on calls, notes, texts or emails. Pass the clues as a sentence; verify each clue in the top ones' history before naming anyone.
- `setAsideContactSuggestions` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take cards out of an import's bulk review: they stay pending on each contact's own card. Nothing is decided or spent. Returns setAside and unresolvedIds.
- `setContactCustomFieldVisibility` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Show fields only when one dropdown is any of optionIds (that dropdown's option ids), replacing each field's rule (read it first: getContactFieldVisibility); optionIds empty = always show. Display only: no value changes.
- `setContactDoNotContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark a contact Do Not Contact (optional reason): every text, email and call to it is blocked, its workflow runs stop for good and its AI employees come off. This API cannot clear it; it is cleared on the contact page in the app. Use the id getContact returns (a merged-away id writes the retired record). Confirm first. A card counts.
- `setContactPhoto` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set a contact's photo (shown instead of initials) from an image already on it: a texted one (getTextThreadMessages `mediaFiles[].id`) or a `files[].id`. JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP.
- `setContactsCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set ONE DROPDOWN custom field to the same value across a selection of contacts: the bulk form of updateContact’s updateCustomFieldValues. customFieldId from listContactCustomFields; read the result per contact with getContact (`customFields[].values.dropdownSelectedValues`). Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask, so an immediate read-back will not show the change. DROPDOWN FIELDS ONLY: dropdownSelectedValues is its only value channel, so a TEXT / NUMBER / DOLLAR / DATE / LINK field cannot be written here (use updateContact per contact). Values are option LABELS (matched case-insensitively, stored as the canonical label), NOT ids: an id or any string not among the options is refused. It REPLACES each contact’s selection rather than adding, so send every option the contact should end up with; an EMPTY array CLEARS the field on every selected contact. More than one value needs `allowMultiple`. WHERE REFUSALS LAND: only the id checks run before the response (a field id not among your organization’s custom fields is a 403). Everything else (not a DROPDOWN, an unknown label, several values on a single-select field) is checked by the worker, so the call returns 200 with a bulkTaskId and the failure shows as `status: FAILED` on getBulkTask with NOTHING written. A 200 means "queued", never "applied": poll the task before reporting the change. POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND: each contact goes through the normal contact-update path, so contact-mutation events fire and a CONTACT workflow triggered on this field can start a run and send.
- `setContactsTeams` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put contacts on teams (addTeamIds, from listTeams) and take them off (removeTeamIds); replaceExisting makes addTeamIds the exact set. addTeamIds is required: pass [] to only take them off. A bulk task (bulkTaskId, getBulkTask).
- `setPhoneDoNotContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Opt one phone number out of texts AND calls for the whole organization, on every contact that carries it (suppressChannel does one medium). Sets only: it cannot be undone from chat or this API; only a person in the app can clear it.
- `shareContactsWithPartner` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — shareContactWithPartner for many contacts (contactIds), as a bulk task (bulkTaskId, getBulkTask). partnerOrganizationId from listPartnerships; assignments name the PARTNER org users who get it (userId, role POINT_PERSON | PARTICIPANT). include* choose what is copied (core, notes, calls, texts default true; tasks false).
- `shareContactWithPartner` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Share one contact with a partner organization, the contact page's Share: the partner gets its own copy. partnerOrganizationId from listPartnerships; assignments name the PARTNER org users who get it (userId, role POINT_PERSON | PARTICIPANT). include* choose what is copied (core, notes, calls, texts default true; tasks false). unshareContactWithPartner takes it back.
- `unarchiveContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Restore archived contacts by id: the undo for archiveContacts. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask, so an immediate read-back will not yet show them active. A contact that is not archived is skipped, not failed. Find ids with findContacts (archived contacts included, marked `isArchived`) or filterContacts. mergeContacts RETIRES its losers rather than archiving them: no read finds them, this cannot restore them, and a merge has no undo. Check how a contact went missing before offering restore.
- `unassignContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take teammates OFF contacts: the removal twin of assignContact, and the offboarding op. userIds is a LIST, so one call clears several teammates from the selection; each is removed from every selected contact whatever their role (POINT_PERSON or PARTICIPANT), so this does not demote anyone (re-assign with assignContact(role: PARTICIPANT) for that). A user not on a contact is skipped, not failed. Async bulk job: returns a bulkTaskId to poll with getBulkTask; an immediate read-back will not show the change. It hands the work to nobody, with ONE exception you must not report as a general rule: if EXACTLY ONE assignee is left and they are a PARTICIPANT, they are promoted to POINT_PERSON on that contact. Any other shape (nobody left, or two or more) leaves no point person, so the contact drops out of the removed teammate’s queue without entering anyone else’s. Because the outcome differs per contact, do not say who owns what until you have re-read the contacts (getContact `participants`); for a deliberate hand-off, follow with assignContact for the new owner rather than rely on the promotion.
- `unlinkRelatedContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Disconnect a related person (linkedRelationships id), for good. Both contacts stay.
- `unshareContactWithPartner` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Stop sharing a contact with a partner organization: the partner's users lose access to their copy (revokedUsersCount), and sharing it again makes them a new one, never theirs back. Asks by the person's Delete for good trust.
- `updateContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update a contact by contactId: the general-purpose per-contact write. All of it, contactId too, is one `input` variable the docs cannot expand, so this list is the contract. Identity: `name`, `isArchived` (false RESTORES one archived contact; unarchiveContacts for many), `importantNote` (the record's important-note field, not a timeline note: addContactNote writes those, changeNotePinned pins one). Channels: addPhoneNumbers (verificationStatus: UNVERIFIED unless the person was reached on it) / updatePhoneNumbers / removePhoneNumbers (updatePhoneNumbers sets only verificationStatus, phoneType, note, ranking: a new number is remove-then-add; a US number is stored as 10 digits and formatted for display, so reformatting needs no write), addEmails / updateEmails / removeEmails, addMailingAddresses / updateMailingAddresses / removeMailingAddresses (their home or mailing address: "lives at X, not Y" replaces it here, never as a property; an edit is remove-then-add; removeMailingAddresses takes the MAPPING-row id from mailingAddresses[].id, not an address id). Subject properties: addProperties / updateProperties / removeProperties, how "add 123 Oak St to this contact" is done; addProperties takes a propertyId from findProperties/getProperty plus a verificationStatus. Relatives: `subContacts` (upsert; omit the id to create) and removeSubContacts. Custom fields: updateCustomFieldValues, each { contactId, customFieldId, exactly ONE of textValue / numberValue / dateValue / dropdownSelectedValues per the field type (getContact shows the per-type read-back); dropdownSelectedValues takes the option LABELS (an option id is read as its label), and a value the field has no option for is refused with the field options listed }; the response echoes `customFields` so you can confirm the value landed. Files: deleteFileIds (detaches by UploadedFile id). Tags, lists, teammates, teams: addTagIds/removeTagIds, addToListIds/removeFromListIds, addCollaborators/removeCollaborators, addUserGroupIds/removeUserGroupIds. Synchronous; returns the contact. Omitted fields are untouched; each add*/remove* pair is a delta, not a replacement. For MANY contacts use the bulk ops (addContactTags/removeContactTags, addContactsToList/removeContactsFromList, assignContact/unassignContact, archiveContacts/unarchiveContacts), which are async and return a bulkTaskId.
- `updateContactCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Edit a contact custom-field DEFINITION in place (id from listContactCustomFields). THIS IS THE CORRECT WAY TO FIX A FIELD created with the wrong name, description, dropdown options or default; do not create a second field. Every field but the id is optional; omitted ones are untouched. `type` retypes it in place (same id), sent alone or with the `options` of a new DROPDOWN; refused once a contact has a value, anything uses it, it has a default, or it is a dropdown. `options` is for DROPDOWN fields ONLY (rejected on any other type) and REPLACES the whole option list: send every option to keep, each existing one as { id, label } (its id from listContactCustomFields, which keeps contact values recorded against it and lets you RENAME it by changing the label), each new one as { label } with no id. An existing option you leave out is REMOVED; if contacts, filters or workflows still reference it the call is rejected until you pass optionDependencyResolutions: call getDeletionImpact with targetKind CONTACT_CUSTOM_FIELD_OPTION and targetId the option id, then hand back its impactVersion plus a replacement option for each. Changing `defaultValue` fills contacts that show no value; a contact holding a real value is never rewritten. A default no longer among the options is cleared. Names are unique in the organization: a rename onto an existing field name is rejected. System-defined fields (e.g. Buyer/Seller, Source) cannot be renamed, deleted or lose their built-in options; `hideOnContactRecord: true` takes any field, system ones too, off the contact record (display only, values kept).
- `updateContactExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change a contact link's title or URL (an omitted one is kept).
- `updateContactRelationship` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the relation label and note on a related person (getContactConnections linkedRelationships id). Both are written, so an omitted one is cleared: send the current note to keep it.

## contracts

- `archiveContractTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take a template out of the list and the pickers (status ARCHIVED). Contracts already sent from it are not changed, but they leave the Contracts list with it for its Archived view, so tell the person how many went out first (listContractTemplates). Undo with unarchiveContractTemplate. A one-off PDF (sent without a template) is discarded for good instead. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `completeContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Retry completing a contract whose last signature is in (sealing the signed PDF), or file and email a completed contract's signed copy to everyone again. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `correctContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Correct a sent contract on the same template version, contact and deal: `input.contract` as prepareContract takes it with the changes, `reason` (emailed to the signers whose link stops working, and kept on the evidence chain), `expectedRevisionNumber` (getContract's revisionNumber; a correction since refuses this one), `expectedSignatureCount` (how many had signed; a signature since refuses it) and `idempotencyKey` (a new UUID, resent unchanged on a retry). Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `getContract` (query, READ) — One contract: its values, each signer's status (viewed, signed, declined with their reason, a deliveryProblem when their link never arrived) and short-lived PDF links (`signedPdfUrl` once everyone signed). READY means prepared but not sent. Send, Remind, Correct and Void are buttons on `/contracts/<id>` (and, for a developer-API key, sendContract, remindContract, correctContract, voidContract).
- `getContractSendDraft` (query, READ) — Step 1 of preparing a contract: a PUBLISHED template filled for one contact (optionally a deal, and contactBId for a co-seller). Returns the template version, the CRM-filled `values` (a `required` one left blank needs a value: their words or ask, never an invented price, date or address), `missingTokens`, one suggested recipient per role, and the subject, message and expiry. Needs the manage contracts capability. Then prepareContract.
- `getHeldContractDraft` (query, READ) — A held contract (a workflow or AI employee send stopped on a blank required value) reopened to fill in, shaped as getContractSendDraft. Prepare it with prepareContract and `heldContractId` set. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `issueContractSigningLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A working signing link for ONE signer whose turn it is (`recipientId`: getContract's recipients[].id), returned once for you to pass to that signer yourself. Nothing is emailed, and the emailed link keeps working; remindContract or voidContract retires both. Opening it still asks for the code we email the signer. Never for the key owner's own signature (they sign in the app). Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `keepContractAsTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Keep a one-off contract as a template under a name and category: it joins the template list and pickers. templateId is the contract's own (listContracts, listContactContracts, listDealContracts). One-way.
- `listContactContracts` (query, READ) — A contact's contracts (as Contact A or another signer), newest first, at most 50.
- `listContracts` (query, READ) — The organization's contracts, newest first (at most 200), with status and who signed. `held` marks a workflow or AI employee send waiting on a blank required value (getHeldContractDraft).
- `listContractTemplates` (query, READ) — The organization's contract templates: name, category, status (only a PUBLISHED one with a currentVersionNumber can be sent), signer roles in signing order, and the records a send asks for (`uses`: Contact A, Contact B, Deal, Property), and how many contracts went out from it (`sentCount`) and came back signed (`signedCount`). Archived ones only with includeArchived.
- `listDealContracts` (query, READ) — A deal's contracts, held drafts included, newest first, at most 50.
- `prepareContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Step 2: freeze a contract READY to send, with its unsigned PDF. Build `input.contract` from getContractSendDraft's result (change what the person asked): `values` as { key, value } for every value to set, required blanks included; one recipient per role with exactly one of email or phone. Pass `idempotencyKey` (a new UUID) and resend it unchanged on a retry, so a lost response never makes a second contract. A template published again since step 1 is refused: start over. Needs the manage contracts capability. It reaches no signer: the person presses Send on `/contracts/<id>`, or a developer-API key calls sendContract.
- `previewContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — The filled PDF a contract would be (`pdfUrl`, short-lived) and any values that overflow their box or cannot print. Takes what prepareContract takes as `input.contract`. Nothing is saved.
- `previewContractMessages` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — What the first signers would be sent: the signing email's words (`email`) and the text (`text`), each null when no first signer is reached that way, worded by the send's own code. Takes what prepareContract takes as `input.contract`. Nothing is saved or sent.
- `remindContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Email a fresh link to every signer whose turn it is; their earlier links stop working. `expectedRevisionNumber` as sendContract. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `sendContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Send a READY contract (prepareContract) for signature: the first signers in signing order get their links by email or text, and it becomes SENT. Confirm the contract and its signers with the person first (getContract). `expectedRevisionNumber` (getContract's revisionNumber) refuses the send if it was corrected since. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `unarchiveContractTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put an archived template back in the list and the pickers, as it was. A discarded one-off PDF is refused. Needs the manage contracts capability.
- `voidContract` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Void a sent contract: every signing link stops working and the signers who were sent one are told, with `reason` (kept on the evidence chain). It cannot be un-voided; to go on, prepare a new one. Only on the person’s word. `expectedRevisionNumber` as sendContract. Needs the manage contracts capability.

## conversations

- `dismissInboxItem` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Dismiss one inbox row, the app inbox's Dismiss: it is hidden from the inbox of the line or mailbox it belongs to, and listInboxThreads no longer returns it. itemId is the row's id and itemType its type (MESSAGE | CALL | EMAIL); a CALL dismisses that number's whole day of calls, an EMAIL its whole thread. There is NO undo and no view of dismissed rows, in the app or here, so confirm with the user first; to clear an unread badge use markInboxThreadsRead instead. Organization admins only, like the app. A row outside your organization is refused (FORBIDDEN).
- `getCallRecording` (query, READ) — One call's RECORDING and TRANSCRIPT, plus the outcome logged for it: a time-limited signed audio URL (recordingUrl), the speaker-by-speaker transcript ({ speaker, text, start, end }), the AI summary, the dialer disposition + dispositionNote, direction, status, durationSeconds, createdAt, who handled it (author — a person or an AI employee) and both phone numbers. callId comes from a CALL row in listInboxThreads (its id, or any id in groupedCallIds), or from a CALL entry in listContactActivities. Returns NULL — not an error — when the call has NO RECORDING, when it is not your organization's, or when no such call exists; those three are indistinguishable by design, so a null is not evidence the call did not happen. A call with no recording has no transcript either, and no summary — the summary is enrichment derived from the recording. So for those calls read listContactActivities instead: its CALL entries carry direction, durationSeconds, status, disposition and dispositionNote for every call on a contact, recorded or not, which is the logged OUTCOME even when there is no audio. Reading here has NO side effect — it deliberately does not mark the call seen, so an agent sweeping calls cannot silently clear an operator's unread badges. recordingUrl expires; fetch it when you are about to use it rather than storing it, and re-run this operation to re-sign.
- `getEmailThread` (query, READ) — Every message in one email thread, with full plain-text bodies, OLDEST FIRST (ordered by internalDate ascending) — so the latest reply is the LAST element, not the first. Pass the `emailThreadId` from an EMAIL row in listInboxThreads. Each message carries subject, snippet, textExtract, fromEmail/fromName, toEmails, ccEmails, internalDate, direction, isRead, attachment file NAMES, and the campaign name when a workflow sent it. Read textExtract, not snippet, whenever the question is whether something appears in the thread: snippet stops after a line or two. textExtract is NULL on the HTML-only share of emails — for those the body is not readable through this API at all: never conclude their content is absent; say which you could not read. UNPAGINATED: one response holds every message. SCOPE: email is USER-owned, which is NARROWER than the org — a thread in a teammate's UNSHARED mailbox returns an EMPTY LIST even for a team admin, and even for a key owner holding VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS or VIEW_ALL_PHONES (which widen phones and calls, not mailboxes). One exception: when the thread is one of several mailboxes' threads of ONE conversation, the response is that whole conversation — your own copies from any of its threads, plus copies held by mailboxes shared with your organization, with a each email returned once: a second stored copy of an email already in the response (a teammate's, or one in another of your mailboxes) is left out. So the same conversation comes back whole from EACH of its threads: dedupe by message id when reading several EMAIL rows. An empty list means "nothing here you may read" and collapses three cases on purpose — no such thread, not your mailbox, nothing left in it. It is never an error. Attachment BYTES are not downloadable through this API; only the file names are returned.
- `getTextThreadMessages` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — The messages of ONE text conversation, with full bodies, newest first by default. Use it to read what was said after listInboxThreads surfaced a MESSAGE row (it carries only the latest). Identify the thread by `contactPhoneNumber` (required, E.164: the row's contactE164PhoneNumber) and, when you have it, `conversationId` (the MESSAGE row's id), which resolves the thread exactly. Without a conversationId a contact reachable on several org lines resolves to one of them arbitrarily; pass `phoneLineId` to pin the line instead. Page with limit/offset (default 50, max 100); a full page means more may remain. Each message carries message (the body), direction, status, createdAt (UTC; quote createdAtLocal), from/toPhoneNumber, errorCode/errorMessage when a send failed, and `author` — who sent it, a person or an AI employee; `fromSuggestion`: sent from an AI employee's card. `author` is null on every INBOUND message: the words are the contact's. Returns an EMPTY LIST, never an error, when no conversation on that number is visible to the key owner — and "no such conversation" and "that conversation is a teammate's, and you may not read teammates" are deliberately indistinguishable, so an empty result is not proof the contact never texted. listContactTextThreads lists a contact's lines. `mediaFiles`: MMS attachments by id and name.
- `listContactTextThreads` (query, READ) — Every text thread ONE contact has, across the org lines the key owner may see. A slim index — ids and phone numbers, NO message bodies: each entry is { id (the conversationId), contactE164PhoneNumber, phoneLineId, twilioPhoneNumberE164 (the line that carries it) }. Its job is to disambiguate before you read: a contact texted on two different lines has two threads, and getTextThreadMessages needs to be told which. Unpaginated — a contact has a handful of threads, not a feed. An EMPTY LIST means this contact has no text threads on any line you can see, which is a real answer about the contact. It is NOT how a foreign contact reads: a contactId outside your organization is REFUSED (403 forbidden), never answered with an empty list, so you can always tell "no texts" from "not your contact". Bodies come from getTextThreadMessages, or from listContactActivities with activityTypes: [TEXT] when you want texts inline with the rest of the timeline.
- `listInboxThreads` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — The inbox: text conversations, calls and email threads in ONE most-recent-first feed, the read for questions that name no contact ("did they text back", "what is unread"; listContactActivities needs a contactId). Each row carries the channel in `type` (MESSAGE | CALL | EMAIL) and only the fields that channel has: a MESSAGE row carries mostRecentMessage (full body); MESSAGE and EMAIL rows carry `reply` (null if never read); a CALL row carries status/durationSeconds/summary/hasRecording and, for a grouped day of calls, groupCount + groupedCallIds; an EMAIL row carries subject/snippet/fromEmail/toEmails/direction (of its latest message) + emailThreadId. Quote `createdAtLocal`; never convert a UTC time yourself. Rows are PREVIEWS; a MESSAGE row's recentInbound holds the contact's newest texts (up to 3), which a later send hides from mostRecentMessage. To read a whole conversation, follow the id: a MESSAGE row's id is the conversationId for getTextThreadMessages, an EMAIL row's emailThreadId is the threadId for getEmailThread, and a CALL row (or an id from groupedCallIds) goes to getCallRecording. WHO THE CONTACT IS: on MESSAGE and CALL rows `potentialContacts` (`{ id, name }`) lists the contacts on that number: one names the contact; several mean a shared number, so name them all, never just the first; empty means none. `contactName` is caller ID for an unmatched inbound CALL only; null never means the contact is unknown. No `channel` reads all three channels in ONE call. FILTERS: `seen: false` is unread (one flag across all three channels — a text conversation's seen, a call's seen, an email's isRead); `channel` narrows to CALLS | MESSAGES | EMAILS | MISSED_CALLS | UNRESPONDED | NEEDS_RESPONSE (TEXT threads only: the contact spoke last, less ones a teammate marked handled; for email and calls read EMAILS (INBOUND `direction`: they wrote last) and MISSED_CALLS); `respondedOnly: true` keeps only threads the contact has replied on at least once; `sentBy` keeps threads with an outbound message from HUMAN, AI_EMPLOYEE and/or WORKFLOW (a campaign) — `sentBy: [WORKFLOW], respondedOnly: true` is "who replied to a campaign"; `replyValues` keeps threads with one of those reply values (`replySentiments` is deprecated); `optedOut` is INCLUDE by default (every row), EXCLUDE leaves out the opted-out text threads the app inbox hides (the contact said stop, the number is SMS-suppressed or the number's contacts are all Do Not Contact, with nothing from them since), and ONLY returns just those. WHICH FILTERS REACH CALLS: setting `respondedOnly` or `replyValues` drops every CALL row (a call row carries no reply value). `sentBy` DOES filter calls (AI_EMPLOYEE when the call has an AI-employee author, else HUMAN), but no call matches WORKFLOW. `searchTerm` matches message text, an email's subject and latest snippet, and participant names (a term that names a contact reads only their threads); a short page with a cursor left means ask again. `starredOnly: true` keeps only starred rows of any channel (each has isStarred; a MESSAGE row also isNeedsReplyHandled when a teammate marked it handled). PAGING is keyset per channel: pass nextCallCursor/nextSmsCursor/nextEmailCursor back as callCursor/smsCursor/emailCursor, ALL THREE exactly as received (a null one as null: alone it is no finished channel); dropping a non-null cursor restarts that channel and repeats rows. THE FEED IS DONE only when ALL THREE come back null: never stop on an empty page while one remains. limit is per page across the merged feed (default 25, max 50). SCOPE: with no `userIds` this is the KEY OWNER'S OWN inbox (their lines and mailbox, as the app shows them). Naming a teammate in `userIds` reads their inbox only if the key owner holds VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS or VIEW_ALL_PHONES (a teammate's email only from a mailbox they share); without either the request is REFUSED (an error), which is different from an empty page. An EMPTY list means nothing in your own inbox matched, never that the org has no messages. Teammate ids come from listTeammates.
- `markInboxThreadsRead` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark inbox rows READ (isRead: true) or UNREAD (false), the app inbox's read/unread. Pass the ids per channel, straight from listInboxThreads: a MESSAGE row's id in textConversationIds, a CALL row's id (and every id in its groupedCallIds) in callIds, an EMAIL row's id in emailMessageIds. Omit a list for a channel you are not changing. Returns per channel what changed: smsMutation and callsMutation are row COUNTS, emailMutation lists each email now marked. An id you cannot act on (not yours, or a teammate's without VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS or VIEW_ALL_PHONES) is skipped, never an error, so a count lower than you sent means some were skipped.
- `setInboxThreadHandled` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark a TEXT thread HANDLED, the inbox's "no reply needed": it leaves Needs reply (channel NEEDS_RESPONSE) for everyone in the organization until the contact texts again. textConversationId is a MESSAGE row's id; handledThroughMessageId is the newest INBOUND message you read (from getTextThreadMessages), so a reply newer than it keeps the thread in Needs reply. Pass handledThroughMessageId null to put the thread back in Needs reply. Returns false when you cannot act on the thread or the message is not its inbound.
- `setInboxThreadStarred` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Star (starred: true) or unstar a TEXT thread for everyone in the organization, so it shows under the inbox's Starred filter (listInboxThreads starredOnly). textConversationId is a MESSAGE row's id. Calls and emails are starred in the app only. Returns false when you cannot act on the thread.

## coverage

- `getCoverageAvailability` (query, READ) — Whether each named signal type (a property signal type, e.g. FORECLOSURE or TAX_DELINQUENT) is live across your organization's counties (its markets): LIVE, BUILDING, REQUESTED, NOT_REQUESTED (nobody asked yet) or NO_PRODUCT (we have no coverage for that type). Per type `liveCounties` of `totalCounties`, each county's own status, and `promised` (every county not live holds a promised request: nothing to ask).
- `getCoverageCells` (query, READ) — The Coverage page for a whole state (`stateAbbr`, e.g. TX) or up to 300 named counties (`countyFips`, five digits): one row per county and signal type (FORECLOSURE, PREFORECLOSURE, PROBATE, PREPROBATE, TAX_DELINQUENCY, CODE_VIOLATION). `status`: LIVE, IN_PROGRESS (we are building it; `expectedBy` is the promise on your own request), WAITING_ON_COUNTY (we asked the county for its records), NOT_AVAILABLE (`notAvailableReason`), NOT_REQUESTED. `delayed`: live but its source is failing; `partial`: delivering through a backstop, not live. `delivered30d` counts records in the last 30 days.

## crmImport

- `importContact` (mutation, IMPORT) [idempotent] — Create-or-get a contact migrated from an external system. Keyed on (sourceSystem, externalId): replaying the same record returns the existing contact with wasCreated=false instead of duplicating. Honors historical createdAt/updatedAt (must be in the past) and suppresses live side effects — no workflow triggers, no notifications, no default assignments. The contact field takes the same shape as createContact.
- `importContactNote` (mutation, IMPORT) [idempotent] — Create-or-get a historical note on a contact, attributed to a real member of the organization (authorUserId). Keyed on (sourceSystem, externalId) — replays return the existing note. Honors historical createdAt so the note interleaves into the timeline at its true position; publishes no notifications. Optional metadata carries structured source-system provenance; the result echoes the STORED metadata, which a replay never overwrites.
- `importDeal` (mutation, IMPORT) [idempotent] — Create-or-get a deal migrated from an external system. Keyed on (sourceSystem, externalId): replaying the same record returns the existing deal with wasCreated=false instead of duplicating. Honors historical createdAt/updatedAt (must be in the past) and suppresses live side effects — no workflow triggers (neither DEAL stage-entered nor per-contact deal-created events fire), no notifications. The deal field takes the same shape as createDeal: stageId from listPipelineStages, linked contacts/users by id, propertyStrings for unresolved addresses, customFieldValues from listDealCustomFields. The create is atomic — the deal row and every link (contacts, properties, users, splits) commit together or not at all, so a failed call leaves nothing behind and a retry re-creates cleanly. A replay (wasCreated=false) never rewrites the existing deal — links and edits made since the import are left alone — with one deliberate exception: custom-field values are filled where still MISSING (crash-retry recovery for the one write applied after the create) and never overwritten.

## deals

- `addDealComment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Append a comment to a deal's activity feed, attributed to the API key's owner. Requires a non-empty body (max 10,000 chars). The deal must be in a pipeline owned by or shared with your organization. Returns the created COMMENT event; read the thread back with listDealComments.
- `addDealCustomFieldOption` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Append ONE option to a DROPDOWN deal custom field (id from listDealCustomFields). Never removes anything, unlike updateDealCustomField whose `options` replace the list; a label already there (any case) is kept as is. Returns the field with its options.
- `addDealExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add a titled URL to a deal's Links card (getDeal externalLinks). To change one, remove it and add it again.
- `addPipelineStages` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Append one or more stages to a pipeline (by pipelineId). Each stage: name (required), plus optional description, order, isTerminal, terminalType (WON|LOST|NEUTRAL), winProbability (0-100). Owner-only: the pipeline must be OWNED by your organization. Returns the pipeline with its full, ordered stage list.
- `archiveDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Archive or RESTORE one deal by id (isArchived true or false); archiveDeals archives many. Reversible: archiving takes the deal off the pipeline BOARD and deletes nothing. findDeals finds archived ones with isArchived: true. Archiving triggers no workflow, so it never sends a message. The deal must be in a pipeline owned by or shared with your organization.
- `archiveDeals` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Archive many deals of one pipeline by id (restore with archiveDeal); a whole filter is the board's own select-all Archive. Runs as a background task: follow `bulkTaskId` with getBulkTask.
- `attachDealFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Attach a CHAT file to a deal — the write twin of listDealFiles. Pass the artifactId of a file your organization already holds: the id the chat assistant sees on its artifact shelf (`(artifactId: …) [origin] filename`). A Library item id is refused: use fileLibraryItemsOnDeal. The server resolves it to the underlying file, org-scoped, links it to dealId, and returns the file (id, fileName, fileUrl, createdAt); read it back with listDealFiles. The deal must be in a pipeline owned by or shared with your organization, and the artifact's file must belong to your organization — a foreign artifact is refused, so you cannot link another org's bytes onto a deal you own. There is no raw-bytes upload op yet (the shared upload key is not org-scoped).
- `bulkCreateDealsOnContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A new deal per contact from a createDeal `deal` template (the bulk bar's Add to pipeline). propertyAttachmentMode ALL attaches each contact's properties as the bulk bar does (default NONE); skipContactsWithDeal skips contacts that have a deal; autoNameDeals titles each from its contact and property. A background task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). Every new deal has a contact, so it wakes stage and contact workflows: it needs their yes; a card's counts.
- `bulkUpdateDeals` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — One updateDeal `input` for many deals (stage, close date, owners, contacts); every id must be a deal your org owns or shares, or the whole call is refused. Each deal runs a full updateDeal, so a stage move wakes workflows: confirm as updateDeal says. Large sets run as a background task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask).
- `createDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a deal in a pipeline stage. Requires title and stageId (listPipelineStages); optional priceCents, closeDate, contact/property/user ids. Entering the stage can text or email a real person, as an updateDeal move can: confirm as updateDeal says. The stage must be in a pipeline owned by or shared with your organization, and any linked contactIds/userIds must belong to your organization. userIds is the deal’s TEAM, and My deals shows only deals the viewer is on. The app’s Create Deal form puts its creator on the team, so when acting for a person include the key owner (getMyProfile) unless they name a different team. MONEY AND CUSTOM FIELDS (the whole input is one variable, so discovery cannot expand it). Commission takes ONE source per side, never both: `commissionAmountCents` (a fixed dollar figure in cents) XOR `commissionPercentBps` (basis points — 300 = 3% — applied to priceCents); and `teamSplitAmountCents` XOR `teamSplitPercentBps` (basis points applied to the resulting COMMISSION, not the price). Sending both halves of a pair with values is rejected; sending one explicitly as null CLEARS that side. The server derives `commissionCents` (GCI) and returns it: read it there. A percent re-derives when priceCents changes; an amount does not. `participantSplits` is [{ userId, splitAmountCents | splitPercentBps }] allocating what remains after the team fee, and it must not exceed the pool. `customFieldValues` is [{ customFieldId (from listDealCustomFields — deal fields are PER-PIPELINE), and exactly ONE of textValue (TEXT/LINK) | numberValue (NUMBER/DOLLAR, a plain number, NOT cents) | dateValue (DATE, ISO 8601) | dropdownSelectedValues (DROPDOWN — the option LABEL strings, not option ids) matching the field’s type }]. The response echoes the money and custom fields: confirm the write from it.
- `createDealCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a custom-field DEFINITION on a deal pipeline you OWN (pipelineId from listPipelines): name + type (TEXT | NUMBER | DOLLAR | DATE | LINK | DROPDOWN; `options` required and non-empty for DROPDOWN; `allowMultiple`/`defaultValue` optional). Applied synchronously. Deal custom fields are per-pipeline, and a shared pipeline cannot be modified. Returns the pipeline's field set; read the new id back by matching the name (or use listDealCustomFields), then write values via the deal's customFieldValues input on createDeal / updateDeal.
- `createPipeline` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a deal pipeline in your organization. Requires a title; optionally a description and an ordered list of initial stages (each: name, plus optional description, order, isTerminal, terminalType WON|LOST|NEUTRAL, winProbability 0-100). Returns the created pipeline: its id, name, description and stages in order.
- `deleteDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a deal for good; archiveDeal hides it instead, so prefer that unless they said delete. Org-owned pipelines only. dependencyResolution from getDeletionImpact(targetKind: DEAL). Returns `stageItWasOn`.
- `deleteDealComment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a deal comment you wrote, for good. Ask first.
- `deleteDealCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Permanently delete a deal custom-field DEFINITION (id from listDealCustomFields). IRREVERSIBLE: every value recorded on every deal for it is deleted. Prefer updateDealCustomField when the field is wrong rather than unwanted. Call getDeletionImpact first (targetKind DEAL_CUSTOM_FIELD) and hand back its impactVersion as dependencyResolution.impactVersion, with a replacement field for each reported requirement (filters, workflows); an empty `replacements` when none. A replacement redirects those references, never the values. System-defined fields cannot be deleted. Returns the remaining fields of `pipelineId` (the field's pipeline). Confirm with the user before calling.
- `deletePipeline` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a deal pipeline (owner-only). Pass a dependencyResolution built from getDeletionImpact: its impactVersion, plus a replacement for every deal the pipeline still holds (empty replacements if getDeletionImpact reports none). Deals are moved to the replacement pipeline/stage you choose, then the pipeline is removed.
- `deletePipelineStage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a single pipeline stage (owner-only). Pass a dependencyResolution from getDeletionImpact (targetKind DEAL_STAGE): its impactVersion plus a replacement stage for any deals currently on the stage.
- `editDealComment` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace the body of your own deal comment (listDealComments id).
- `filterDeals` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Run a SAVED deal filter (`filterId` from listDealFilters or saveFilter type DEAL) over ONE pipeline (`pipelineId` from listPipelineNames) and page the matching deals with limit/offset: id, title, isArchived, stage and assignees, plus pagination.total (every match, not the page) and hasMore. Saved filters only: to try criteria first, save the filter, run it here, and fix it in place with updateFilter. A deal filter does not carry its pipeline, so the same filter can run over any pipeline you pass. Use getDeal for one deal in full.
- `findDeals` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Search AND TOTAL the deals you can see: `totals` sums EVERY match, not the page (price, average, commission; totalCount is the count), so a total is one call. Filters: title, contact (contactIds: deals of ANY of these contacts in ONE read, matched by each row's linked contacts; page hasMore before calling one dealless, never a findDeals per contact), pipeline, stage (stageId, or stageName in all your own pipelines), outcome OPEN/WON/LOST, stageChangedAfter/Before (last stage move, eg a win; Before exclusive), closeDateAfter/Before, archived, assignees. NUMBERS — quote `totals` as they read; never add, average or count rows yourself. IMPORTANT: archived deals are INCLUDED BY DEFAULT (they sort last). Pass isArchived: false for active-only, always for "what is in my pipeline", or true to find archived ones (to restore with archiveDeal); check each result's isArchived before calling a deal current. Each deal carries its assigned users — an empty array means the deal is UNASSIGNED, nobody owns it — and its linked contacts (id + name). hasAssignedUsers: false gives the unowned deals over every deal you can see (totalCount is the count); userIds (listTeammates, never empty) gives one person's. Whether anyone is on a linked CONTACT comes only from getContact, one call per contact; a partner org's contact it refuses is "not visible to you", not "nobody". Each row carries the commission figures: commissionCents (the derived GCI) and the stored commissionAmountCents / commissionPercentBps / teamSplitAmountCents / teamSplitPercentBps, so a portfolio money question ("our GCI on everything closing this month") is one page. Read them as getDeal documents: amount XOR percent per side; all-null means no commission RECORDED, not zero. participantSplits is NOT here (getDeal). `customFieldValues` IS here, LEANER than on getDeal: the value plus the field NAME (`dealCustomField { name }`), no ids or type, for surveying (who holds which card, which have no Difficulty set) rather than writing back. Read the ONE sub-field matching the type, as getDeal documents. A field never given a value is absent, so an empty list means nothing filled in, never no fields. Custom fields multiply per row: on a `truncated` page lower `limit` rather than assume the missing deals have no values. TASKS — `taskSummary` counts open tasks and appointments on the DEAL (not its contacts); 0 means none, so "which deals have no task" is this page. In Ask Goliath omitting isArchived reads live deals only; null reads both.
- `getDeal` (query, READ) — Fetch one deal by id — title, value, close date, stage, pipeline, COMMISSION AND TEAM SPLIT, CUSTOM-FIELD VALUES, assigned users (empty = unassigned), linked contacts (id + name), and linked deals (`linkedItems`). It does NOT return who is on those contacts: this op also reaches deals on pipelines another org SHARED with yours, whose contacts belong to that org, and the participant read is scoped to your own org — it would come back empty for them and read as "nobody is on this contact" when someone is. To see who is on a contact, call getContact with that contactId: it is guarded to your org, so a contact you cannot see fails loudly instead of answering empty. MONEY — `priceFormatted`/`commissionFormatted` are the price and GCI in dollars: quote them. Commission, team split and participant splits are now READABLE here, and they are the answer to GCI questions. `commissionCents` is the DERIVED total commission on the deal: quote THAT as the deal’s GCI. The other four are the stored write SOURCES, and each side is amount-XOR-percent, so exactly one of a pair is ever non-null: `commissionAmountCents` (a fixed dollar figure, in cents) or `commissionPercentBps` (basis points — 300 bps = 3%, applied to priceCents); and `teamSplitAmountCents` or `teamSplitPercentBps` (basis points applied to the COMMISSION, not the price). So when commissionPercentBps is set, commissionCents is priceCents x bps/10000 and changing the price silently changes the commission; when commissionAmountCents is set, commissionCents equals it and the price is irrelevant. All four sources null with commissionCents null means no commission has been recorded — NOT zero commission; do not report $0 for a deal nobody has filled in. `participantSplits` is the per-teammate allocation of what is left after the team fee (each row: user, splitAmountCents or splitPercentBps). Write all of these through updateDeal / createDeal, which echo them back. CUSTOM FIELDS — `customFieldValues` is the read-back for the customFieldValues input on createDeal / updateDeal (INT-907; there was no read path before). It carries ONLY the fields this deal actually has a value for: a defined field the deal has never been given a value for is ABSENT from the list, not present-and-null, which is the opposite of a contact’s customFields. So an empty list means nothing is filled in, never that the pipeline has no fields — get the pipeline’s full definition set from listDealCustomFields(pipelineId). Each entry names its definition under `dealCustomField` (id, name, type) and carries the value in the ONE sub-field matching that type: TEXT/LINK -> textValue, NUMBER/DOLLAR -> numberValue (a plain number, NOT cents), DATE -> dateValue (ISO 8601), DROPDOWN -> dropdownSelectedValues (the option LABEL strings, not option ids; more than one only when the definition’s allowMultiple is true).
- `getDealDetailTabs` (query, READ) — One pipeline's deal-sheet tabs: each tab's name and its fields in order (`native:<key>` or `custom:<fieldId>`), with the layout version.
- `getDealPipelineLayout` (query, READ) — One pipeline's field layout: each custom field with its display order, showOnCard and cardDisplayOrder (the up-to-5 fields the board card shows), and hiddenDetailFieldKeys (what the deal sheet and create/edit form hide: `native:team|closeDate|dealValue|commission` or `custom:<fieldId>`; null or empty = all shown). Read it before setDealCardFields or setDealDetailHiddenFields, which replace the whole list.
- `getDeletionImpact` (query, READ) — Preview what deleting an org-owned record affects before you do it — it serves every delete op that takes a dependencyResolution, not just the deal ones. Pass targetKind + targetId; returns impactVersion (hand it back to the matching delete op), requiresReplacement, the dependent records grouped, and — when replacement is required — the replacementRequirements (what needs a new home and the valid options). Supported targetKinds: DEAL (deleteDeal), DEAL_PIPELINE / DEAL_STAGE (deletePipeline / deletePipelineStage), CONTACT_CUSTOM_FIELD (deleteContactCustomField), CONTACT_CUSTOM_FIELD_OPTION / DEAL_CUSTOM_FIELD_OPTION (a dropdown option dropped by updateContactCustomField / updateDealCustomField's optionDependencyResolutions), CONTACT_TAG (deleteContactTags), CONTACT_LIST (deleteContactLists), and CONTENT_TEMPLATE (deleteContentTemplate). WORKFLOW_GROUP (a workflow's or appointment reminder's group id) says what references it: deleteAppointmentReminder takes the result as its dependencyResolution, while deleteWorkflow takes no impactVersion, so for a workflow it is read-only. Always call this first: those delete ops need the impactVersion, and it goes stale if anything changes in between — re-read it rather than reusing an old one.
- `getPipelineAnalytics` (query, ADMIN) [rate-limited] — Per-pipeline TRENDS for a rolling period (SEVEN_DAYS | FOURTEEN_DAYS | THIRTY_DAYS | YEAR_TO_DATE; THIRTY_DAYS is the last 30 days, not this month) from a NIGHTLY snapshot (asOfDate): stage duration, stage mix, won/lost/active. wonDeals / lostDeals count EVENTS (moves into a won or lost stage in the window, archived deals included) and miss moves since the snapshot, so they can disagree with the deals as they stand: for "how many won", a win rate or money use findDeals `totals` (outcome WON / LOST, a stageChanged window). Requires the ADMIN scope.
- `linkPipelineItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Link two unarchived deals on your org's own pipelines; both list it (getDeal linkedItems).
- `listDealActivity` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — One deal's activity feed, most-recent-first — the audit trail behind "who changed the price on this deal, and when did it get reassigned?". Each event carries eventType, createdAt, actor (the person, null for system/automation), and a SuperJSON `payload` whose `json` object holds the per-eventType detail. Pass `eventTypes` to narrow to the types you care about — a narrowed read pages at the DATABASE, so a sparse type's full history stays reachable however busy the rest of the feed is; omit it for the mixed feed, which caps at the 200 most recent events. Page with `offset`. THE FULL eventType VOCABULARY, with the payload keys under `payload.json` for each (there is no schema expansion for a SuperJSON scalar, so this text is the only description of the shape). Money keys are cents, `*Bps` are basis points, dates are ISO 8601, and a `from*` key is null when the field had no previous value: `STAGE_CHANGED` (fromStageId, fromStageName, toStageId, toStageName — names are snapshotted at write time, so a renamed stage keeps them; workflow: {workflowAutomationId, name} of the workflow VERSION that made the move (not its workflowGroupId; a republish gives a new one), else absent or null; byPerson: true if a person moved it in-app); `VALUE_CHANGED` (fromCents, toCents — the deal price); `COMMISSION_CHANGED` and `TEAM_SPLIT_CHANGED` (fromCents, toCents, fromBps, toBps — the pair that answers commission-history questions); `CLOSE_DATE_CHANGED` (fromDate, toDate); `ASSIGNED` and `UNASSIGNED` (userId, userName — the person the deal was assigned to or taken from, NOT the actor who did it); `CONTACT_LINKED` and `CONTACT_UNLINKED` (contactId, contactName); `TASK_ADDED` and `TASK_COMPLETED` (taskId, taskTitle, isAppointment — true means it was an appointment, not a to-do); `FILE_ADDED` and `FILE_REMOVED` (fileId, fileName); `DEAL_CREATED`, `DEAL_ARCHIVED`, `DEAL_RESTORED` (no payload keys beyond actor); `COMMENT` (body — the comment text; listDealComments is the same feed pre-narrowed to this type); `SCRAPER_HEALTH_MOVED` (only on Scraper Health cards — the reasoning written with each move by moveScraperHealthCard / upsertScraperHealthCard: healthActor (monitor | doctor | person — which kind of mover, since `actor` is always the key owner), fromStage and toStage (stage NAMES, fromStage null on the event that opened the card), why, checked, found, nextTime (free text, null when not given), delivered, expected, windowDays (the numbers at that moment), handoffSummary (the short "what happened, where it stands" a person reads first)); `CONTRACT_EVENT` (contractId, envelopeId: the contract and its signing attempt; kind: SENT, OPENED, SIGNED, COMPLETED, DECLINED, VOIDED or EXPIRED; recipientId: the signer who opened, signed or declined, null otherwise; fileId: on COMPLETED, the signed PDF filed on the contract contacts. The title and names are not in the payload: read the contract for them). Those nineteen are the whole vocabulary: an eventType outside this list does not exist. What the feed does NOT record is edits to a deal's title, description or custom-field values — no event type covers them, so their history is not reconstructable here.
- `listDealComments` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — One deal's comment thread, most-recent-first (the activity feed narrowed to COMMENT events, paged at the database — the full thread stays reachable however busy the rest of the feed is). The comment text is in the SuperJSON payload at `json.body`; actor identifies the commenter. Page with offset.
- `listDealCustomFields` (query, READ) — List a deal pipeline's custom-field DEFINITIONS (by pipelineId from listPipelines): id, name, type (TEXT/NUMBER/DOLLAR/DATE/LINK/DROPDOWN), dropdown options, allowMultiple, defaultValue. Deal custom fields are per-pipeline. DEFINITIONS ONLY — no deal's recorded value appears here: read those from getDeal's `customFieldValues`, which lists only the fields a given deal has been given a value for. Use each id as the customFieldId in the deal's customFieldValues input on createDeal / updateDeal to write values.
- `listDealFiles` (query, READ) [max limit 25] — Files attached to a deal, most-recent-first — screenshots, recordings, documents. Each entry carries id, fileName, contentType-bearing fileUrl and createdAt. fileUrl is a time-limited signed HTTPS URL: fetch it promptly and do not persist or share it, and re-read this op rather than caching the URL. Each URL is signed per file, so the page is small (limit defaults to 25 and is capped there) — a full page means there may be more, so page with offset. This is the ONLY way to reach an attachment's bytes — a Slack-sourced deal records its attachments as a bare filename at the end of the description (`Attachments: Screenshot ….png`), which names the file but cannot open it. To ADD a file your org already holds (by its artifactId), use attachDealFile; to detach one, removeDealFile. Returns an empty list for a deal with no files, which is different from a deal you cannot see: a foreign or unknown dealId is refused at the gateway.
- `listDealFilters` (query, READ) — List the saved DEAL filters VISIBLE to the key owner: every shared deal filter in the organization plus your own private ones. Metadata plus `criteriaSummary` (its conditions in one line); read one filter's whole tree with getFilter, create one with saveFilter (type: DEAL), change it with updateFilter. Run one with filterDeals. The Deals board in the app has no saved-filter list, so a deal filter lives here, not in a sidebar. Every row carries `userId`, the OWNER: a row whose userId is not the key owner's is a teammate's filter, so say whose it is before changing or deleting it.
