- `listPipelineNames` (query, READ) — List the organization's own deal pipelines, id and name only, oldest first. `sameNameCount` is how many share the row's name. Use this to find a pipeline id by name. For every pipeline's stages in one call, use listPipelines.
- `listPipelines` (query, READ) — List the organization's deal pipelines with per-stage deal counts and values. Counts cover only deals you can see. `total` and stage `value` are WHOLE DOLLARS, not cents (1355000 is $1,355,000). Archived deals are excluded; a date window or a won total is findDeals `totals`. `deals`/`total` include won/lost stages; open is `outcome` open. `sameNameCount` is how many pipelines share the row's name: quote it, never count rows. Use the returned pipeline id with findDeals (its pipelineId filter) to list a pipeline's deals.
- `listPipelineStages` (query, READ) — One pipeline's stages, in order (all pipelines: listStagesOfPipelines).
- `listPipelineTransitions` (query, ADMIN) [rate-limited] — Stage-to-stage deal movement (the funnel) for a reporting period (same period values as getPipelineAnalytics), optionally narrowed to one pipelineId — per transition: deal counts, exits from the source stage, and won/lost outcomes. Data is a nightly snapshot — see asOfDate. Requires the ADMIN scope (key owner must be a team admin).
- `listStagesOfPipelines` (query, READ) — Every owned and shared pipeline and its stages, in order; a large organization's answer is cut short. A stage by name is SEARCH_CONTEXT DEAL_STAGE (every pipeline; a miss is final), and every deal in it, in your own pipelines, findDeals `stageName`. Names repeat: move a deal only within its own pipeline.
- `listStalledDeals` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — List deals going cold — no activity for a while, ordered by days inactive, of deals you can see. Returns each deal with its stage, pipeline, linked contact, and inactiveDays.
- `removeDealExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove a deal link.
- `removeDealFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Detach one file from a deal by fileId (fileIds come from listDealFiles). This removes the link only — the underlying stored file/bytes are not deleted. Removing a file that is not on the deal, or already removed, is a no-op. Returns the deal id. The deal must be in a pipeline owned by or shared with your organization.
- `reorderDealCustomFields` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the display order of one pipeline's custom fields: pass every field id of that pipeline (listDealCustomFields), first = top. An id from another pipeline is refused. Presentation only: no value, filter or workflow changes.
- `reorderPipelineStages` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Reorder a pipeline's stages (by pipelineId): pass every stage id in the desired order. Owner-only: the pipeline must be OWNED by your organization. Returns the pipeline with its stages in the new order.
- `setDealCardFields` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Choose the fields every deal card on one pipeline's board shows: at most 5 field ids of that pipeline, built-ins included, in order. REPLACES the set (empty shows none), for everyone. Org admins only. Returns the fields with showOnCard and cardDisplayOrder.
- `setDealDetailHiddenFields` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Hide fields from one pipeline's deal sheet and create/edit form, for everyone: `hiddenFieldKeys` REPLACES the hidden set (getDealPipelineLayout first; an empty list shows everything). Keys are `native:team|closeDate|dealValue|commission` or `custom:<fieldId>`; Stage is never hidden and an unknown key is dropped. Hiding keeps every value.
- `setDealDetailTabs` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace one pipeline's deal-sheet tabs for everyone (getDealDetailTabs first, and pass its version as expectedVersion: a stale one is refused). Owner pipelines only.
- `surveyDeals` (query, READ) [max limit 45] — Survey deals — findDeals' search (same visibility), without stageName/outcome/windows/totals, with a deliberately LEAN row: deal id, title, isArchived, stage NAME, pipeline NAME, assigned users by NAME, open-task counts, and custom-field values. Use this whenever the question is about MANY deals rather than about a few in full — "who holds which card", "which cards have no Difficulty set", "what is on this board", any board-wide count or grouping. Use findDeals instead when you need money (commission / team split), linked contacts, close date, price, createdAt/updatedAt, or the ids inside a row; use getDeal for one deal in full. A capped result DROPS WHOLE DEALS silently: when `truncated` is true, lower `limit` and page (`__omittedItems` counts the dropped rows). `totalCount` is the UNPAGED total to quote for "how many". IDS — the row carries names, not ids, for everything except the deal itself: stage ids from listStagesOfPipelines, user ids from listTeammates, custom-field ids and types from listDealCustomFields. The deal `id` IS here — pass it to getDeal or updateDeal to act on a row. ARCHIVED deals are included when isArchived is omitted, as in findDeals; check each row's isArchived. ASSIGNEES — an EMPTY `users` means UNASSIGNED; filter with hasAssignedUsers / userIds as in findDeals. No linked contacts here. CUSTOM FIELDS — each entry carries the value plus the field NAME (no id, no type). Read the value from the ONE slot matching the field type: TEXT/LINK -> textValue, NUMBER/DOLLAR -> numberValue (a plain number, NOT cents), DATE -> dateValue (ISO 8601), DROPDOWN -> dropdownSelectedValues (the option LABEL strings). A field the deal has never been given a value for is ABSENT from the list rather than present-and-null, so an empty list means nothing is filled in on that deal — never that the pipeline has no fields (get the definitions from listDealCustomFields(pipelineId)). TASKS — `taskSummary` counts open tasks and appointments on the DEAL (not its contacts); 0 means none, so "which deals have no task" is this page. In Ask Goliath omitting isArchived reads live deals only; null reads both.
- `unlinkPipelineItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove a deal link (getDeal linkedItems id).
- `updateDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update a deal by id: title, price, close date, stage. THIS IS THE STAGE-MOVE OPERATION: send input { stageId } alone (from listPipelineStages); fields left out are untouched, and the move stamps lastStageChangeAt. A stage change is POTENTIALLY OUTBOUND by TWO paths: (1) entering the stage wakes any DEAL workflow triggered on it; (2) it fires a deal-updated event for EVERY attached contact, and a CONTACT workflow anywhere in the org can match the destination stage, so a clean pipeline does NOT prove the move is silent. Either can text or email a real person. Do NOT reason "reversible, so just do it": undoing the move does not recall a message. A move the person asked for by name is their yes; any other move of a deal with contacts needs their yes before it runs (a card counts). The deal, stage and linked contactIds/userIds must belong to your organization (or a pipeline shared with it). contactIds, propertyIds and userIds REPLACE the whole linked set: send every id to keep. Pass expectedUpdatedAt (updatedAt from getDeal, findDeals or a previous write) whenever you decided from an earlier read, so a concurrent edit fails loudly. It makes the write conditional and ALL-OR-NOTHING: a change since gives CONFLICT with nothing written, and a rejected userIds, participantSplits or customFieldValues rolls the whole edit back. The token is single-use: re-read before guarding again. Without it a later custom-field failure cannot undo the committed core write. A deleted deal is NOT_FOUND (do not retry); a bad token is BAD_USER_INPUT. MONEY AND CUSTOM FIELDS (the whole input is one variable, so discovery cannot expand it). One commission source per side: `commissionAmountCents` XOR `commissionPercentBps` (basis points, 300 = 3%, of priceCents), and `teamSplitAmountCents` XOR `teamSplitPercentBps` (of the COMMISSION). Both halves with values is rejected; one sent as null CLEARS that side. The server derives `commissionCents` (GCI) and returns it: read it there. A percent re-derives when priceCents changes; an amount does not. `participantSplits` is [{ userId, splitAmountCents | splitPercentBps }] of what remains after the team fee, within the pool. `customFieldValues` is [{ customFieldId (listDealCustomFields; fields are PER-PIPELINE), exactly ONE of textValue (TEXT/LINK) | numberValue (NUMBER/DOLLAR, a plain number, NOT cents) | dateValue (DATE, ISO 8601) | dropdownSelectedValues (DROPDOWN option LABELS, not ids) }]. The response echoes the money and custom fields: confirm the write from it.
- `updateDealCustomField` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Edit an existing deal custom-field DEFINITION in place (by id from listDealCustomFields). THIS IS THE CORRECT WAY TO ADD A DROPDOWN OPTION or fix a wrong name or default — do not create a second field. Owner-only: the field's pipeline must be OWNED by your organization; a field on a pipeline merely shared with you cannot be edited. Omitted fields are untouched. The field's TYPE cannot be changed. `options` applies to DROPDOWN fields and REPLACES the whole option list rather than appending: send every option you want to keep, each existing one as { id, label } with its id from listDealCustomFields, and each new one as { label } with no id. To RENAME an option, send its existing id with the new label: every value already recorded on deals, the field's default, and the saved filters and queued bulk tasks naming the old label all move to the new one. Sending a new label WITHOUT the id instead removes the old option and creates a different one. Any existing option you leave out is REMOVED; if deals or filters still reference a removed option the call is rejected until you pass optionDependencyResolutions: from getDeletionImpact (DEAL_CUSTOM_FIELD_OPTION, the option id), the person picking each replacement. A default that is no longer one of the options is cleared. Names must be unique within the pipeline. Returns the updated field with its full option list.
- `updateDealExternalLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change a deal link's title or url (linkId from getDeal's externalLinks); an omitted one is kept.
- `updatePipeline` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update a deal pipeline's title and/or description (by pipelineId from listPipelines). Owner-only: the pipeline must be OWNED by your organization — a pipeline merely shared with you cannot be edited.
- `updatePipelineStage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update one pipeline stage (by stageId from listPipelineStages) — rename, change description, toggle isTerminal / terminalType (WON|LOST|NEUTRAL), or set winProbability (0-100). Only the fields you pass change. Owner-only: the stage's pipeline must be OWNED by your organization.

## employees

- `acceptEmployeeSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Accept one of an AI employee's suggestion cards (listEmployeeSuggestions): its edit lands on the employee's instructions, as the employee page's Accept does. `outcome` APPLIED, RETIRED (the instructions moved on; the card is gone) or REFUSED (`message` says what to fix). Only when the person asks for this card, and it waits for their yes (the write says how to ask).
- `assignEmployeeToContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put one AI employee on one contact, optionally on a schedule, the contact card's Add. From then on it answers the contact's texts, emails and calls, and a schedule runs it on that cadence. A schedule is a 5-field cron (`cronExpression`) read in an IANA `timezone`, at most once a day, and `maxRuns`, how many runs before it stops (never open-ended; at most five years of runs). The employee must be switched on and from this organization. Many contacts with no schedule: attachEmployeeToContacts. Needs their yes; a card's counts.
- `attachEmployeeMailbox` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Give an AI employee a mailbox to email from and be woken by (`mailboxId` from listEmployeeChannelOptions): a connected inbox, shared with the organization, with a live connection, that no other employee owns. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `attachEmployeeToContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put an AI employee on contacts (at most 200 ids per call; send more in further calls). It then answers those contacts' texts, emails and calls and works them. The employee must be switched on (setEmployeeStatus) and every contact one the key owner can open. Recorded as the key owner's own assignment, so a contact someone took the employee off is put back because you named it. `changedCount` is how many it was newly put on; the rest already had it. When `interruptedContactId` is set the batch stopped there (`interruptedReason` says why): the contacts before it are done, so send that one and the rest again. Confirm the contacts with the person first.
- `cancelEmployeeFollowUp` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Cancel a follow-up an AI employee booked on a contact before it runs (`followUpId`: a FOLLOW_UP row's `id` from getContactEmployees' `upcomingAgentRuns`). A CRON row is a schedule: clearEmployeeSchedule. Returns CANCELLED, or NOT_FOUND when it already ran or is not this contact's.
- `clearEmployeeSchedule` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Drop the schedule of one employee on one contact (`attachmentId` from getContactEmployees). It stays on the contact and still answers when the contact writes in. Safe to repeat. A booked FOLLOW_UP is not a schedule: that is cancelEmployeeFollowUp.
- `commentOnEmployeeSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Comment on one of an AI employee's suggestion cards ("keep the opener shorter"). It changes nothing on the card; the employee reads it when it writes its next cards, recorded as a comment through the API, not as feedback heard from a person. Only when the person asks, passing on what they said. `heard` is false while the organization's memory is off. `submissionKey` is REQUIRED: a new one (1 to 100 characters, e.g. a UUID) per comment, sent again unchanged on a retry, so a retried call is heard once.
- `createEmployee` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Hire an AI employee. It is ALWAYS created switched off (INACTIVE), whatever the config says: it answers nobody until it is switched on. Omit `config` for the generalist an operator gets with no template (texts, emails and calls once a phone line or mailbox is attached, notes, tasks, notifying a teammate, booking its own follow-up), then shape it with updateEmployeeConfig; or pass a COMPLETE config document in the shape getEmployee returns as `configDocument`. The same checks the employee builder runs apply, and a refusal names each field and what to change. Returns the new employee and its `configDocument`.
- `createEmployeeAnswerWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create the DRAFT workflow that hands an employee its contacts' inbound texts (on its lines, else the org's) or emails (its mailboxes, else any). Nothing runs until it is published (promoteWorkflowDraft). One that already starts the employee comes back instead.
- `deleteEmployee` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete an AI employee, the employee page's Fire. It is taken off every contact (their schedules go), its mailboxes and lines are released and its forms stop waking it; its history stays, but it cannot be brought back. Admins only: a member is refused, so check getMyProfile's `organizationRole` first and tell a member an organization admin has to fire it. Refused while anything still names it (a workflow step, a saved filter, an automation trigger, an assignment policy); the refusal lists what to change first. Say its contact count (getEmployee's `commitments`). Needs their yes; a card's counts. To stop it for now, switch it off instead (setEmployeeStatus).
- `detachEmployeeFromContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take an AI employee off contacts (at most 200 ids per call). It stops answering and working them and their schedules are dropped; the history stays. `changedCount` is how many it was taken off. When `interruptedContactId` is set the batch stopped there (`interruptedReason` says why): the contacts before it are done, so send that one and the rest again. Confirm with the person first.
- `detachEmployeeMailbox` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take a mailbox off an AI employee (an id from getEmployee `mailboxes`): it stops emailing from it and is no longer woken by mail to it. Safe to repeat. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `detachEmployeePhoneLine` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Release a phone line an AI employee still holds from before lines were shared (an id from getEmployee `legacyPhoneLines`). It cannot be attached back, since lines are no longer assigned to employees: it stops answering calls to that number and no longer takes on new people who text it. Refused when the line is not on this employee. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `discardEmployeeReplyDraft` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Retired (#41897): always refused, since no reply is held any more. Do not call it; a reply waiting on a person is a reply card in the app.
- `dismissEmployeeSuggestion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Dismiss one of an AI employee's suggestion cards (listEmployeeSuggestions) with a reason (NOT_RELEVANT, WRONG_TONE, WRONG_FACTS, ALREADY_DONE or OTHER). Recorded as dismissed through the API, not as feedback heard from a person. Only when the person says to, with the reason they gave.
- `getContactEmployees` (query, READ) — The AI employees on one contact, as the contact page's card shows them. `aiEmployees[].id` is the attachment id setEmployeeSchedule and clearEmployeeSchedule take (`agentId` is the employee); `status` PAUSED means it stopped working this contact (REMOVED, with `includeRemoved`, means it was taken off); `isWorkingNow` means it is mid-conversation. `upcomingAgentRuns` is what they will do next, soonest first, AT MOST 25 with no total (when 25 come back more may be booked, so after acting on these read again before saying none are left): a CRON row is a schedule's next run, a FOLLOW_UP row a follow-up the employee booked itself, whose `id` cancelEmployeeFollowUp takes.
- `getEmployee` (query, READ) — One AI employee in full. `abilities` is what it can do RIGHT NOW, resolved (a tool missing from the stored config follows its default, and most defaults are on, so read `abilities`, never infer from the document). `config.wakes` is what wakes it. `mailboxes` and `triggerForms` are its channels; `legacyPhoneLines` lists only lines it still holds from before lines were shared, since an employee needs no number of its own (it texts on the number the conversation is on, otherwise a shared organization number): an empty list is the normal state, never something to attach, ask about or report; `defaultAssignees` who owns a contact it works when nobody does. `commitments`: `assignedContactCount` the contacts it is on, `scheduledContactCount` only those on a repeating schedule, and `bookedFollowUpContactCount` those with a follow-up it booked itself that has not run yet, so 0 scheduled never means no follow-up is coming. It holds no trust of its own: what it does on its own follows the trust of the person each act is for (the line or mailbox owner, else the contact's teammate, else its Manager), set on that person's Memory, Trust page. A text `sendWindow` holds only what it starts (follow-ups, outreach): its text reply to a lead who wrote in goes out at any hour. `configDocument` is the whole configuration as one JSON document; change part of it with updateEmployeeConfig's `edits` and `configPatch`. Webhook urls read back redacted and are kept on save. `updatedAt` is the `expectedUpdatedAt` to pass so a teammate's save in between is refused rather than overwritten.
- `getEmployeeCaseload` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — The contacts one AI employee is on, newest attachment first, offset-paged (`offset`, `limit`; `total` is the full count). Each row says whether it is working that contact now, when it last worked it, the next run of a repeating schedule (`attachment.schedule`), the soonest follow-up it booked itself (`nextBookedFollowUpAt`, null when none), and whether the contact replied or escalated. A new touch on a contact with one booked comes before that follow-up. `includeRemoved: true` adds contacts a person took it off.
- `listContactReplyDrafts` (query, READ) — Retired (#41897): always returns an empty list. AI employees no longer hold replies here; a reply waiting on a person is a reply card in the app.
- `listEmployeeChannelOptions` (query, READ) — What an AI employee can be bound to right now: `availableMailboxes` (connected Gmail or Outlook inboxes shared with the organization that no employee owns yet; the `id` attachEmployeeMailbox takes) and `availableTriggerForms` (the organization's forms, any status; ids for setEmployeeTriggerForms). Phone numbers are not assigned to employees: an employee replies on the number the conversation is on, otherwise a shared organization number.
- `listEmployeeRevisions` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — An AI employee's saved versions, newest first (offset-paged; advance by `nextOffset`). One per save: the version from before a change is the one saved just before it (`createdAt`). Each says when, who saved it (`actorName`, else `actorUserId`; neither for the system) and the name and job title it held. To put one back, restoreEmployeeRevision.
- `listEmployees` (query, READ) — The organization's AI employees: id, name, job title, status (ACTIVE = working, INACTIVE = hired but switched off), the template it started from, whether it can answer calls, and how many contacts it is on. `contactAgentCounts` counts that list (`total`, `active`, `inactive`): quote those numbers for how many employees there are and how many are on or off, never a tally of the rows. `textHours` is when it starts texts, in words (anytime when none is set), and `quietHoursNotice` the quiet-hours note to say when the window crosses 8 AM to 9 PM: what hours each texts are answered from this one read, never a getEmployee per employee (a roster past about 100 employees ends in an omitted marker naming the rest: read those with getEmployee). The `id` is the `employeeId` every other employee operation takes. Start here.
- `listEmployeeSuggestions` (query, READ) — An AI employee's pending suggestion cards, newest first: edits it proposes to its own instructions (`action`), with how sure it is (`confidence`). A person accepts one on the employee's page; dismissEmployeeSuggestion and commentOnEmployeeSuggestion answer one for them.
- `removeEmployeesFromContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take AI employees off contacts: they stop working them and their schedules are dropped; the history stays. EMPTY employeeIds takes off EVERY employee, system-managed ones included, so say so before you send it. A bulk task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). The person approves it on a card.
- `restoreEmployeeRevision` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put an AI employee back to a saved version (`revisionId` from listEmployeeRevisions): its instructions, settings, name and job title as that version held them (the avatar is kept, and a setting that version never had keeps its current value), saved as a new version. updateEmployeeConfig's checks apply, the screening one included. Pass `expectedUpdatedAt`. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `runEmployeesOnContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put AI employees on contacts and wake each pairing once (runNow, default true), and/or on a `schedule` (cron, timezone, maxRuns; no denser than daily). `message` (max 2000 chars) is an internal instruction carried into every run; the contact never sees it. Employees must be switched on. Like attachEmployeeToContacts it puts back a contact someone took that employee off (unless they did so after this call), so leave those out first. A contact the employee already has a follow-up booked for (`nextBookedFollowUpAt` on getEmployeeCaseload) gets a second touch before that one: say how many of the batch have one, so the person can choose. A bulk task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). The person approves it on a card.
- `setEmployeeDailyCaps` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set an AI employee's own daily caps, which bound what it spends: `dailyRunCap` (live runs a day) and `dailyCallCap` (connected calls a day). Each is a whole number from 1 to 10,000; there is no 0, so to stop it, switch it off with setEmployeeStatus. An omitted cap is kept; an explicit null removes it (no per-employee cap). No screen sets these. Read the current caps with getEmployee and state the old and new first. Pass `expectedUpdatedAt`. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `setEmployeeDefaultAssignees` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Who becomes the owner of a contact an AI employee works when the contact has no owner. `mode` decides what `assigneeUserIds` holds (teammate user ids, listTeamMembers): TEAM_RANDOM (the default, any active teammate), NONE (nobody) and SAME_AS_NEW_LEADS (the organization's lead routing) take `[]`; SPECIFIC_USER exactly one; ROUND_ROBIN_LIST two or more, in rotation order. A mismatched pair is refused.
- `setEmployeeSchedule` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace (or add) the schedule of one employee on one contact (`attachmentId` from getContactEmployees). A fresh cadence: runs already spent do not count against it. A schedule is a 5-field cron (`cronExpression`) read in an IANA `timezone`, at most once a day, and `maxRuns`, how many runs before it stops (never open-ended; at most five years of runs). Each run can text, email or call the contact, so it needs their yes; a card's counts.
- `setEmployeeStatus` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Switch an AI employee on (ACTIVE) or off (INACTIVE). ON means it starts answering and working the contacts it is on, with real people, right away, which may publish its answer workflows; OFF stops it mid-conversation on every contact it is working. Say which and to how many contacts (getEmployee's `commitments`) and get the person's yes before either. The employee's own chat records the change. Same as the switch on the employee's page.
- `setEmployeeTriggerForms` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set which forms wake an AI employee when someone submits one. `formIds` REPLACES the set (ids from listEmployeeChannelOptions; every one must be this organization's); `[]` means no form wakes it. A form that is not live yet wakes it once it goes live. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.
- `stopEmployeeRuns` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Stop what one AI employee is doing on one contact right now (getContactEmployees' `isWorkingNow`). The run stops at its next step, with anything it started; it stays on the contact and wakes again the next time something wakes it. A stopped run does not come back. Returns STOP_REQUESTED, or NOTHING_RUNNING when it was idle.
- `updateEmployeeConfig` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change an AI employee's configuration. To change part of it (a sentence, its tone, an hour), send only the change: `edits` are exact `{ find, replace }` pairs, each `find` copied from `configDocument` and found exactly once across its text (instructions, call scripts), applied in order, all or nothing; `configPatch` is a JSON merge patch for settings (objects merge, anything else replaces; a list to clear is `[]`, e.g. `{ channels: { emailConfig: { sendWindow: {...} } } }`), and a whole new `prompt` goes there too. Whatever you do not name is left as it is. Send `config`, the COMPLETE document, only to rewrite everything; a write that drops text or a channel nobody edited is refused. `name`, `title` and `avatar` are kept when omitted; an empty `title` clears it. The employee builder's checks run on every call and a refusal names each field and what to change: the voice must be one the workspace can use, the instructions must fit, and no line may tell the employee to claim to be a person or deny being an AI. A change that turns off do-not-call or known-litigator screening is refused with the exact sentence to put to the person; ask them, and send the same call again with `acknowledgeScreeningWeakening: true` only if they agree. Pass `expectedUpdatedAt` (the `updatedAt` you read) so a teammate's save in between is refused rather than overwritten. A text `sendWindow` outside 8 AM to 9 PM is saved as asked; the result's `quietHoursNotice` then names the hours in words, and the reply says it once. `textHours` is the window as saved, in words. Does not switch the employee on or off.
- `updateEmployeeIdentity` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename an AI employee or change its job title or avatar, nothing else (an omitted field is kept; an empty `title` clears it). A rename is carried into its instructions, as on its page. Pass `expectedUpdatedAt`. On an employee that is switched on it takes effect on its next run: needs their yes; a card’s counts.

## files

- `deleteDataExport` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Dismiss a FAILED standalone export from the Files list (the row is kept for the record). Any other export is refused as not found.
- `deleteExportConfiguration` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete an export preset for the whole org, for good (listExportConfigurations id). Exports already made keep their files. Returns false when nothing matched.
- `deletePendingUpload` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY remove an upload that is still waiting for review (not yet imported). Returns true; an upload already imported, already gone or not yours is refused with an error, not false. Requires the user's explicit approval.
- `exportContacts` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Export contacts to a spreadsheet, the download dialog's Start. Selection: `ids` (selectAll false), or a saved `filterId` with `selectAll: true` (every match; `excludeIds` leaves some out) or `selectCount: N` (the first N); `totalCount` is how many the selection holds (round up for a filter) and `estimatedItemCount` the same count. `fileName` names the file. Spends export credits: the same credits as the app with no other cap (plan allowance first, then real money; checkBillingAction first), so name the count and the credits and have the person agree before a large one. Async: poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId); the file is getExportReport(dataExportId) once it finishes. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.
- `exportProperties` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Export properties (esIds) to a spreadsheet. Selection: `ids` (selectAll false), or a saved `filterId` with `selectAll: true` (every match; `excludeIds` leaves some out) or `selectCount: N` (the first N); `totalCount` is how many the selection holds (round up for a filter) and `estimatedItemCount` the same count. `fileName` names the file. `includeStreetViewImages` adds a Street View link per row. Spends export credits: the same credits as the app with no other cap (plan allowance first, then real money; checkBillingAction first), so name the count and the credits and have the person agree before a large one. Async: poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId); the file is getExportReport(dataExportId) once it finishes. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.
- `getExportReport` (query, READ) — One export's report, by `dataExportId` (a listFiles `downloads` id, or the one a bulk task returns): its type, rows, the saved filter it was run from, and its skip-trace and enrichment outcomes and spend. It never reads the file, so it cannot say which columns or phone numbers the file holds.
- `getUploadReport` (query, READ) — One upload's report — what its report sheet shows: rows in the file, how many contacts or properties it created, matched to existing records, restored, merged, skipped, failed or duplicated, and its skip-trace outcome and spend. Needs to be the uploader or able to see all contacts. Read the rows behind a count with listUploadReportRows.
- `listExportConfigurations` (query, READ) — The org's saved export presets (the download dialog's row shapes): id, name, description, and which one is the default the dialog opens with.
- `listFiles` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — The Files list, newest first: `uploads` (imports — status, type, file name, rows, who and when; the id is the `fileProcessingTaskId` for getUploadReport) and `downloads` (standalone exports — the id is the `dataExportId` for getExportReport). `filterTree` is a BULK_TASK filter tree, the same `{ id, operator, conditions: [{ id, fieldId, value }], groups }` shape every filter takes. Uploads only: `{"id":"r","operator":"AND","groups":[],"conditions":[{"id":"u","fieldId":"hasFileProcessingTask","value":true}]}`. Downloads only: conditions `hasDataExport` true AND `hasFileProcessingTask` false. Both: an OR group of the two presence conditions. Add `fileName` (text) to search names, `fileProcessingTaskType` / `dataExportType` (["CONTACTS"|"PROPERTIES"|"SKIPTRACES"|"PROPERTY_SIGNALS"]) for a type. Page with limit/offset.
- `listUploadReportRows` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — The rows of one upload's report in one `bucket` (ALL_ROWS, CREATED, MATCHED, RESTORED, MERGED_AFTER_IMPORT, DUPLICATE_ROWS, SKIPPED, FAILED): the row number, its outcome and reason, the original CSV row, and the contact or property it became. Page with limit/offset; `total` counts the bucket. A later step on these contacts acts on each row's `contact.id`, never a lookup by name (two contacts can share one).
- `renameDataExport` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename an export's file. The contact list or property tag the export made keeps the name it was given.
- `renameUploadedFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename an uploaded file (listFiles `uploads[].file.id`, or a deal's or contact's file).
- `setDefaultExportConfiguration` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Make one export preset (listExportConfigurations id) the org's default in the download dialog, for everyone.
- `skipTraceAndCreateContactsFromProperties` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Bulk skip trace properties (esIds) and make a contact for each owner, into an export list, plus `contactListIds` and enrolled in `contactWorkflowIds` (which can text or email them). Selection: `ids` (selectAll false), or a saved `filterId` with `selectAll: true` (every match; `excludeIds` leaves some out) or `selectCount: N` (the first N); `totalCount` is how many the selection holds (round up for a filter) and `estimatedItemCount` the same count. `fileName` names the file. CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT PER PROPERTY: the same credits as the app with no other cap (plan allowance first, then real money; checkBillingAction first), so name the count and the credits and have the person agree before a large one. Async: poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId); the file is getExportReport(dataExportId) once it finishes. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.
- `skipTraceAndExportProperties` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Bulk skip trace properties (esIds) and export owners, phones and emails to a spreadsheet. Selection: `ids` (selectAll false), or a saved `filterId` with `selectAll: true` (every match; `excludeIds` leaves some out) or `selectCount: N` (the first N); `totalCount` is how many the selection holds (round up for a filter) and `estimatedItemCount` the same count. `fileName` names the file. CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT PER PROPERTY: the same credits as the app with no other cap (plan allowance first, then real money; checkBillingAction first), so name the count and the credits and have the person agree before a large one. Async: poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId); the file is getExportReport(dataExportId) once it finishes. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.
- `skipTraceContacts` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Bulk skip trace contacts for phones and emails. Selection: `ids` (selectAll false), or a saved `filterId` with `selectAll: true` (every match; `excludeIds` leaves some out) or `selectCount: N` (the first N); `totalCount` is how many the selection holds (round up for a filter) and `estimatedItemCount` the same count. `fileName` names the file. `skiptraceAddress` picks the address (omit for the default). CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT PER CONTACT: the same credits as the app with no other cap (plan allowance first, then real money; checkBillingAction first), so name the count and the credits and have the person agree before a large one. Async: poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId); the file is getExportReport(dataExportId) once it finishes. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.

## forms

- `createForm` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a lead-capture form. Requires name and fieldConfig. At least one field is required and at most one calendar field is allowed. Entries must match that shape exactly - a malformed entry (bad type/width/etc.) or an unrecognized mapping is rejected with a validation error naming the offending field. fieldConfig is the form's ENTIRE page-and-field document, in one of two shapes. (a) SINGLE PAGE: a flat array of field objects. (b) MULTI-STEP (pages / steps): { "fields": [ ...the same fields, each with a "stepId" ], "steps": [ { "id": "page-1", "name": "Your details", "title": "...", "subtitle": "...", "ctaLabel": "Continue" } ], "showStepProgress": true }. Multi-page forms ARE supported. Steps are pages in array order, with a "Step N of M" progress indicator unless "showStepProgress" is false. Step "id" is unique; "name" labels the step in the FORM BUILDER only. Visitors see "title"/"subtitle" and "ctaLabel" (button text); a "ctaLabel" on the LAST step BEATS submitButtonLabel. In a ONE-step envelope they render nothing (use headerText / descriptionText / submitButtonLabel). An unknown stepId is REJECTED, as is any "stepId" in shape (a): steps require the envelope. No "stepId" = first page; keep "order" unique and ascending. BRANCHING: a step's "routes" run in order, each { "match": "all" | "any", "conditions": [ { "fieldKey", "anyOf": [option labels; "true"/"false" for a checkbox] } ], "goTo": a LATER step id | "submit" }; "otherwise" (same values) covers the rest (default: next step). Conditions test dropdown/multiselect/checkbox fields on that step or earlier; a bad destination, or a step "id" of "submit", is REJECTED. A skipped step's required fields are not required. "endings": [ { "id", "name", "title", "subtitle", "icon" (check|calendar|mail|heart|star|info|none), "iconColor" (#rrggbb), "workflowGroupIds", "agentIds", "tagIds", "listIds" } ]; "goTo"/"otherwise" "end:<id>" ends there, adding its ids to the form's actions ("submitted" is reserved). "createsLead": true on one step before the last creates the lead when it is done; later answers join that contact. "collectsConsent": true shows consent and terms on that step only (default: the lead step, else the last).Each field object is { fieldKey, label, type, required, order, width, mapping, dropdownOptions?, placeholder?, stepId? } plus the optional keys below. `type` is one of text|email|phone|number|dollar|dropdown|multiselect|textarea|checkbox|address|calendar; `width` is full|half|third. `mapping` is one of firstName|lastName|fullName|email|phone|address|note|none|customField:<id> — fullName is ONE box for the whole name. LENGTH LIMITS, refused at write time (never truncated) with a message naming the field: `fieldKey` at 200 characters, every `dropdownOptions` entry (and the `formOptionLabel` copied from it) at 256. FIELD KEYS beyond the common ones — the list above is NOT the whole vocabulary. `hideLabel` hides the label visually while leaving it for screen readers. `validation` takes { minLength, maxLength, pattern, customErrorMessage } and, for an address field, { addressMode: "single" | "split", requireStreet, requireCity, requireState, requireZipCode, requireCountry }. `customFieldOptionMappings` is [{ formOptionLabel, customFieldOptionId }] and maps the option labels of a dropdown OR multiselect field onto an EXISTING custom field's options instead of minting new ones. Every label (a multiselect answer is split per label) resolves through this table, and an unmapped label is SILENTLY SKIPPED — the submission succeeds and that CRM field stays empty. So map every option. `calendarConfig` configures a calendar field: { slotDurationMinutes: [..], defaultDurationMinutes, bufferBeforeMinutes, bufferAfterMinutes, maxAdvanceDays, minNoticeHours, appointmentTitleTemplate, defaultLocation?, locationType?: "VIDEO_CALL" | "CUSTOM" | "PHONE_CALL", meetingId?, meetingPasscode?, calendarProvider?: "GOOGLE" | "MICROSOFT", requireCardToConfirm? }. `locationType: "VIDEO_CALL"` makes the join link minted on the host’s calendar (Google Meet, or Teams when calendarProvider is MICROSOFT) the location; "CUSTOM" (the default) shows `defaultLocation` — an address or a pasted Zoom link. A CUSTOM `defaultLocation` that is a Zoom, Teams or Webex URL is the booking’s ONLY join point: no Meet / Teams link is minted, and reminders, webhooks and the host notification use it. `meetingId` and `meetingPasscode` go in the invite; the fallback confirmation carries only the link. The public form hides both but shows the link, so a `?pwd=` link is public. "PHONE_CALL" mints no link and the host calls the number the booker entered, so the form must have a REQUIRED `type: "phone"` field mapped to `phone`, or the write is refused. A calendar field with NO calendarConfig renders no picker at all, and nothing errors, so always send it. CONSENT IS NOT A CHECKBOX FIELD. A `type: "checkbox"` field is an ordinary answer in submittedData: no wording is captured, no consent snapshot or `SmsConsent` row is written, so it proves nothing to a carrier, an A2P review or a TCPA dispute. The Legal & Consent fields are the only consent evidence — `collectSmsConsent` with `smsTransactionalConsentText` and `smsMarketingConsentText`, `showMarketingConsent` with `marketingConsentText`, and `termsAndConditionsText` (below). A checkbox whose label reads as SMS consent is REFUSED at write time, naming the field to use instead; on updateForm only a field you ADD is refused, one the form already had is carried forward. A DROPDOWN OR MULTISELECT OPTION worded as consent records just as little and is NOT refused, so never collect consent that way. A NEW CALENDAR FORM CAN BE BUILT AND PUBLISHED ENTIRELY THROUGH THIS API — never say routing has to be set up in the app: author the fields, set `assignmentConfig`, then updateForm(status: ACTIVE). Activating a CALENDAR form is rejected with "Please add an agent to route form submissions to." when the effective pool is empty, or "Pick a schedule for every assignee on a calendar form." when an assignee has no calendarConfig — both fixable in the publishing call. The gate is CALENDAR-ONLY: a form with no calendar field publishes with an empty pool, it just routes nobody. Some organizations also enforce a connected-mailbox launch gate on the first DRAFT/INACTIVE-to-ACTIVE transition: every assignee must have the form's pinned GOOGLE or MICROSOFT provider connected (either, when none is pinned); if it rejects, connect the named account in the app and retry. Assignees whose calendarConfig.isFixed is true are excluded from rotation and always attend; if every assignee is fixed there is no rotation, and the first assignee is the host.  Dedupe (dedupePrimaryField, with dedupeSecondaryField as fallback) only takes effect when allowDuplicateContact is false; it defaults to true, meaning every submission creates a new contact. Optional submitButtonLabel sets the submit button text; optional styleConfig sets the visual styling (see updateForm for the full key vocabulary). New forms start in DRAFT - publish with updateForm(status: ACTIVE). assignmentConfig is the LEAD ROUTING pool. `assignees` is an ordered list — ARRAY ORDER IS THE ROTATION ORDER among NON-FIXED assignees (`isFixed` ones always attend): one hosts every booking, two or more is least-recently-booked round-robin. Each is { userId } (from listTeammates, same-org), plus, on a CALENDAR form, a required calendarConfig: { isFixed, checkExternalCalendars } — a calendar form REJECTS an assignee without one; a non-calendar form does not reject one that carries it (stored, unused). `teamIds` are UserGroup ids added to every created/matched contact; `participantUserIds` are users attached as PARTICIPANT on it. DESIRED-STATE, REPLACED WHOLE: omit the key and the stored pool is untouched; pass it and the three lists BECOME the pool, so read with getForm, merge, and send the merged object back rather than one list alone. All three keys are required when you send it — pass [] for the ones you do not want, no duplicates. The response echoes the stored pool with names; confirm from that. The EFFECTIVE pool is the one you send, else the stored one, so an already-routed form reactivates without resending it (the calendar publish gate reads the effective pool). SMS/marketing consent, which is the A2P opt-in EVIDENCE surface: `collectSmsConsent` renders the transactional opt-in checkbox, labelled `smsTransactionalConsentText`, and `smsDisclaimerText` is the paragraph BELOW both boxes, which nobody ticks. SEND THE TEXT WITH THE TOGGLE: the snapshot resolves the SAME defaults the renderer resolves, so an OMITTED or null label records the built-in copy, but that copy is generic. NEVER send an empty string for a consent label: `""` (unlike null) renders a checkbox with no wording and files that empty string as the evidence — omit it or send null. Turning on `collectSmsConsent` ALONE also renders a marketing checkbox, worded and recorded from `smsMarketingConsentText` (or a default), so set that deliberately. `showMarketingConsent` is the separate standalone SMS marketing checkbox. Enabling it requires BOTH `showMarketingConsent: true` and non-empty `marketingConsentText` that explicitly describes SMS/text messages, plus a field with `type: "phone"` and `mapping: "phone"`; submissions are recorded as `SmsConsent`. Never use this pair for email authorization — standalone email consent is not supported. On update, resend the toggle and its SMS wording together. With no `marketingConsentText` it does not render at all, though the toggle reads as on; an omitted key, not null, records a box never offered. Transactional and marketing consent are DISTINCT — collecting one is not collecting the other. `triggerAgentIds` wires AI employees to the form: DESIRED-STATE, so the ids you send BECOME the complete set (send [] to detach all), and every submission puts them on the created or matched contact — read the current set from getForm and merge rather than sending one id alone. Legal text: `termsAndConditionsText` sits under the submit button, `privacyPolicyUrl`/`termsOfServiceUrl` link out, and `privacyPolicyContent`/`termsOfServiceContent` hold inline copy instead of a link. `slackMessageTemplate` is the {{token}} body for the Slack notification. The Powered by Goliath footer is NOT settable here (a Scale entitlement). `gtmContainerId` is a Google Tag Manager container, validated as GTM-XXXX and honoured on the hosted page only, not on an embed. `source` is the lead-source label stored on the form; getForm returns it and ownerType alongside. Notification DESTINATIONS: `enableEmailNotification`, `enableSmsNotification` and `enableSlackNotification`; the Slack one (and `slackMessageTemplate`) needs `slackChannelId` (plus `slackChannelName` for display). A channel or template without its toggle changes nothing a person will see, so send the toggle with them. getForm READS BACK everything in this paragraph, to verify a write or read the current copy before changing one field. The optional slug IS settable here, and this is the only operation in this API that takes it (updateForm does not thread it - a later rename is an app action): it is the last path segment of the form's public URL, must be 1-128 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens and may not start or end with a hyphen, and must be unique within your organization - a taken slug is rejected with "This slug is already taken", it is never silently suffixed. Omit it and one is generated from the name.
- `createFormContactLink` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A link to an ACTIVE form for one contact, opening prefilled with their details; their answers land on their contact. url for an email's link, shortUrl for a text.
- `deleteForm` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — HARD-DELETE a lead-capture form by id. IRREVERSIBLE and CASCADING - this also permanently removes ALL of the form's submissions, events, and viewer/lead history. To turn a form off without losing data, use updateForm(status: INACTIVE) instead. Returns true on success.
- `duplicateForm` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Copy a form: its fields, steps and settings, never its submissions or analytics. name defaults to "<name> copy". Returns the new form.
- `getForm` (query, READ) — Fetch one lead-capture form by id - full configuration including fieldConfig (the page-and-field document: either a flat array of fields for a single-page form, or a { fields, steps, showStepProgress } envelope for a multi-page one - see createForm), styleConfig (the JSON object of visual styling - colors, typography, spacing, border radius, button/input styling, custom CSS; null = default styling; see updateForm for the key vocabulary), submitButtonLabel, auto-apply tags/lists, dedupe settings, notification toggles, and the assignee pool. Use fieldConfig to interpret the submittedData keys returned by listFormSubmissions; read fieldConfig before editing fields or pages, and styleConfig before restyling, so an updateForm write merges instead of clobbering.
- `getFormActiveTime` (query, READ) [rate-limited] — Daily active-engagement time on one form over a date range - per day: session count and active-millisecond percentiles (p50/p90), split by submitted vs abandoned sessions. startDate and endDate are ISO YYYY-MM-DD; ranges longer than 90 days are rejected.
- `getFormAnalytics` (query, READ) [rate-limited] — Conversion funnel for one form over a date range - views, starts, submits, the start/submit/submit-of-started rates (0-1 fractions), median seconds-to-submit, plus a per-day time series. startDate and endDate are ISO YYYY-MM-DD; ranges longer than 90 days are rejected.
- `getFormRoutingDistribution` (query, READ) — Lead-assignment distribution for one form's round-robin pool - the number of leads routed to each assigned user. userId maps to a teammate from listTeammates.
- `getFormSubmission` (query, READ) — Fetch one form submission (lead) by id - its submitted field values (submittedData) and the linked CRM contactId.
- `getFormTrafficSources` (query, READ) [rate-limited] — Where a form's traffic and submissions come from - breakdowns by traffic source, device class, and location, each with views, submits, and the submit rate.
- `listFormActivity` (query, READ) [max limit 50; rate-limited] — Recent per-session activity for one form, newest first, cursor-paginated via after. Each row is a viewer session with its status, submit/abandon timestamps, traffic source, device, seconds-to-submit, the matched contact name, and the assigned point-person. Pass excludeViewOnly: true to drop sessions that never started filling.
- `listFormActivityLocations` (query, READ) [max limit 500; rate-limited] — Approximate geo coordinates of recent sessions for one form, for plotting a lead map. Latitude/longitude are rounded to ~1km. Each point carries its session status and the linked submission id (if any).
- `listForms` (query, READ) — The org's lead-capture forms (embed forms): name, slug, status (DRAFT | ACTIVE | INACTIVE), lifetime submissions, public URL, folderId. The id feeds getForm, listFormSubmissions and getFormAnalytics.
- `listFormSubmissions` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — List form submissions (leads), newest first, optionally filtered to one form via formId. Each row carries the submitted field values (submittedData) and the contactId of the CRM contact it created or matched - use that contactId with getContact, updateContact, or addContactNote. Returns a capped page plus the unpaged totalCount.
- `updateForm` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update a lead-capture form by id. Patch semantics - omitted fields are left unchanged; passing fieldConfig replaces the ENTIRE document, fields AND steps, so adding, renaming, reordering, or removing a page is a fieldConfig write: read the current document with getForm, edit it, and send the whole thing back (same shape rules as createForm - a malformed entry or unrecognized mapping is rejected, not silently dropped). fieldConfig is the form's ENTIRE page-and-field document, in one of two shapes. (a) SINGLE PAGE: a flat array of field objects. (b) MULTI-STEP (pages / steps): { "fields": [ ...the same fields, each with a "stepId" ], "steps": [ { "id": "page-1", "name": "Your details", "title": "...", "subtitle": "...", "ctaLabel": "Continue" } ], "showStepProgress": true }. Multi-page forms ARE supported. Steps are pages in array order, with a "Step N of M" progress indicator unless "showStepProgress" is false. Step "id" is unique; "name" labels the step in the FORM BUILDER only. Visitors see "title"/"subtitle" and "ctaLabel" (button text); a "ctaLabel" on the LAST step BEATS submitButtonLabel. In a ONE-step envelope they render nothing (use headerText / descriptionText / submitButtonLabel). An unknown stepId is REJECTED, as is any "stepId" in shape (a): steps require the envelope. No "stepId" = first page; keep "order" unique and ascending. BRANCHING: a step's "routes" run in order, each { "match": "all" | "any", "conditions": [ { "fieldKey", "anyOf": [option labels; "true"/"false" for a checkbox] } ], "goTo": a LATER step id | "submit" }; "otherwise" (same values) covers the rest (default: next step). Conditions test dropdown/multiselect/checkbox fields on that step or earlier; a bad destination, or a step "id" of "submit", is REJECTED. A skipped step's required fields are not required. "endings": [ { "id", "name", "title", "subtitle", "icon" (check|calendar|mail|heart|star|info|none), "iconColor" (#rrggbb), "workflowGroupIds", "agentIds", "tagIds", "listIds" } ]; "goTo"/"otherwise" "end:<id>" ends there, adding its ids to the form's actions ("submitted" is reserved). "createsLead": true on one step before the last creates the lead when it is done; later answers join that contact. "collectsConsent": true shows consent and terms on that step only (default: the lead step, else the last).Each field object is { fieldKey, label, type, required, order, width, mapping, dropdownOptions?, placeholder?, stepId? } plus the optional keys below. `type` is one of text|email|phone|number|dollar|dropdown|multiselect|textarea|checkbox|address|calendar; `width` is full|half|third. `mapping` is one of firstName|lastName|fullName|email|phone|address|note|none|customField:<id> — fullName is ONE box for the whole name. LENGTH LIMITS, refused at write time (never truncated) with a message naming the field: `fieldKey` at 200 characters, every `dropdownOptions` entry (and the `formOptionLabel` copied from it) at 256. FIELD KEYS beyond the common ones — the list above is NOT the whole vocabulary. `hideLabel` hides the label visually while leaving it for screen readers. `validation` takes { minLength, maxLength, pattern, customErrorMessage } and, for an address field, { addressMode: "single" | "split", requireStreet, requireCity, requireState, requireZipCode, requireCountry }. `customFieldOptionMappings` is [{ formOptionLabel, customFieldOptionId }] and maps the option labels of a dropdown OR multiselect field onto an EXISTING custom field's options instead of minting new ones. Every label (a multiselect answer is split per label) resolves through this table, and an unmapped label is SILENTLY SKIPPED — the submission succeeds and that CRM field stays empty. So map every option. `calendarConfig` configures a calendar field: { slotDurationMinutes: [..], defaultDurationMinutes, bufferBeforeMinutes, bufferAfterMinutes, maxAdvanceDays, minNoticeHours, appointmentTitleTemplate, defaultLocation?, locationType?: "VIDEO_CALL" | "CUSTOM" | "PHONE_CALL", meetingId?, meetingPasscode?, calendarProvider?: "GOOGLE" | "MICROSOFT", requireCardToConfirm? }. `locationType: "VIDEO_CALL"` makes the join link minted on the host’s calendar (Google Meet, or Teams when calendarProvider is MICROSOFT) the location; "CUSTOM" (the default) shows `defaultLocation` — an address or a pasted Zoom link. A CUSTOM `defaultLocation` that is a Zoom, Teams or Webex URL is the booking’s ONLY join point: no Meet / Teams link is minted, and reminders, webhooks and the host notification use it. `meetingId` and `meetingPasscode` go in the invite; the fallback confirmation carries only the link. The public form hides both but shows the link, so a `?pwd=` link is public. "PHONE_CALL" mints no link and the host calls the number the booker entered, so the form must have a REQUIRED `type: "phone"` field mapped to `phone`, or the write is refused. A calendar field with NO calendarConfig renders no picker at all, and nothing errors, so always send it. CONSENT IS NOT A CHECKBOX FIELD. A `type: "checkbox"` field is an ordinary answer in submittedData: no wording is captured, no consent snapshot or `SmsConsent` row is written, so it proves nothing to a carrier, an A2P review or a TCPA dispute. The Legal & Consent fields are the only consent evidence — `collectSmsConsent` with `smsTransactionalConsentText` and `smsMarketingConsentText`, `showMarketingConsent` with `marketingConsentText`, and `termsAndConditionsText` (below). A checkbox whose label reads as SMS consent is REFUSED at write time, naming the field to use instead; on updateForm only a field you ADD is refused, one the form already had is carried forward. A DROPDOWN OR MULTISELECT OPTION worded as consent records just as little and is NOT refused, so never collect consent that way. A NEW CALENDAR FORM CAN BE BUILT AND PUBLISHED ENTIRELY THROUGH THIS API — never say routing has to be set up in the app: author the fields, set `assignmentConfig`, then updateForm(status: ACTIVE). Activating a CALENDAR form is rejected with "Please add an agent to route form submissions to." when the effective pool is empty, or "Pick a schedule for every assignee on a calendar form." when an assignee has no calendarConfig — both fixable in the publishing call. The gate is CALENDAR-ONLY: a form with no calendar field publishes with an empty pool, it just routes nobody. Some organizations also enforce a connected-mailbox launch gate on the first DRAFT/INACTIVE-to-ACTIVE transition: every assignee must have the form's pinned GOOGLE or MICROSOFT provider connected (either, when none is pinned); if it rejects, connect the named account in the app and retry. Assignees whose calendarConfig.isFixed is true are excluded from rotation and always attend; if every assignee is fixed there is no rotation, and the first assignee is the host.  The mutation returns the stored fieldConfig, so you can verify the pages landed without a second getForm. Activate or deactivate with status (ACTIVE | INACTIVE); prefer status: INACTIVE over deleteForm to turn a form off without losing its submissions. submitButtonLabel sets the submit button text. styleConfig restyles the rendered form (both the hosted page and the iframe embed): a JSON object replaced whole on each write - read the current value with getForm, merge your changes, and send the merged object back; {} resets everything to defaults. All keys optional. Colors are CSS color strings: primaryColor (buttons/accents), backgroundColor, textColor, errorColor, successColor, inputBackgroundColor, inputBorderColor, inputPlaceholderColor, inputFocusColor (focus ring), buttonTextColor, requiredIndicatorColor, dividerColor, formBorderColor. fontFamily is a font name (e.g. "Georgia"). Pixel numbers (JSON numbers, no units): borderRadius (inputs+buttons corner rounding), spacing (gap between fields), inputBorderWidth, inputFocusRingWidth, labelGap, buttonTopMargin, formMaxWidth, formPadding, formBorderWidth. Enums: layout (vertical | horizontal - responsive field layout), inputHeight / labelSize / buttonSize (small | medium | large), labelWeight / buttonFontWeight (normal | medium | semibold | bold), labelPosition (above | inline | floating), buttonStyle (filled | outlined | rounded), buttonWidth (auto | full), buttonTextTransform (none | uppercase | capitalize), buttonHoverEffect (darken | lighten | none), formShadow (none | sm | md | lg). Booleans: formBorder, showDividers. customCss is NOT free-form CSS: only the rules the form builder Customize-CSS tab can author; anything else is REJECTED naming the offending selector or property. The twelve allowed selectors, with the properties permitted under each: `.embed-root` (padding, max-width, align-items); `.embed-form .form-container` (background, padding, border-radius, max-width, box-shadow); `.embed-form .form-label` (color, font-size, font-weight, margin-bottom); `.embed-form .form-input` (background, border, border-radius, padding, font-size, color); `.embed-form .form-submit` (background, color, border-radius, padding, font-size, font-weight); `.embed-form .form-error` (color, font-size, margin-top); `.embed-form .form-field` (margin-bottom, gap); and, for a form with a calendar field, `.embed-form .cal-day--available` (background, color, border-radius), `.embed-form .cal-day--selected` (background, color), `.embed-form .cal-slot-btn` (border-color, color, border-radius, background), `.embed-form .cal-slot-btn--selected` (background, color, border-color) and `.embed-form .cal-summary-card` (background, border, border-radius, padding). No other selector, pseudo-element or property. Prefer the typed keys above. Unknown or mistyped keys elsewhere in styleConfig are silently ignored at render time (the default applies), so stay within this vocabulary. The slug (the last segment of the public URL) is settable at CREATION - createForm takes an optional slug - but THIS operation does not thread it, so it cannot be changed here. It is NOT immutable: the app's form builder renames it, and a rename changes the public URL for good (old links stop resolving), so "change my form URL" is an app hand-off, not an impossibility. assignmentConfig is the LEAD ROUTING pool. `assignees` is an ordered list — ARRAY ORDER IS THE ROTATION ORDER among NON-FIXED assignees (`isFixed` ones always attend): one hosts every booking, two or more is least-recently-booked round-robin. Each is { userId } (from listTeammates, same-org), plus, on a CALENDAR form, a required calendarConfig: { isFixed, checkExternalCalendars } — a calendar form REJECTS an assignee without one; a non-calendar form does not reject one that carries it (stored, unused). `teamIds` are UserGroup ids added to every created/matched contact; `participantUserIds` are users attached as PARTICIPANT on it. DESIRED-STATE, REPLACED WHOLE: omit the key and the stored pool is untouched; pass it and the three lists BECOME the pool, so read with getForm, merge, and send the merged object back rather than one list alone. All three keys are required when you send it — pass [] for the ones you do not want, no duplicates. The response echoes the stored pool with names; confirm from that. The EFFECTIVE pool is the one you send, else the stored one, so an already-routed form reactivates without resending it (the calendar publish gate reads the effective pool). SMS/marketing consent, which is the A2P opt-in EVIDENCE surface: `collectSmsConsent` renders the transactional opt-in checkbox, labelled `smsTransactionalConsentText`, and `smsDisclaimerText` is the paragraph BELOW both boxes, which nobody ticks. SEND THE TEXT WITH THE TOGGLE: the snapshot resolves the SAME defaults the renderer resolves, so an OMITTED or null label records the built-in copy, but that copy is generic. NEVER send an empty string for a consent label: `""` (unlike null) renders a checkbox with no wording and files that empty string as the evidence — omit it or send null. Turning on `collectSmsConsent` ALONE also renders a marketing checkbox, worded and recorded from `smsMarketingConsentText` (or a default), so set that deliberately. `showMarketingConsent` is the separate standalone SMS marketing checkbox. Enabling it requires BOTH `showMarketingConsent: true` and non-empty `marketingConsentText` that explicitly describes SMS/text messages, plus a field with `type: "phone"` and `mapping: "phone"`; submissions are recorded as `SmsConsent`. Never use this pair for email authorization — standalone email consent is not supported. On update, resend the toggle and its SMS wording together. With no `marketingConsentText` it does not render at all, though the toggle reads as on; an omitted key, not null, records a box never offered. Transactional and marketing consent are DISTINCT — collecting one is not collecting the other. `triggerAgentIds` wires AI employees to the form: DESIRED-STATE, so the ids you send BECOME the complete set (send [] to detach all), and every submission puts them on the created or matched contact — read the current set from getForm and merge rather than sending one id alone. Legal text: `termsAndConditionsText` sits under the submit button, `privacyPolicyUrl`/`termsOfServiceUrl` link out, and `privacyPolicyContent`/`termsOfServiceContent` hold inline copy instead of a link. `slackMessageTemplate` is the {{token}} body for the Slack notification. The Powered by Goliath footer is NOT settable here (a Scale entitlement). `gtmContainerId` is a Google Tag Manager container, validated as GTM-XXXX and honoured on the hosted page only, not on an embed. `source` is the lead-source label stored on the form; getForm returns it and ownerType alongside. Notification DESTINATIONS: `enableEmailNotification`, `enableSmsNotification` and `enableSlackNotification`; the Slack one (and `slackMessageTemplate`) needs `slackChannelId` (plus `slackChannelName` for display). A channel or template without its toggle changes nothing a person will see, so send the toggle with them. getForm READS BACK everything in this paragraph, to verify a write or read the current copy before changing one field.

## libraryFileRuns

- `confirmLibraryFileRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Run it: the step the Files review's confirm runs. A skip trace spends credits and adds the phones and emails to the file as a new version; a tag puts the properties on tagName's list. skipTrace is true for a SKIPTRACE run and false for TAG_PROPERTIES. Only after the person said yes to this run. It starts in the background and returns at once.
- `mapLibraryFileRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Map a run's columns with the import mapper (up to a few minutes). skipTrace is true for a SKIPTRACE run and false for TAG_PROPERTIES. Returns totalRows and the columns with example values (csvSample). Nothing runs.
- `previewLibraryFileRun` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — The first rows of a mapped run as it reads them: for a skip trace each row's lookups (inputs: whose owner, at which address), for a tag the properties. The row count is how many rows it reads. A skip trace costs up to one credit per lookup: rows times the lookups per row. skipTrace is true for a SKIPTRACE run and false for TAG_PROPERTIES. limit is 1 to 10. Read only.
- `reviseLibraryFileRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change how a run maps the spreadsheet's columns, in the person's words (message), then read previewLibraryFileRun again. skipTrace is true for a SKIPTRACE run and false for TAG_PROPERTIES. Nothing runs.
- `startLibraryFileRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Start a run on a Library file (a .csv, .xlsx or .xls spreadsheet; spaceItemId from the chat trailer or searchSpaceItems): a skip trace finds owner phones and emails, a tag puts its properties on a list (a contact import is startContactImport). skipTrace is true for a SKIPTRACE run and false for TAG_PROPERTIES. Returns the run (fileProcessingTaskId); it shows on the file in Files. Nothing runs yet: map it next (mapLibraryFileRun). A retry in this chat returns the run it already started.

## memory

- `addMemoryEntries` (mutation, IMPORT) [idempotent] — Add conversation records from another system to your memory, idempotent on `externalId`. Your people's words (FROM_ACCOUNT) are learned from; the other side's are context. Hidden records, typed notes and calendar emails are refused.

## notifications

- `clearOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — "Dealt with": the row leaves the key owner's Today until something newer than anchorAt happens to it. subjectGrn is `<Model>_<id>` of what the row is about (TextConversation, EmailThread, Deal, Call, Task); kind is TODAY.
- `decideCatchUpCard` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Decide one HARVEST or BUNDLE card (`family`; the others are answered through their own operations) as the decision bar does, on the person's word: `verb` ACCEPT or DISMISS, `shownIds` every row the card showed (listCatchUpCards), `suggestionIds` the ticked ones (ACCEPT sets the unticked aside; DISMISS dismisses them), `reason` for a DISMISS. An ACCEPT runs each row's action (a record change, a merge, a skip trace that spends credits and is queued as `bulkTaskId`, or a send). Behind the send consent attestation and Pause everything. `remainingIds` are rows still on the card.
- `deleteNotifications` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete notifications from your feed for good, by id (listNotifications). Only your own; another user's id is skipped. Returns how many were deleted. To clear the badge, mark them read instead.
- `getAvailableNotificationTypes` (query, READ) — The catalog of notification types you can filter by — each with its notificationType (the exact string to pass as notificationTypeFilter on listNotifications / getNotificationCounts), a human description, and a category. Call this first to filter reliably: notificationTypeFilter is a free string, so a typo silently returns an empty feed rather than an error.
- `getNotificationCounts` (query, READ) — Unread and read counts for your own notification feed (the badge numbers). Optional notificationTypeFilter narrows to one type — use an EXACT value from getAvailableNotificationTypes (an unrecognized string returns 0/0, not an error). Cheap poll for "do I have anything new" before calling listNotifications.
- `hideOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — "Don't show this again" on the key owner's Today, until unhideOnToday. subjectGrn is `<Model>_<id>` of what the row is about (TextConversation, EmailThread, Deal, Call, Task); kind is TODAY.
- `hideTaskSourceOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Hide from the key owner's Today every task one workflow (`WorkflowGroup_<id>`) or AI employee (`Agent_<id>`) made. The tasks stay in the task list.
- `listCatchUpCards` (query, READ) [max limit 200] — The key owner's Catch up deck, ranked as the app deals it: each card's id, kind, the sentence it asks (`ask`, else `title`), its rows (`bundleRows`, each `defaultChecked`) and `suggestionIds`. `nextCursor` continues the same ranking. What decideCatchUpCard takes.
- `listNotifications` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — List your in-app notifications (the bell feed), newest first. Optional filters: notificationTypeFilter (one notification type — use an EXACT value from getAvailableNotificationTypes; an unrecognized string is not an error, it just returns an empty feed with total 0), seen (true = only read, false = only unread, omitted = both), and searchTerm. Cursor-paginated — pass the returned canFetchNext as a signal there is another page and re-call with cursor set to the last notification's id (limit defaults to 25, capped at 50). total is the full match count and hasUnread flags any unread in the feed, so nothing is silently truncated. Reads ONLY your own notifications — true for EVERY key including an admin's, because this operation exposes no recipient selector at all. The app does have the admin/Goliath-staff teammate feed (one or more teammates' notifications combined), so if the user asks to see a colleague's bell, point them at the app instead of saying nobody can see it. Each row carries the related-record ids (contactId, dealId, noteId, replyId, taskId, callId) and actionType/actionTargetId for deep-linking.
- `markAllNotificationsRead` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark your WHOLE notification feed read (`isSeen: true`) or unread (false). `userId` must be your own (getMyProfile `currentUser.id`); any other is refused. Optional `notificationTypeFilter` (exact getAvailableNotificationTypes value) narrows it; `notIncludedNotificationIds` are left alone. Returns how many changed. Never a teammate's feed.
- `markContactNotificationsRead` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark every one of your notifications about one contact read. Returns how many changed.
- `markNotificationsRead` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark specific notifications read or unread by id. Pass isSeen: true to mark read (clears them from the unread badge) or false to mark unread. notificationIds come from listNotifications. Only your own notifications are affected — a notification id belonging to another user is a silent no-op, never an error. Returns the updated {id, seen} for each row that changed.
- `markWrongOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — "This is wrong": a hide with the person's reason and an optional note (at most 280 characters). subjectGrn is `<Model>_<id>` of what the row is about (TextConversation, EmailThread, Deal, Call, Task); kind is TODAY.
- `setEmailDigestCadence` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — When your notification emails go out: AS_IT_HAPPENS (one email a few minutes after a notification) or DAILY (one email each morning at 8am in your timezone; AI hand-offs and workflow pages still arrive right away). Yours only.
- `skipOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — "Not now": the row leaves the key owner's Today until their next local day, or sooner when something newer happens (anchorAt: when the row's event happened). subjectGrn is `<Model>_<id>` of what the row is about (TextConversation, EmailThread, Deal, Call, Task); kind is TODAY.
- `undoCatchUpDecision` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take back a decideCatchUpCard: the same cardId and verb, `suggestionIds` the rows it decided (its ticked rows less `remainingIds`), and for an ACCEPT `setAsideIds` its unticked `shownIds` (only rows it set aside come back). Dismissals and set-asides come back; an applied row (a merge, a spend, a send) stands and is counted in `refused`. Card decisions only: trust and memory moves are the person's, in the app.
- `unhideOnToday` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Show a row again: undoes a skip, hide or "this is wrong". subjectGrn is `<Model>_<id>` of what the row is about (TextConversation, EmailThread, Deal, Call, Task); kind is TODAY. To undo hideTaskSourceOnToday instead, send that source's GRN with kind TODAY_TASKS.

## partnerships

- `acceptPartnershipInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Accept a pending partnership invitation from another organization (partnerOrgId from listPendingPartnershipInvites). permittedUserIds optionally limits which of your users are visible to the partner (empty = all). Only applies to invitations the partner initiated. Moves the partnership to ACTIVE.
- `cancelPartnershipInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Cancel a pending partnership invitation your organization initiated (partnerOrgId from listPartnerships, status PENDING), before the partner has accepted it.
- `canShareWithPartners` (query, READ) — True when your organization has at least one ACTIVE partnership in a sending direction (SEND_ONLY or BIDIRECTIONAL from your side) — i.e. there is a partner your organization could share leads with. False means sharing a contact with a partner is not possible until an invitation is sent and accepted; check this before promising a user that a lead can be handed to a partner.
- `createPartnershipInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Send a partnership invitation to another organization (partnerOrgId from lookupPartnerOrg). direction is SEND_ONLY, RECEIVE_ONLY, or BIDIRECTIONAL (whose leads flow to whom). permittedUserIds optionally limits which of your users are visible to the partner (empty = all); recipientUserIds optionally targets which partner admins are notified — omit it (the default) to notify all of them; no operation lists partner admins, so choosing them is done in the app. Confirm the partner, direction and permittedUserIds with the user first. The partnership is PENDING until the partner org accepts — track it in listPartnerships.
- `listPartnerships` (query, READ) — List every partnership your organization has with another organization — ACTIVE, PENDING and TERMINATED — always viewed from your side: partnerOrg is the OTHER organization, and its id is the partnerOrgId every partnership mutation takes (terminatePartnership, updatePartnershipPermittedUsers, cancelPartnershipInvite). direction says whose leads flow to whom (SEND_ONLY: yours to theirs; RECEIVE_ONLY: theirs to yours; BIDIRECTIONAL). awaitingCurrentOrgResponse is true when the partner invited you and you have not answered — those are the rows listPendingPartnershipInvites returns. permittedUserIds are YOUR users the partner may see when sending leads (empty = all). This is the answer to "who are we partnered with?".
- `listPendingPartnershipInvites` (query, READ) — List the partnership invitations OTHER organizations have sent you that are still waiting on your answer (awaitingCurrentOrgResponse is always true here). Each row's partnerOrg.id is the partnerOrgId to pass to acceptPartnershipInvite or rejectPartnershipInvite. Invitations YOUR organization sent and is waiting on are not here — they appear in listPartnerships with status PENDING and awaitingCurrentOrgResponse false.
- `lookupPartnerOrg` (query, ADMIN) — Resolve a prospective partner organization by exactly one of an admin's phone number or email. Returns the matched admin and their organization — use the organization id as partnerOrgId when sending a partnership invitation. For an organization you are ALREADY partnered with, listPartnerships has the id without a lookup.
- `rejectPartnershipInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Reject a pending partnership invitation the other organization sent you (partnerOrgId from listPendingPartnershipInvites). Terminates the pending rows.
- `terminatePartnership` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — End an active partnership (partnerOrgId from listPartnerships); either party may. Stops all cross-org lead sharing with them. Confirm with the user first, naming the partner.
- `updatePartnershipPermittedUsers` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Update which of your organization's users are visible to a partner when they send leads (partnerOrgId). Pass the full permittedUserIds list; an empty array means all users are visible.

## phoneNumbers

- `addNumbersToDialingPool` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put numbers the org already owns (listCommunicationChannels) into the dialer's rotation. A teammate's line is allowed; an AI employee's is refused. Admins only.
- `buyDialingPoolNumbers` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Buy phone numbers straight into the bulk-dialing rotation: each is a RECURRING monthly charge.
