Either `count` (with an optional preferred `areaCode`; the provider picks) or `phoneNumbers` (E.164s from searchAvailablePhoneNumbers; a number taken meanwhile is a shortfall, never swapped). A number past the plan's included numbers adds $5/mo and is refused unless `confirmExtraPhoneNumberCharge` is true, sent only once the person agreed to that charge. `purchaseAttemptKey`: mint ONE per intended purchase and resend it unchanged on every retry, so a lost response never buys twice. Returns addedLines and, when some failed, failure { failedCount, message, kind }. ADMIN: the key owner must currently be an org admin.
- `getDialingPool` (query, READ) — The org's bulk-dialing rotation: each line (id, number, label), its calls today against its daily limit and restUntil, and the day's room.
- `getMyDialingRoom` (query, READ) — Can the key owner start a call list now? null: they have no phone line to call from (an admin assigns them a number). Else linesInRotation and linesResting of the bulk-dialing numbers their calls can go out on; none in rotation, or all resting, means a call list cannot dial.
- `getPhoneLineRingPolicy` (query, READ) — One line's own ring policy (its override of the org default), in getPhoneRouting's shape; null when the line follows the default. `phoneLineId` from getPhoneRouting or listCommunicationChannels.
- `getPhoneRouting` (query, READ) — Who answers an inbound call or text: the call routing the Automations Map's Phone calls area shows, and who gets a new contact. `orgDefaultRingPolicy` is the default every line follows unless it has its own (null = none configured): `humanStage` is who rings first (`targetKind` LINE_OWNER the number's own user, SPECIFIC_USER one teammate, TEAM a team, ORG_USER_ROTATION a rotation of lines, EXTERNAL or AREA_CODE_MAP forwarding; a null humanStage means nobody rings and the AI pickup answers at once), for `ringSeconds`, only inside its `schedule` (null = always); `aiStage` is the AI employees that pick up a missed call, in `rotation` (no AI answers only when it is empty or every one has `canAnswerCalls` false). `defaultInboundIntakePolicy` is who gets a NEW contact created by inbound traffic. Each line lists its owner and `ringPolicyId` / `assignmentPolicyId` (null = follows the default); read a line's own policy with getPhoneLineRingPolicy. Change a ring policy with setOrgDefaultRingPolicy or setPhoneLineRingPolicy.
- `getVoiceTrustSummary` (query, READ) — One org-wide picture of caller-trust registration — the carrier registration that keeps outbound calls from showing as "Spam Likely". accountState is chosen by loudest call to action, not by progress (FAILED > REGISTERING > REGISTERED > SELF_MANAGED > NOT_ELIGIBLE), so one refused account reads FAILED even when another is done. The line counts split the org's numbers by registration (registered / registering / failed, summing to eligibleLineCount) and by carrier health (watch / atRisk). needsAttention is the only flag that means "a human must act now" — a refused account or a number carriers appear to be rejecting; failedLineCount alone does not raise it, because a single errored attempt is retried by the next sweep. Read-only: registration runs on its own schedule and there is nothing to submit through this API.
- `provisionPhoneNumber` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Buy a phone number from Twilio (a RECURRING monthly charge) and assign it to targetUserId. It shows at once in listCommunicationChannels, ready to send from. Confirm first: name the number, who gets it and the monthly charge. phoneNumber must be an E.164 number returned by searchAvailablePhoneNumbers (an unavailable number is rejected). targetUserId is normally the key owner (listCommunicationChannels.currentUser.id); a user outside your organization is rejected. A number past the phone numbers the plan includes adds $5/mo on top of the plan: it is refused (PHONE_NUMBER_ALLOWANCE_REFUSED) unless `confirmExtraPhoneNumberCharge` is true, which you send only once the person agreed to that extra charge. checkBillingAction tells you beforehand whether a number is included. ADMIN scope: the key owner must currently be an org admin. Idempotent — reuse an Idempotency-Key to make a retry safe.
- `removeNumbersFromDialingPool` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take numbers out of the rotation; they stay owned. Their warm-up restarts if they come back (addNumbersToDialingPool). Admins only.
- `restDialingPoolNumber` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Bench one rotation line for the standard rest window: it returns on its own at restUntil (say the date). Admins only.
- `searchAvailablePhoneNumbers` (query, READ) — Search Twilio for buyable phone numbers, optionally narrowed by areaCode (a 3-digit US area code). Returns candidate numbers (E.164 phoneNumber plus locality/region) to feed into provisionPhoneNumber. Call this first when the org has no line to send from (listCommunicationChannels returned an empty twilioPhoneNumbers).
- `setOrgDefaultRingPolicy` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace the org's default call routing (every line without its own): humanStage (targetKind, ringSeconds 5 to 60, its target, an optional schedule) then aiStage (AI employees whose calls are on, SINGLE or ROUND_ROBIN). It saves the WHOLE policy, so read it first with getPhoneRouting and send it back changed; an omitted schedule or area-code map keeps what is saved. policy null deletes the default. Say the new path in plain words; it changes who picks up the org's calls from the next call on.
- `setPhoneLineLabel` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Name a phone line ("Facebook campaign"), or label null to clear it. Admins only.
- `setPhoneLineRingPolicy` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace one line's own call routing, shaped as setOrgDefaultRingPolicy's (read it with getPhoneLineRingPolicy first). policy null deletes it and the line follows the org default. Say the new path in plain words.
- `setPhoneLineRunsOnMetaAds` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark a tracking number as one the org runs only on Meta ads (its calls are attributed there), or false to clear it. Admins only.
- `unrestDialingPoolNumber` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Return a benched line to the rotation now, whoever benched it. Admins only.

## properties

- `addPropertiesToList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add properties to one or more lists (list ids from searchPropertyTags). ASYNC bulk-task op — returns bulkTaskId before the change applies; poll getBulkTask. TWO selection forms, never combined (ids with a filter is rejected). EXPLICIT: `propertyIds` (esIds) with `totalCount` = how many. FILTER-BACKED: `filterId` (saved; must be visible to the key owner — a teammate's private filter is refused) OR `filterTree` (inline, saveFilter's DSL, parsed STRICTLY — an unknown fieldId rejects the call) with `selectAll: true` for EVERY match or `selectCount: N` for the first N in the runner's DEFAULT traversal order — NOT the `sort` you previewed with on filterProperties, which the bulk task does not take; for a sorted top-N, pass that sorted page's ids as `propertyIds` (one window, not both; neither is REFUSED). An inline filterTree has no saved areas: save one with inSavedAreas and pass its filterId. `excludeIds` applies to a filter-backed selection only (on the explicit form, leave the id out). `totalCount` is an EXECUTION CAP the task stops at. It is DERIVED server-side for explicit ids (their count) and for `selectCount: N` (N — exclusions are not subtracted, the runner drops them as it goes) — whatever you send is ignored there, and a negative value is rejected — and TRUSTED only for `selectAll: true`: pass the filter's `total` from filterProperties UNSUBTRACTED (never minus `excludeIds` — the runner handles exclusions). An understated select-all count silently turns it into a partial write, so round UP. Pass the same `includeIncompleteRecords` you used on filterProperties. A filter-backed selection can touch thousands of properties in one call: state the match count to the user and get a go-ahead BEFORE submitting one.
- `addPropertyTags` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add existing tag(s) (by tag id) to a property. Get tag ids from searchPropertyTags. Returns the property with its updated tag set.
- `cancelCoverageRequest` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Withdraw the org's request for one family in one county (countyFips): the request is deleted, and asking again starts a new one. Admins only. False when there was none.
- `countPropertySignals` (query, READ) — Count PUBLIC-RECORD SIGNAL EVENTS in an area, by type and publication-day window. Filings, not contacts: tagged leads are filterContacts. An event is one property's signal of one type on one day (three liens = three); standing conditions (ABSENTEE_OWNER…) are not events, and it is NOT filterProperties' `total`. AREA: a saved `filterId` OR an inline `filterTree` (saveFilter's PROPERTY DSL, strict: `conditions` and `groups`, never `children`): a county is `countyFilters` with its `fips` (searchCounties), a city `cityFilters` with its `id` (searchCities). `signalTypes` narrows (omit for all); `from` / `to` are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` days. Returns `totalEvents`, `propertyCount` (distinct properties with a counted event), `byType`, and `uncountedByType` / `uncountedPropertyCount`: properties with a type only from an open recorded filing or listing mark (no day, so no event), which filterProperties finds. Each row is what that type's `byType` misses (rows overlap); `uncountedPropertyCount` counts properties missed entirely. Never call a type absent while `uncountedByType` lists it. `includeIncompleteRecords: true` lifts the completeness gate. Spends nothing.
- `createFilterFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a saved-filter folder (returns id). `scope` is the filters' type (PROPERTY, CONTACT, DEAL); `personal: true` makes it private, else it and filters filed in it are shared; with `parentId` it takes the parent's visibility instead. Reuse a listFilterFolders row only if name, parentId and isPrivate all match.
- `createPropertyList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Get or create an org-wide PROPERTY list by exact name (synchronous). Returns `list { id, name }` and `created`: say you made one only when `created` is true, and use the returned `name` (a plain tag holding the name adds a number).
- `deleteFilter` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY delete a saved filter by id (any type): no archive, no undo. Ids from listPropertyFilters / listContactFilters / saveFilter; returns true when a row was deleted, and a foreign or unknown id is rejected. WHOSE FILTER IS IT: an org admin can delete a teammate's SHARED filter here, so check `userId` against getMyProfile (`currentUser.id`) first, name the owner (getTeammatesByIds), and never delete someone else's filter unasked. A merely wrong filter is fixed with updateFilter. A teammate's PRIVATE filter is refused outright.
- `deleteFilterFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a filter folder (listFilterFolders id); its contents move up a level.
- `deleteFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a folder by id (listFolders). Its subfolders, filters, lists and forms move up a level, never deleted. A shared folder goes for the whole team.
- `filterProperties` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Run a property filter and paginate the matches with limit/offset. Returns a page of properties plus total and hasMore. Pass EITHER filterId (a saved filter from listPropertyFilters) OR filterTree (the same filter-tree DSL saveFilter takes; conditions key `fieldId`, not `field`) to run an UNSAVED tree: same totals, nothing persisted. Use filterTree to verify a filter before saving it, and to see whether a condition keeps a record with no value for its field. NEVER save a filter in order to measure one — save only the final filter the user asked for. Sort with `sort: { field, direction }` (`ASC` / `DESC`). `field` is a CLOSED vocabulary: `spicy_lead_score`, `estimated_value_dollars`, `estimatedRent`, `last_property_signal_date` / `lastPropertySignalDate`, `closed_date` / `closedDate`, `unit_count` / `unitCount`, `latestListingStatusDate` / `z_latest_listing_status_date`, `fsboListedDate`, `frboListedDate`, `fsboListingRemovedDate`, `frboListingRemovedDate`, `listingRemovedDate`, `listingRemovedRentDate`, `listingRemovedSaleDate`, `auction_date` (earliest upcoming auction, properties with none last). Any other field is silently IGNORED (default order, no error), so never infer support from a call that worked. `includeIncompleteRecords: true` lifts the index's completeness gate: by default properties with no parcel identity and no signal (~39% of the index) are HIDDEN, the usual reason a known address is missing. It only widens. Pass the same flag to addPropertiesToList so the bulk selection matches the page shown.
- `findProperties` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Search properties by (partial) address. Returns address suggestions with the property id (esId) to use in getProperty.
- `findPropertiesByMlsId` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Search properties by (partial) MLS id. Returns address suggestions with the property id (esId) to use in getProperty.
- `findPropertiesByParcel` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Search properties by (partial) parcel id. Returns address suggestions with the property id (esId) to use in getProperty.
- `findPropertiesNearPoint` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — Properties within ~150 m of a point, the parcel it is on first: candidates, not one answer (match a house number).
- `getFilter` (query, READ) — Fetch ONE saved filter by id, including its full `root` criteria tree — the only operation that returns the tree (listPropertyFilters / listContactFilters / listDealFilters return metadata only). Works for contact, property and deal filters. Call this BEFORE updateFilter whenever you are changing PART of a filter: updateFilter replaces `root` wholesale, so without reading the current tree first you would be re-authoring it blind and would silently drop every condition you didn't know was there. Read it, modify the one condition you mean to change, and send the modified tree back. The tree is saveFilter's DSL. Tag and list conditions hold ids: name them via searchContactTags (searchPropertyTags for PROPERTY). `queryOptions` (PROPERTY only) holds execution options outside the tree — `{ includeIncompleteRecords: true }` runs the filter with the completeness gate OFF (~39% more of the index), which is why a count can exceed what the tree explains.
- `getProperty` (query, READ) — Fetch one property by id — address, skip-trace status, signal recency, owner of record and mailing address (`metadata`, as the page shows them), and visible `tags` and `lists` (each `{ id, name, isEditable }`). Lists include read-only system ingestion lists alongside your organization lists. Read `lists` BEFORE addPropertiesToList / removePropertiesFromList to answer "is it already on that list?"; only reuse a list ID for mutations when `isEditable` is true. Other organizations' private tags and lists are excluded.
- `getPropertyOwners` (query, READ) — A property's people. `crmContacts`: your own contacts at it (linked, or at its street and ZIP), with `relation` (OWNS or null = owner; FORMER_OWNER, MAILING and the rest are not) and the phones and emails already on them. `people`: owners and relatives from public records, with phones and emails generally only after a skip trace. A crmContacts phone means you already have a number. Reading never spends a credit.
- `getPropertySignals` (query, READ) — A property's filings (newest 50), notice text in `adBody`. OWNER_SEARCH / MAILING_ADDRESS: matched via the owner. `suppressedReason` set: not live.
- `getRelatedProperties` (query, READ) — Batch property attributes by id (esId): owner of record and mailing address, beds/baths/size, year built, last sale, value, occupancy, county, lat/long, years owned, `ownerPortfolioSize` (parcels the owner holds).
- `getZoningCodes` (query, READ) — List the zoning codes available for a location (by state + city id or county FIPS). Returns a plain list of zoning-code strings.
- `listFilterFieldNames` (query, READ) — The COMPLETE vocabulary of filterable fields for a domain (CONTACT, PROPERTY or DEAL): every fieldId saveFilter accepts, with label, category and UI component. It always arrives whole, unlike the fuller `listFilterFields`, which drops WHOLE FIELDS when unnarrowed, so it is the only trustworthy answer to "is X filterable here?". Find the fieldId here, then call `listFilterFields` with those `fieldIds` for descriptions and value shapes. A field absent from THIS list is genuinely not filterable; never tell a user a filter is impossible from a truncated `listFilterFields` response or a rejected fieldId guess. Static schema introspection: reads no org data.
- `listFilterFields` (query, READ) — The filterable-field catalog for a filter domain WITH full value shapes — how to WRITE a condition once you know which field you want (CONTACT, PROPERTY or DEAL; other FilterType values are rejected). Call this BEFORE authoring a saveFilter tree: never guess fieldIds. `fieldIds` is REQUIRED — name the fields you actually need. Unnarrowed, the catalog would be TRUNCATED BY DROPPING WHOLE FIELDS, so this operation is NEVER evidence that a field does not exist: to discover what exists, or before telling anyone a filter cannot express something, call `listFilterFieldNames`, which always arrives complete. An unknown requested fieldId errors naming it (it means that field does NOT exist; do not invent a value shape for it). Each row carries label/category/description, the UI component kind (the value-shape hint — e.g. numericRange, multiSelect, dateRange), acceptedValueKeys (for object-shaped values: the exact top-level keys, e.g. min/max), and static options for select-like fields. USE `valueShapes`, NOT `acceptedValueKeys`, WHENEVER A FIELD HAS MORE THAN ONE: some fields accept several mutually-exclusive value shapes, and acceptedValueKeys flattens them into one list that is NOT itself a valid value. `valueShapes` reports them arm by arm — each with the `discriminatorKey`/`discriminatorValue` literal that selects it, and only that arm’s keys, each marked required or optional with its `acceptedValues` when the key is an enum or literal. A shape carrying `scalar` instead of keys is a BARE value — `bedrooms` accepts `3` as well as `{min, max}` — so send the plain value for that arm, not an object. Pick ONE shape, send that arm’s discriminator literal verbatim, and send only its keys: `dateCustomFieldFilters`, for instance, has seven arms keyed on `comparison`; ON, BEFORE and AFTER take a strict YYYY-MM-DD `date`, MORE_THAN, LESS_THAN and WITHIN_NEXT take number+timeUnit (an interval), and BETWEEN takes from/to (absolute bounds). An unrecognized `comparison` literal fails the WHOLE save; keys borrowed from another arm are silently STRIPPED, so the filter saves without that constraint. Contact CUSTOM fields are NOT addressed by their custom-field UUID as a fieldId — use the wrapper fields this catalog lists (e.g. dropdownCustomFieldFilters / textCustomFieldFilters) whose VALUE carries the custom-field id. `countyFilters` takes a county `fips` (searchCounties), `cityFilters` a city `id` (searchCities). Static schema introspection: reads no org data and never changes with account state.
- `listFilterFolders` (query, READ) — Saved-filter folders of one `type` (PROPERTY, CONTACT, DEAL), empty ones included: the org's shared ones plus your private ones. A filter's `folderId` is one of these; file filters with updateFilter `folderId`.
- `listFolders` (query, READ) — Every folder on one surface (`scope`: PROPERTY, CONTACT, DEAL, FORM, …), flat: the org's shared tree plus your personal one. `ownerUserId` set = personal. `itemCount` counts items filed directly in it. Filter folders also come from listFilterFolders; workflow and template folders have their own ops.
- `listMyCoverageRequests` (query, READ) — The org's coverage requests: signal family and county (countyFips), when asked, status, expectedBy (the promise) and liveSince.
- `listPropertyFilters` (query, READ) — List the saved property filters VISIBLE to the key owner; run one by id with filterProperties (the tree stays server-side — getFilter reads it). Each row has `userId` (the OWNER), `folderId`, `createdAt` and `criteriaSummary` (its conditions in one line; getFilter for the whole tree). READ `userId` BEFORE ANY WRITE: the list is every SHARED filter in the org, whoever made it, plus your own private ones (`isPrivate: true`), and updateFilter / deleteFilter will write a TEAMMATE's for an org admin. Your id is getMyProfile `currentUser.id`; name a teammate's id with getTeammatesByIds. Say whose a filter is before changing or deleting it.
- `manualSkiptrace` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Skip-trace an explicitly-provided owner + mailing address (no property record needed). CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT (plan allowance first except in a trial, then real money; checkBillingAction) — requires the ADMIN scope, and the key owner must be a team admin.
- `moveFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put a folder under another folder of the same surface (`parentId`), or at the top level (`parentId: null`). Refused when it would cross between personal and shared, nest a folder inside itself, or go too deep.
- `moveItemsToFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — File items into a folder (`folderId`), or to the top level (`folderId: null`). `items` are `{ kind, id }`; kind is FILTER, CONTACT_LIST, PROPERTY_LIST, FORM, TEMPLATE, LIBRARY_FILE or WORKFLOW_GROUP. All or nothing: one id not found refuses the whole call. Refused when the folder's surface does not hold that kind. A saved filter's privacy FOLLOWS the folder: into a personal folder makes it private to you, into a shared one shares it with the team, so say so before moving a filter across. Returns how many moved.
- `removePropertiesFromList` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove properties from ONE list (`listId` from searchPropertyTags or getProperty's `lists`). ASYNC bulk-task op — poll getBulkTask(bulkTaskId). Same selection rules as addPropertiesToList: EXPLICIT `propertyIds` + `totalCount`, or FILTER-BACKED `filterId` / `filterTree` (strict) with `selectAll: true` or `selectCount: N` for the first N in DEFAULT traversal order, never a previewed `sort` — use `propertyIds` for a sorted top-N (one window, not both; neither is REFUSED), `excludeIds` on the filter-backed form only. `totalCount` is an EXECUTION CAP, derived server-side for explicit ids and `selectCount` and trusted only for select-all: the filter's `total` from filterProperties UNSUBTRACTED; understated means the removal stops early, so round up. Not on the list is skipped, not an error. Removes MEMBERSHIP only — list and properties survive. A filter-backed selection can touch thousands of properties in one call: state the match count to the user and get a go-ahead BEFORE submitting one.
- `removePropertyTag` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Remove one tag (by tag id) from a property. Returns the property with its updated tag set.
- `renameFilterFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a filter folder (listFilterFolders id); onto a sibling’s name it MERGES into it.
- `renameFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a folder by id (listFolders); a name a sibling already has is refused. For a saved-filter folder prefer renameFilterFolder, which merges into a same-named sibling as the app does.
- `reorderFilters` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the display order of saved filters: `filterIds` first to last (listPropertyFilters / listContactFilters / listDealFilters ids).
- `reorderFolderItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the display order of items inside one folder: `orderedItems` (`{ kind, id }`) first to last. TEMPLATE and FORM items are refused (they have no order). Returns how many were ordered.
- `reorderFolders` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the order of one set of sibling folders: `scope`, their `parentId` (null = top level), `personal` (which side), and `orderedIds` first to last. An id outside that set refuses the call; siblings you leave out keep their order after the listed ones. Returns the surface's folders.
- `requestCoverage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Ask for coverage of places ("Cook County, IL"; a county keys to its cell, anything else comes back in gaps) for signals by name (signals, always sent: [] when asking by family), or families picked outright (FORECLOSURE, PREFORECLOSURE, PROBATE, PREPROBATE, TAX_DELINQUENCY, CODE_VIOLATION). For those six, read listMyCoverageRequests first: one already asked is not asked again. Any other signal (liens, evictions) is recorded and reaches sales, but no read returns it: ask it once and give no date. Any member.
- `requestSignalsInMyCounties` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Ask for signal types that are not live yet in every county the org works, as a builder's "Request it" does; the 2-week promise starts now. context names what was being built (`workflowGroup:<id>`, `filter:<id>`).
- `runPropertyComparables` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Comparable sales for a property (its id from a property read), as the property page's Comps tab: each comp's facts, distance and price per square foot, and the medians with the subject's implied value. Optional criteria narrow it (every bound is required when sent). Spends nothing.
- `saveFilter` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a saved filter. `type` CONTACT runs with filterContacts, PROPERTY with filterProperties, DEAL (status, title, pipeline stage, assignees, deal custom fields) with filterDeals — find deal filters with listDealFilters; the Deals board shows no saved-filter list, so tell the user it lives in the API. Other FilterType values are rejected. `root` is the filter-tree DSL, a recursive group: { id, operator: "AND"|"OR", negated?: boolean, conditions: [{ id, fieldId, value }], groups: [<group>] }. `negated: true` inverts a whole GROUP (group-level only) — the way to say "not already on any of my lists". EVERY group and condition needs its own caller-minted non-empty `id` (mint a UUID each); missing ids are the most common rejection. Every `fieldId` must be a real field of the domain: an unknown one, or a bad value, rejects the whole save naming the field and saves nothing, so NEVER probe by saving — read listFilterFields FIRST. Geo conditions take ids: `countyFilters` a `fips` from searchCounties, `cityFilters` a city `id` from searchCities (a county name or unknown FIPS is rejected on any type, a bare city name on PROPERTY). To see what a tree DOES first — its count, whether it keeps records with no value — run it inline as `filterTree` on filterProperties/filterContacts/countContacts, which saves nothing. Save only the final filter the user asked for: a measuring filter is visible to them and their team. File it into a folder with `folderId` (listFilterFolders). Owner + org come from the API key; no userId/organizationId input, so a key cannot plant a filter in another tenant. The response may carry `warnings`: non-fatal notes on the saved criteria (e.g. same-named counties from DIFFERENT states, like Cook, IL + Cook, MN — saved, and it matches all of them). RELAY each one with the result, not as a failure; if the selection is not what the user meant, fix it with updateFilter.
- `searchCities` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — Find US cities by (partial) name and return each match's `id`, `name` and `state`. This is how you IDENTIFY a city: the `cityFilters` condition in a property filter tree takes the returned `id` as its `value` (with `label` set to "Name, ST", e.g. "Memphis, TN"), and saveFilter/updateFilter REJECT a bare city name on PROPERTY filters (CONTACT matches a name leniently) — a name alone is ambiguous across states (11,347 US city names occur in more than one state), so a filter built from one would match nothing. Disambiguate by including the state in the search term (e.g. "Memphis TN") when a name is common. The same `id` is also what getZoningCodes takes as `cityId`.
- `searchCounties` (query, READ) [max limit 10] — Find US counties by (partial) name and return each match's `name`, `fullName`, `state` and `fips`. The `countyFilters` condition in a property filter tree takes the 5-digit **`fips`** as its `value` (with `label` set to the display name) — a county DISPLAY NAME is rejected by saveFilter/updateFilter, because the query compiles to a `county_fips` term and a name would match nothing. Include the state in the search term (e.g. "Orange County FL") when a county name is common. The same `fips` is what getZoningCodes takes as `countyFips`.
- `searchPropertyTags` (query, READ) — Search your organization's property tags and lists by name. Use a tag id with addPropertyTags and a list id with addPropertiesToList.
- `skipTraceProperty` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Skip-trace a property (by id/esId) to discover its owner and their phone numbers/emails. Returns the discovered people inline; re-read them later (free) with getPropertyOwners. CONSUMES ONE SKIPTRACE CREDIT (plan allowance first except in a trial, then real money; checkBillingAction) — requires the ADMIN scope, and the key owner must be a team admin.
- `updateFilter` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Edit a saved filter IN PLACE by id (property, contact or deal) — its criteria, name, description, folder or visibility. Never saveFilter again under the same name: that makes a SECOND filter and leaves the wrong one. Ids come from listPropertyFilters / listContactFilters / listDealFilters or the saveFilter response. Every field but the id is optional and an OMITTED one is untouched, so a rename keeps criteria, folder and visibility. An explicit null differs: `folderId: null` takes the filter OUT of its folder (the only way to), while `description: null` is ignored (a description can be replaced, not cleared). `root` REPLACES the whole tree, never merges: to change PART of a filter, getFilter (the only op returning `root`), edit the one condition, and send the whole tree back — never author a replacement from the user's description alone, or you drop every condition you never saw. The tree is saveFilter's DSL (every node needs its own non-empty `id`), validated the same way: an unknown fieldId or invalid value rejects the WHOLE update naming the condition, nothing saved — so NEVER probe by updating; read listFilterFields first (pass `fieldIds` for just those). County/city values as on saveFilter (`fips` from searchCounties, city `id` from searchCities). The response echoes the persisted tree. `type` cannot change — delete and re-create. WHOSE FILTER IS IT: getFilter and the list ops return `userId`, the owner. A TEAMMATE's shared filter is writable here by an org admin with no confirmation and no history, so check `userId` against getMyProfile (`currentUser.id`) and, when it is not yours, say whose it is (getTeammatesByIds) before changing it. A teammate's PRIVATE filter is refused outright and never appears in the list ops. The response may carry `warnings`: non-fatal notes on the saved criteria (e.g. same-named counties from DIFFERENT states, like Cook, IL + Cook, MN — saved, and it matches all of them). RELAY each one with the result, not as a failure; if the selection is not what the user meant, fix it with updateFilter.

## scheduledTasks

- `createScheduledTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Schedule Ask Goliath to run `instruction` as the key owner: give exactly one of `cronExpression` (recurring, 5 fields) or `fireAt` (once), read in `timezone` (IANA). Optional `expiresAt` (it stops after). Each run asks the owner before any action (no abilities). Refused while scheduled tasks are off for the workspace.
- `deleteScheduledTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a scheduled task for good (its chat stays). To stop it for now, pauseScheduledTask. Only the task's owner or an org admin may change it (`canEdit`).
- `getScheduledTask` (query, READ) — One scheduled task by id (listScheduledTasks): its `instruction` (what Ask Goliath is told on every run), `cronExpression` and `timezone` (a one-off has `oneOffAt`), `abilities` (actions its runs may take without asking), `expiresAt`, `notifyOnlyOnChange`, its chat (`sessionId`) and whether it is `running` now.
- `listScheduledTasks` (query, READ) — Every scheduled task in your organization (yours first, then teammates', newest first), each a chat that runs Ask Goliath on a schedule as its owner: title, `status` (ACTIVE, PAUSED, PAUSED_ERRORS after repeated failures, EXHAUSTED when finished), `cadence` (ONE_OFF or RECURRING), `schedule` in words, `nextRunAt`, `lastRunAt`, `runCount`, owner, tags, and `canEdit`. Narrow by `ownerUserId`, `tag`, `statuses` or `cadence`. getScheduledTask reads one with its instruction.
- `pauseScheduledTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pause a scheduled task: it stops running until resumed. Only the task's owner or an org admin may change it (`canEdit`).
- `resumeScheduledTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Resume a paused task from its next occurrence; missed runs are not made up. Only the task's owner or an org admin may change it (`canEdit`).
- `updateScheduledTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change a scheduled task; only what you send changes. `timing` is { cronExpression or fireAt, timezone }, exactly one of the two. `clearExpiresAt: true` removes its end (do not send it with `expiresAt`). Only the task's owner or an org admin may change it (`canEdit`).

## spaces

- `addMemoryNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: add a note to a shelf the key owner may open, as a person stated it, pinned. PERSON with no `subjectId` is the owner's own, TEAM the organization's (its admins only), otherwise the EMPLOYEE or CONTACT id (listMemorySubjects). `kind` is RULE, PREFERENCE, DECISION, PROCEDURE, FACT or PROGRESS. The same words again return the existing note, re-pinned. In a chat, REMEMBER writes the person's own shelf, and TEAM for an org admin; this reaches the others.
- `beginSpaceUpload` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Start uploading a file of any type into a folder you can edit (or as `replacesItemId`'s next version). PUT the bytes to `uploadUrl` with exactly `contentType`, then call completeSpaceUpload.
- `completeSpaceUpload` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Finish an upload once its bytes are PUT: makes the file or its next version. A retry returns the same file. `actorGrn`: the dev session making it.
- `copySpaceItem` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Copy a FILE into a folder or root you can edit. The copy is yours and starts with no sharing; copying somewhere with a different audience needs MANAGER on the source unless it was already open to the whole team, and an AI agent can never make that kind of copy. Folders cannot be copied yet.
- `copyUploadedFileToSpace` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Copy an upload's original file (listFiles `uploads[].file.id`) into a folder or root you can edit, as Uploads' "Copy to My files" does: a new file of your own, independent of the upload. Needs EDITOR there.
- `createSpaceFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a folder at a root (My files or Team; `folderId` omitted) or inside a folder you can edit. A name already used there gets " (2)". Pass `creationKey` (any unique string) to make a retry return the folder it already made.
- `createSpaceTextFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Save text as a new file — a report, notes, a JSON or CSV export, a memo — in a folder you can edit. The NAME decides the type (`.md`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.txt`, `.html`, `.ts` …); binary types are refused (they are uploaded in the app). Up to 5 MB. The file is yours, labelled as made by AI for you when an agent writes it. An `.html` file saved here is an ordinary file, never a Page (Pages are made only by Ask Goliath's page tools). Pass `creationKey` to make a retry safe. Default to the person's My files unless they named a folder.
- `deleteSpaceItemsForever` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY delete items that are already in the trash — rows, every version and the stored bytes. Cannot be undone. Items not in the trash are refused (trash them first). Requires the user's explicit approval.
- `describeSpaceItem` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set (or clear, with `description` null) the short description shown under a folder or file you can edit.
- `editMemoryNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: correct a note's words (`noteId` from getMemorySubjectNotes). Saving pins it. The correction is a NEW note id, returned; the old words are superseded, not retired, so restoreMemoryNote cannot bring them back.
- `editSpaceSheetCells` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Change cells of a spreadsheet (.xlsx, CSV, TSV) by A1 address as one new version, without re-sending the sheet: each of `edits` writes `values` (rows of cells) right and down from its `start` cell — a value, a formula (`=SUM(B2:B9)`) or "" to clear — and `appendRows` adds rows under the last filled row. Every other cell, sheet, hidden sheet, number format, column width and row height stays as it was, and every formula on the sheet is computed again (one over another sheet keeps the value Excel saved), so read it back with readSpaceSheet for totals. A value is written as typed: a plain number as a number, anything else (a date, "$1,200") as text. Pass the `versionId` readSpaceSheet returned as `baseVersionId`: a save since is refused. At most 10,000 cells per call. An .xlsx with charts, images, pivot tables, comments, Excel tables, macros, conditional formatting, data validation, sparklines, links to other workbooks, data connections, slicers or embedded objects is refused (a save would drop them); cell colours and fonts are not kept, as when it is edited in Library.
- `editSpaceTextLines` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Reorganize or rewrite part of a text file by line number (from getSpaceTextLines), as one new version like a save: each edit replaces a range `startLine`–`endLine` with `text` (empty deletes it), MOVES the range before `beforeLine` (no `text` — its characters are kept exactly, nothing re-sent), or with no range inserts `text` before `beforeLine`. Every number is the read version's, the edits apply together, and every line no edit names stays exactly as it was. Overlapping ranges, a target inside a range being changed, and a stale `baseVersionId` are refused. Use it to put a long file into sections, reorder it, or fix lines without re-sending the whole file.
- `fileLibraryItemsOnContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Put Library items on a contact's Files & Photos, as the contact's Attach › From Library does: a snapshot copy of each file (up to 20, 300 MB each), and a PAGE as its PDF printed now as you see it. Ids are Library item ids (searchSpaceItems, listSpaceFolder, a page's id), never a chat artifactId. Returns each copy (`uploadedFileId`, `fileName`); undo with removeContactFiles (the copy's `uploadedFileId`). Never put a Library item on a record as a link.
- `fileLibraryItemsOnDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — fileLibraryItemsOnContact for a deal's files: a snapshot copy of each Library file, a page as its PDF. Library item ids, never a chat artifactId (that is attachDealFile). Undo with removeDealFile (the copy's `uploadedFileId`).
- `filterSpaceSheet` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — A filtered list from a spreadsheet as a NEW CSV beside it, every row read on the server. Use it for any "the rows where…" job; never retype readSpaceSheet rows into a file or split the job up. `columns`: headers to keep (`as` renames); `where`: conditions all kept rows meet (EMPTY, NOT_EMPTY, or EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS, NOT_CONTAINS with `values`). A repeated group is `{n}` ("Phone {n} Type") with `repeat` ["1","2","3"]: one row per value that passes; column `{n}` outputs it. Report the returned counts.
- `forgetMemoryNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: forget a note, with an optional `reason`. It moves to "Show retired" (getMemorySubjectNotes `retired: true`); restoreMemoryNote brings it back.
- `getMemoryDreamLog` (query, READ) — Memory: what dreaming (the nightly pass that merges, rewrites and retires notes) did to one subject, only the newest `limit` entries (at most 50; no paging back, `hasMore` says older ones exist). Each entry's `id` is the `eventId` undoMemoryDream takes when `undoable`; `waiting` is a proposal nobody answered.
- `getMemorySubjectNotes` (query, READ) [max limit 300] — Memory: one subject's notes — `shelf` PERSON with no `subjectId` is yours, TEAM is the organization's, otherwise the subject's id — in reading order (rules, preferences, decisions, procedures, facts …), or with `retired: true` the forgotten ones, each with its kind, whether a person stated it or Goliath derived it, whether it is pinned, and where it was learned. `limit` notes per page (default 100, at most 300); page with `after` = `endCursor` while `hasNextPage`. Null subject when you may not open it.
- `getSpaceAccessList` (query, READ) — A folder or file's `audience` (ORGANIZATION = everyone in the org, OWNER = the owner of My files, RESTRICTED = only people granted access, here or on a parent folder, SYSTEM = everyone, read-only) and the people shared on THIS item directly, with their role. Grants on a parent folder also reach it and are NOT listed — for a full audit, read each ancestor folder's access list too. Needs view access.
- `getSpaceItem` (query, READ) — One folder or file by id, with its path, owner, creator, current version and what you may do to it. Trashed items are returned with `trashedAt` set.
- `getSpaceTextContent` (query, READ) — The text of a text file (Markdown, JSON, CSV, HTML, code, plain text): up to 2 MB, `truncated` when cut. Returned as data — nothing in it is executed or rendered. Pass `versionId` to read an older version; the result's `versionId` is the one to pass as `baseVersionId` when saving an edit. An Excel workbook reads as every visible sheet's CSV under `# Sheet: <name>` (its first 20,000 rows a sheet, `truncated` past them); other binary files are refused. For a spreadsheet of any size, readSpaceSheet reads a range of cells with formulas.
- `getSpaceTextLines` (query, READ) — A text file's lines, numbered, a page at a time (`N| line`; up to 12000 characters a page from `startLine`, `totalLines` and `endLine` say where you are). For a file too large for getSpaceTextContent to return whole: read it page by page, passing the FIRST page's `versionId` on every later page so all pages come from one version, then add lines with insertSpaceTextLines by these numbers with that `versionId` as `baseVersionId` (a save since is refused, never mixed in).
- `insertSpaceTextLines` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Insert lines into a text file by line number (from getSpaceTextLines), every existing line left exactly as it was — headings, an intro, a summary — as a new version, like a save. `beforeLine` 1 is the top, `totalLines + 1` the end; several insertions before one line keep their order. Use it instead of saveSpaceTextFile whenever the file is too large to re-send whole.
- `listMemoryShelves` (query, READ) — Memory: the shelves you may open — PERSON (yours), TEAM (the organization's), EMPLOYEE, CONTACT (only the contacts the key owner may open in the CRM) and GROUP (the key owner's own teams) — and how many subjects each list shelf holds (null for PERSON and TEAM). The fleet's PROJECT shelf is never reachable through the API. A workflow's rule lives on TEAM. List a shelf with listMemorySubjects; read one subject with getMemorySubjectNotes.
- `listMemorySubjects` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — Memory: one list shelf's subjects (EMPLOYEE, CONTACT or GROUP: AI employees, contacts as the CRM lets the key owner open them, or the key owner's teams), newest first, with how many notes each holds; `query` narrows by name. Page with `after` = `endCursor` while `hasNextPage`. Each `subjectId` opens with getMemorySubjectNotes.
- `listRecentSpaceItems` (query, READ) — The "Recent" view: files you can see (pages and documents included), most recently CHANGED first, `limit` of them (default 100, at most 200), each with `createdAt` and `createdBy`. "What did I make yesterday / this week": `mine: true` (files the person owns: theirs, or made for them in their chats) with `createdAfter` / `createdBefore` at the window's edges in their time zone; count every row, and never present `updatedAt` as when a file was made. With `mine` or a window, only a full page (`limit` rows) can mean more.
- `listSpaceCalls` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Records › Calls: the organization's calls, newest first — direction, when, how long, whether recorded, the contact, status and disposition. Filter by `direction`, `contactId`, `handledBy` (`{ userId }` or `{ agentId }`) or `query` (the contact's name; transcripts are not searched). Read one call's recording, transcript and summary with the conversations domain's getCallRecording(callId). Page with `after` = `nextCursor`.
- `listSpaceContactFiles` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Records › Contact files: attachments and voicemails contacts sent or received, newest first. Filter by `contactId`, `dealId` (any contact on the deal), `channel`, `direction`, or `query` (the file's or the contact's name). Only files whose contact you may open. Each row's `source` says where it came from (a text thread, an email subject, a call). Page with `after` = `nextCursor`.
- `listSpaceFolder` (query, READ) — One folder's files and folders only (a root when `folderId` is omitted). Team's templates, forms, contracts, tables are never listed here: count them with listContentTemplates, listForms, listContractTemplates, listWorkflowTables before saying what Team or Library holds; an empty Team root is not an empty Team. Folders first, then files, by name; each item has `abilities`, `fileType`, size, owner, creator and `path`. Items you cannot see are not returned.
- `listSpaceItemActivity` (query, READ) — A folder or file's history, newest first — only the latest 50 events, so an older event's absence proves nothing: created, renamed, moved, edited, shared, trashed, restored, downloaded, attached — with who did it (a person, or an AI agent acting for one).
- `listSpaceItemVersions` (query, READ) — A file's saved versions, newest first — at most the newest 200: number, size, who saved it, and which is current. Read an older one with getSpaceTextContent(versionId); bring it back with restoreSpaceItemVersion.
- `listSpaceRoots` (query, READ) — Library's roots (files and folders only; Team's templates, forms, contracts and tables: listContentTemplates, listForms, listContractTemplates, listWorkflowTables). The organization's file-system roots you can open: Team (everyone in the org), your own My files (`isMine`, private), and the read-only system folders Goliath writes (Uploads, Downloads, Records). Each `id` is the `spaceId` (the root: My files, Team or a system folder) every other Library operation takes; a root's folder id is null. Start here.
- `listSpacesSharedWithMe` (query, READ) — The "Shared with me" view: folders and files teammates shared with you directly, newest first. Each item's `viewerRole` is your EFFECTIVE role on it (the share, or more through Team files, ownership or a folder above), not necessarily what the share alone granted; getSpaceAccessList lists each share's role.
- `listSpaceTrash` (query, READ) — The "Trash" view: what was trashed (by anyone) that you can see, with `trashedAt`. Trashed items are deleted for good 30 days later; restoreSpaceItems brings them back.
- `moveSpaceItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move up to 200 items into a folder or a root (`destination.folderId` omitted), all or nothing. Needs edit access on both sides; a move that would change who can see an item (out of a restricted folder, or between My files and Team) also needs MANAGER on it unless it was already open to the whole team — and an AI agent can never make that kind of move: ask the person to do it in Library. Folders move with everything in them.
- `pinMemoryNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: pin (`pinned` true) or unpin a note. A pinned note rides in every agent memory block for its shelf; dreaming never changes a pin.
- `publishSpacePage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Publish HTML as a Library Page that opens rendered (strict page CSP: HTML loading anything from outside Goliath is refused). Lands in `destination`, else your Pages folder. `actorGrn` (required): the dev session.
- `queueMemoryDream` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: queue one dreaming pass now for the key owner's own PERSON shelf (no `subjectId`), outside the nightly run: a model run that spends, at most $0.50, so it needs the person's approval. Any other shelf (TEAM, an EMPLOYEE) is Goliath-admin only. False when dreaming is off for the organization.
- `readSpaceSheet` (query, READ) — A spreadsheet's cells (.xlsx, CSV, TSV) by A1 range — any size, any sheet — instead of reading it whole: `range` B2:F40, C7, A:C (whole columns) or 5:9 (whole rows), default every filled cell; `sheet` by name, default the first. Rows come tab-separated, each led by its row number under a line of column letters, a formula as `=SUM(B2:B9) → 1200` (formula, then the value it shows); a range below row 1, or a `find`, shows row 1 first so the columns are named. Up to 12000 characters a page: `nextStartRow` says where to read on. `find` (a few words, case-insensitive) keeps only the rows holding one, with `matchedRows` counting them all. `sheets` lists every sheet's size; `truncated` means the sheet goes on past the 200,000 rows or 500 columns a read reaches. A formula over another sheet shows the value Excel last saved. Pass the result's `versionId` as `baseVersionId` to editSpaceSheetCells.
- `renameSpaceItem` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a folder or file you can edit. Refused when something in the same folder already has that name. Renaming a file can change its type (its extension).
- `restoreMemoryNote` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: bring a forgotten note back (`noteId` from getMemorySubjectNotes with `retired: true`).
- `restoreSpaceItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Restore trashed items to where they were — exactly what was trashed together comes back. An item whose folder is gone returns to its root (My files or Team); a name taken meanwhile gets " (2)".
- `restoreSpaceItemVersion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Make an older version of a file you can edit current again, as a NEW version — nothing is lost; the version it replaces stays in the history.
- `savePagePdf` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Save a PAGE as a PDF file in Library ("turn this into a PDF", "give it to me as a PDF"): printed now as you see it, saved where the files you make for this person go (their chosen folder, else My files). Returns the new file and its `path`. A snapshot: later edits to the page do not change it. Only a page prints; for anything else make a page of it first.
- `saveSpaceTextFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Save new text as the next version of a text file you can edit (earlier versions are kept and can be restored in the app). Pass `baseVersionId` — the `versionId` getSpaceTextContent returned — so a save over someone else's newer version is refused instead of overwriting it.
- `searchSpaceItems` (query, READ) — Find folders and files by NAME (case-insensitive substring) across everything you can see — at most 50, most recently changed first. Searches names only, not file contents.
- `searchSpaces` (query, READ) [max limit 25] — One search across everything the Library rail reaches — FILES (folders and files), LIBRARY (templates, contracts, contract templates, forms, tables, pages) and DATA (uploads, downloads) — matching titles and, for templates and contracts, their content. Grouped by zone, best `limit` per zone, each hit with its own id (a Library item id, a template id, a contract id …), `kind` and the app link (`target.href`) to send the person. Narrow with `zones`. Each source applies its own page's access rule.
- `searchSpaceText` (query, READ) — Find words INSIDE one text file: the numbered lines (`N| line`) holding any of `terms` (case-insensitive, matches inside longer words), with `contextLines` (default 2) around each and `…` between blocks — one read instead of paging a long file with getSpaceTextLines. Pass a few variants of the idea ("hire", "hiring", "recruit"). `matchedLines` counts every hit; `truncated` means some were left out for space — narrow the terms or read around a hit with getSpaceTextLines.
- `setAgentFilesFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Choose where the files you make in this person's chats are saved for them: a folder they can edit (`folderId`), or null for the root of My files, the default. Every later file goes there; files already saved stay where they are.
- `setSpaceAccessMode` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — RESTRICTED closes a folder or file (and everything in it) to all but its owner and the people it is shared with; INHERIT opens it back to the audience of the folder it is in, which can WIDEN who sees it. Needs MANAGER. Requires the user's explicit approval.
- `setSpaceGrant` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Share a folder or file — and everything in it — with one teammate (`userId`, an active member of your organization) as VIEWER, EDITOR or MANAGER, or stop sharing with `role` null. Needs MANAGER. Library never shares outside the organization. Requires the user's explicit approval: it changes who can see the file.
- `trashSpaceItems` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move up to 200 items (folders with everything in them) to the trash. Reversible for 30 days with restoreSpaceItems. Returns how many items went.
- `undoMemoryDream` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Memory: undo one dreaming change (`eventId` from getMemoryDreamLog): what it retired or merged comes back, what it wrote is forgotten. On a waiting trust proposal it DECLINES the step. Accepting a trust step is not an operation: the person does it in the app. Refused when a later change depends on it.
- `updateSpacePage` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Save a page's next version (`html`), rename it (`title`), or both. Pass `baseVersionId` to refuse a save over a newer one. `actorGrn` (required): the dev session.

## tasks

- `bulkCreateTasksOnContacts` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — The Contacts bulk bar's Add task: ONE task (createTaskOnContact's rules) on each of contactIds, as a background task (`bulkTaskId`, getBulkTask). assignToPointPerson gives each contact's task to that contact's point person instead of participants, and skips a contact with none. A checklist over many contacts is STILL one action per step. Confirm the task and the count first.
- `cancelTaskClear` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Undo a clear inside its 10 seconds (CANCELLED, nothing changed); ALREADY_STARTED means use restoreClearedTasks.
- `clearStaleWorkflowTasks` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Clear the key owner's stale workflow tasks: open to-dos a workflow made, on their list alone, due more than 7 days before today in timezone (an IANA zone). At most 2,000; they are removed (never completed) in 10 seconds. No read counts them beforehand: ask for the clear as described, then report taskCount (and hasMore); restoreClearedTasks undoes it. bulkTaskId null: nothing qualified.
- `completeTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark a task complete by taskId + its contactId (listMyTasks/listContactTasks). USE THIS whenever the task has a contact: it also writes the completion to the contact's timeline, and the response echoes the contact's tasks with completedAt, to confirm and show what's open. Synchronous. isCompleted: false reopens. The task must be on that contact. A task listed with contact: null has no contactId: use completeTaskById. Confirm with the user before completing anything for them.
- `completeTaskById` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Complete a task by taskId ALONE, for tasks with NO contact (listMyTasks contact: null; typically deal tasks). Returns the task. isCompleted: false reopens. It REFUSES a task with a contact (it would skip the timeline entry): use completeTask. A contact-less APPOINTMENT completes too (type says so); no task count includes it. It only completes tasks YOU are on: a non-admin key gets a permission error for someone else's. Confirm with the user first.
- `createTaskOnContact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a to-do task on a contact: one line item (title, optional description, due day, assignees) in someone's queue, checked off with completeTask; NOT a calendar event (createAppointment) and NOT a background job (bulkTasks). Requires contactId, title, dueDate, timezone. DUE DATES ARE A LOCAL DAY, NOT AN INSTANT: timezone (PST/MST/CST/EST/…) is the zone the day is read in, and it decides the TODAY/OVERDUE bucket in listMyTasks; send the user's zone, and for a day-level ask ("follow up Friday") pick an end-of-business time there, not a bare midnight. ALWAYS pass participants (getMyProfile for the key owner, listTeammates for a colleague; same-org): with none the task is UNASSIGNED and in nobody's listMyTasks, which is how a checklist silently goes missing. ONE TASK PER CALL: an ad-hoc multi-step checklist is one call per step, in order, with staggered due dates (a saved TASK_SET is one applyTaskSet call). bulkCreateTasksOnContacts puts ONE task on many contacts, so a checklist over many contacts is STILL one action per step even there; never promise a whole ad-hoc multi-step checklist in one click, here or in the app. The response echoes the contact's FULL task list: confirm the checklist from the last call's list. From a chat, a dealIds deal holding an open task refuses the create and names it: ask whether to move that one or add another, then resend with alongsideOpenTasks: true. Confirm the plan with the user before creating tasks for them.
- `createTaskOnDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a to-do task on a deal with no contact: pipeline work that belongs to the deal (order the title search, chase the inspection report). dealId from findDeals/getDeal. createTaskOnContact's rules apply: timezone is the zone the due day is read in, participants (getMyProfile/listTeammates) put it in a real queue (none = unassigned, invisible to listMyTasks), and a multi-step checklist is one call per step with staggered due dates. The response echoes the deal's full task list; getDeal `tasks` reads it too (never listContactTasks). Edit or delete it with updateTaskOnDeal / deleteTaskOnDeal. From a chat, a deal holding an open task refuses the create and names it: ask whether to move that one or add another, then resend with alongsideOpenTasks: true. Confirm with the user before creating tasks for them.
- `deleteTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — PERMANENTLY delete ONE task by taskId + its contactId: gone from the contact and the queue with NO undo, so ALWAYS confirm with the user, naming the task. Prefer completeTask if the work is DONE (keeps the record and completedAt) or updateTask if details were wrong; delete is for a task that should never have existed. Many at once is deleteTasks: for a sweep ('delete my completed tasks') list them with listMyTasks, get explicit confirmation of the list, then delete. Returns the contact's remaining tasks. The task must belong to the given contact; a task with no contact is deleteTaskOnDeal.
- `deleteTaskOnDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — deleteTask ONLY for a row whose contact is null, by taskId + its dealId; refused like updateTaskOnDeal for a contact (use deleteTask), an appointment (deleteAppointment) or a task the non-admin key is not on. Same rules.
- `deleteTasks` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — deleteTask for many: items [{ id: taskId, contactId }] (up to 200), each task on its own contact; returns deletedCount. Same rules: no undo. List them; needs their yes (Ask Goliath: bulk card). An appointment is refused (deleteAppointment).
- `listContactTasks` (query, READ) — List every to-do task on one contact (by contactId from findContacts/getContact/listMyTasks) — title, description, dueDate, completedAt, and assigned participants. Use it to review a contact's outstanding work before a call, or to find the taskId + contactId pair completeTask needs. Appointments are separate — see listAppointments.
- `listMyTasks` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — The key owner's OWN to-do queue (appointments, never OVERDUE here: listAppointments). With no participants filter it is the key owner's, for every role. Pass userIds in participants (listTeammates, same-org) for a teammate's queue or a team backlog; a MEMBER key stays narrowed to itself regardless, and a team-admin key sees only tasks on contacts THE KEY OWNER CAN ACCESS, never a complete backlog. A task with no participants is unassigned and appears in neither. Each row's participants say WHO IT BELONGS TO: read them before acting, never assume the reader owns what came back. OVERDUE is INCOMPLETE tasks due before TODAY in timezone, so a task due 9am today is not in it. For what is overdue or past due, read completed: false with dueBefore now. Also filter by taskStatus TODAY/FUTURE, completed, dueBefore/dueAfter, searchTerm; timezone sets day boundaries: EST/CST/MST/AZ/PST/HST or that zone's IANA name (America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Denver, America/Phoenix, America/Los_Angeles, Pacific/Honolulu; AZ is Arizona, which keeps MST all year); any other is refused. Rows carry dueDate, completedAt, the contact (id + name: the contactId completeTask needs; null when it has none) and deals (the dealId updateTaskOnDeal needs when contact is null). PAGING: this operation IS cursor-paginated, so "show me the rest" is answerable here. When canFetchNext is true, re-call with the SAME filters and cursor set to the LAST row's id to get the rows after it; repeat until canFetchNext is false. Forward only — there is no backwards page, so to revisit earlier rows restart from the top. Keep every filter identical between pages; changing one restarts the walk. total is the unpaged match count for the filters, so nothing is silently truncated. Order: latest-due first with dueBefore/OVERDUE and no dueAfter/TODAY/FUTURE; completed: true by latest completion; else soonest-first, open first.
- `rescheduleTasks` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move MANY tasks to ONE due date in one call ('all my overdue tasks to tomorrow'): taskIds (up to 200, from listMyTasks) OR dueBefore + expectedCount: the key owner's own open tasks due before then, never their ids (up to 500), moved only if exactly expectedCount (listMyTasks' total); dueDate (ISO) and timezone (the user's zone; every task gets it). Each task is saved as updateTask saves it (contact tasks get their UPDATED_TASK timeline entry; deal tasks, which have none, keep no old date); no contactId needed. By ids it does NOT check ownership: a teammate's contact task the key owner can see moves too, so read participants first (a dueBefore selection: only tasks the key owner is on). Every task is checked first, and nothing moves (the refusal names the ids) if any is deleted, an APPOINTMENT (use updateAppointment), on a contact the key owner cannot access, or, for a non-admin key, a contact-less task the key owner is not on. A save failing after that names the ids that did not move: retry only those. Confirm first. Ask Goliath: bulk card.
- `restoreClearedTasks` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Bring back the tasks a clear removed (for 30 days after it), by the clear's bulkTaskId.
- `updateTask` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Fix an existing task by taskId + its linked contactId (from listMyTasks or listContactTasks): title, description, taskType, dueDate (ISO, with timezone), timezone, or participants (teammate userIds from listTeammates). PATCH: only the fields you pass change; participants REPLACES the whole assignee list. UNDO: Task keeps no history, but every edit on a contact-linked task writes an UPDATED_TASK entry with oldValues to the contact's timeline (listContactActivities; one per edit, the oldest holds the original) — read it and write the old value back; never call a value unrecoverable without looking. WHOSE TASK: empty participants = UNASSIGNED, nobody's; a NON-EMPTY list that does not include the key owner is a TEAMMATE's task — an admin key may write it, but say whose first; a queue read is never proof a task is the reader's. The tool for 'push that follow-up to Friday': reschedule in place; many tasks to one date is rescheduleTasks. contactId IDENTIFIES the task's existing contact, it does NOT move it: any other is rejected, and nothing here re-links a task. Delete-then-recreate is NOT a move — it loses completedAt, the outcome, the created date and every notification and automation link — so say the task can't be moved, and rebuild it only if they ask after hearing that. To tick a task off use completeTask. A task with no contact: updateTaskOnDeal.
- `updateTaskOnDeal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — updateTask ONLY for a row whose contact is null, by taskId + its dealId (listMyTasks `deals`); one with a contact is refused (use updateTask), an appointment too, and for a non-admin key one it is not on. Same fields and rules; no timeline keeps old values: note them first to undo.

## team

- `changeTeamMemberRole` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Change a teammate's ROLE, the team page's Change Role: ADMIN (every permission, and the role every ADMIN-scoped operation needs; moving to it drops the member's permission settings) or MEMBER (what they may do is their permissions, set by an admin in the app). userId comes from listTeamMembers, which also shows the current role. It takes effect at once. Refused when it would leave the organization with no active admin (the only admin demoting themself). Organization admins only. Returns the member with their new organizationRole.
- `countOutboundTexts` (query, READ) — HOW MANY TEXTS WENT OUT in a time window — one call, exact, live (not a nightly snapshot). Use it for "how many texts did we send this week" instead of paging listInboxThreads, which is a preview feed and cannot count. WINDOW: startDate (inclusive) and endDate (exclusive) as ISO datetimes WITH an offset — resolve "this week"/"today"/"since 9/28" in the USER's timezone yourself (getMyProfile.resolvedTimezone, or the organization timezone) before calling; an offset-less time is read in the server zone. At most 93 calendar days; a wider window is REFUSED with a message (split it and add the parts). WHAT IS COUNTED: OUTBOUND texts created in the window on a line your organization owns or owned — the organization's texts whoever sent them, never another organization's. INBOUND texts are never counted. SKIPPED sends (the product declined to send — opt-out, Do-Not-Contact, throttle) are NOT counted. Each bucket reports sent (PENDING + SENT + DELIVERED: accepted for dispatch), delivered (the carrier-confirmed subset of sent) and failed (FAILED). byUser is each member's OWN sends: a text with an AI-employee or workflow stamp is never a member's, even when it went out on that member's line. otherSenders holds the rest: aiEmployees (texts an AI employee authored), workflows (texts a workflow or campaign step sent) and unattributed (a person's sends whose user was since removed). total is every bucket summed, so on an org-wide read it IS the whole organization's outbound volume. byUser is ranked by sent + failed, and a row's name is null when the user is gone; on an org-wide read only members with at least one counted text appear, while every member you NAME in userIds appears (zeros included). VISIBILITY (the inbox rule): with no userIds, a key owner who may read teammates (VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS or VIEW_ALL_PHONES; admins) gets the WHOLE organization and otherSenders; anyone else gets ONLY THEIR OWN row and otherSenders null — so a non-admin's total is their own sends, not the team's; say so rather than reporting it as the org total. Naming a teammate in userIds without either is REFUSED (an error, not zeros); with it, userIds narrows to those members and otherSenders is null. getMyCapabilities says which the key owner holds. Teammate ids come from listTeammates.
- `createGoalPlan` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Open a DRAFT goal plan for the month containing periodStartDate, seeded with the active plan's commission goals; an existing draft is returned instead. Only a draft is edited; publishGoalPlan makes it the active plan. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `createTeam` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Create a team (name, optional description, emoji, color, memberUserIds). Organization admins only.
- `createTeamInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Create a team-member invitation. userType: ADMIN or MEMBER (default MEMBER). Either emails (each address is EMAILED its own single-use invite: say so) or isPermanent: true, the reusable link, which emails nobody and invites as MEMBER (a live older link is returned with its own role). No email-less one-time link exists. Never paste an acceptUrl in chat (it goes by email); show the permanent link only on request.
- `createTeammateGoalPlan` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): createGoalPlan for them.
- `deletePersonalGoal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a personal goal from a DRAFT plan for good; updatePersonalGoalStatus ARCHIVED keeps it. goalPlanId/goalId from getGoalPlan. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `deleteTeam` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Delete a team for good. Refused while workflows, forms or filters still use it: pass getDeletionImpact's dependencyResolution (targetKind USER_GROUP). Organization admins only.
- `deleteTeammatePersonalGoal` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): deletePersonalGoal for them (for good; ARCHIVED status keeps it); ids from getTeammateGoalPlan.
- `emailPermanentTeamInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Email the organization's PERMANENT (reusable) invite link to 1–50 addresses per request; duplicates are sent once. The link must already exist — create it once with createTeamInvite (isPermanent: true), or find it in listTeamInvites (isPermanent: true, isAlive: true); when the organization has none this is refused rather than minting one. Returns the permanent invitation and its acceptUrl.
- `getGoalPlan` (query, READ) — Your goals for the month containing periodStartDate (YYYY-MM-DD): draftPlan (being edited) and activePlan (published), either null. Commission goals are targetCents per pipeline (null pipelineId = all pipelines); metric EARNED counts won deals, TOTAL adds pending ones. Personal goals are free text. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `getMemberActivity` (query, READ) — WHAT ONE PERSON DID in a time window — "what did I do today", "how was my week", "what did Sam get done yesterday" — in ONE call: their own texts (sent/delivered/failed), calls (outbound, inbound, connected, conversations, talkSeconds), emailsSent, notesWritten, tasksCreated, appointmentsBooked, tasksCompleted and dealStageMoves. Counts only, live. Use it instead of combining countOutboundTexts, getTeamCallStats and timeline reads. WINDOW: startDate (inclusive) and endDate (exclusive) as ISO datetimes WITH an offset, resolved in the USER's timezone (getMyProfile.resolvedTimezone): "today" is local midnight to now or to the next midnight. At most 93 calendar days; wider is REFUSED. WHO: omit userId for the key owner; naming a teammate needs VIEW_ALL_PHONES (org admins hold it) and is REFUSED otherwise. WHAT IS THEIRS: only work the person did themselves; an AI employee, a workflow or an outreach tool working on their behalf is never counted, nor is a bulk action or import, and notes, tasks and appointments count when made by hand in the app (texts and calls follow countOutboundTexts and getTeamCallStats). emailsSent is outbound mail from their connected mailbox. tasksCompleted is tasks they are on that were completed in the window (who ticked it is not recorded). dealStageMoves is moves they made by hand. For the records themselves, read the timeline or lists afterwards.
- `getTeamActivityTimeseries` (query, ADMIN) [rate-limited] — Daily team activity rows for a reporting period (same period values as getTeamAnalyticsOverview) — calls, texts, emails, tasks, appointments, active agents, and new leads per day. For charting trends. Nightly (asOfDate), never today. Admins.
- `getTeamAnalyticsOverview` (query, ADMIN) [rate-limited] — Team performance (SEVEN_DAYS | FOURTEEN_DAYS | THIRTY_DAYS | YEAR_TO_DATE; default THIRTY_DAYS): totals, deltas, per-agent rows. NIGHTLY as of asOfDate, never today; say which numbers are nightly and which live (getTeamCallStats, countOutboundTexts). filterContacts awaitingReply: unanswered texts/emails. avgSpeedToFirst{Call,Message}Minutes: minutes from a lead being ASSIGNED to the member to their first call / text or email.
- `getTeamCallStats` (query, READ) — Per-member CALL COUNTS AND TALK TIME in a time window — one call, exact, live (not a nightly snapshot). The answer to "break down team talk time this week" and "who made the most calls". WINDOW: startDate (inclusive) and endDate (exclusive) as ISO datetimes WITH an offset — resolve "this week"/"since 9/28" in the USER's timezone yourself (getMyProfile.resolvedTimezone, or the organization timezone) before calling. At most 93 calendar days; a wider window is REFUSED with a message. WHAT IS COUNTED, per member, over the organization's calls created in the window and handled by that member: outboundCalls and inboundCalls (every status, missed and unanswered included); connectedCalls = status COMPLETED, the same "connects" the team analytics pages count as completedCalls; conversationCalls = connected AND (lasted at least 120 seconds, or a transcript or AI summary exists), team analytics' conversationCalls; talkSeconds = summed duration of the connected calls (a connected call with no recorded duration adds 0) — divide by 60 or 3600 yourself. A call an AI EMPLOYEE handled is not counted for any member, even when it carries one (a screened call the AI took over), and calls with no member at all (imported dialer history) are not counted — so these are human calling numbers, and can be lower than the analytics pages, which credit AI-handled calls to the member. byUser is ranked by talkSeconds (name null when the user is gone); totals sums the rows. On an org-wide read only members with at least one call appear; every member you NAME in userIds appears (zeros included). VISIBILITY (the inbox rule): with no userIds, a key owner who may read teammates (VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS or VIEW_ALL_PHONES; admins) gets every member; anyone else gets ONLY THEIR OWN row — say so rather than presenting it as the team. Naming a teammate in userIds without either is REFUSED (an error, not zeros). getMyCapabilities says which the key owner holds. Teammate ids come from listTeammates.
- `getTeammateGoalPlan` (query, ADMIN) — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): getGoalPlan for them.
- `getTeammatesByIds` (query, READ) — Resolve teammate USER IDS to names — pass userIds, get back id, firstName, lastName, email for each. This is the id → person lookup, and the ONLY one: listTeammates searches names, emails and phone numbers and returns at most 50 rows, so it cannot answer "who is <uuid>" in an organization larger than that. Reach for this whenever you are about to REPORT a bare user id to someone — a filter's `userId`, a task's `participants`, a note author — because "owned by 4f3c…" is not an answer a person can act on. Ids outside your organization are rejected; nothing here reveals a user in another org.
- `getTeamMemberCapabilities` (query, ADMIN) — A teammate's permissions, as Manage permissions on their row shows them: every capability they HOLD (one missing is one they do not have). userId comes from listTeamMembers. An Admin holds all of them. Read it before grantTeamMemberCapability or revokeTeamMemberCapability to say what changes. Organization admins only; your own permissions are getMyCapabilities.
- `grantTeamMemberCapability` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Turn ONE permission on for a teammate, a switch in Manage permissions on their row. Off for a member unless granted: VIEW_ALL_CONTACTS, VIEW_ALL_DEALS, VIEW_ALL_PHONES (call and text from any team number), CONTRACTS_VIEW, CONTRACTS_MANAGE. On unless an admin turned them off (granting one gives it back): CAN_SKIPTRACE, CAN_EXPORT, CAN_WORKFLOW (run workflows), VIEW_TEAM_DIRECTORY (see who else is on the team), VIEW_TEAM_CALENDARS (see teammates' calendars on the Team calendar), VIEW_TEAM_CALLS_TEXTS (read teammates' calls and texts in the Team inbox; email only from mailboxes their owner shares), and the app sections CAN_USE_AUTOMATIONS (and workflow operations), CAN_USE_FILES, CAN_USE_MARKETPLACE, VIEW_ORGANIZATION_SETTINGS, CAN_USE_API_KEYS. Their role does not change: this is the answer to "give X access to Y" for a Member, never a promotion to Admin. userId comes from listTeamMembers. An Admin already holds every permission, so it changes nothing for one. Takes effect within a minute. Organization admins only; the person approves it on a card naming the teammate and the permission.
- `listTeamInvites` (query, ADMIN) — List the organization's team invitations — pending (isAlive: true) and spent/revoked (isAlive: false), single-use and permanent; acceptUrl is a full link. A live single-use invite is someone not yet joined; remove one with revokeTeamInvite.
- `listTeammates` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Fuzzy-search ACTIVE teammates by name, email or phone (optional searchTerm; omit it for an alphabetical page). This is the PICKER, not the roster: it returns at most `limit` rows (default 20, maximum 50), ranked by match quality, and SUSPENDED members are excluded at the query — so a page that comes back full may be a truncated page, and a person missing from it may be removed rather than absent. An empty or partial result is NOT 'no such person': they may be invited and not yet joined, so an admin reads listTeamInvites before saying nobody by that name is on the team. For the whole team, for anyone's role, or to tell a current member from a removed one, use listTeamMembers; to resolve a bare user id, use getTeammatesByIds. Use the returned userId with updateContact (addCollaborators), assignContact, and the userIds filter on findDeals.
- `listTeamMembers` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — List EVERY member of your organization with their membership facts — the roster. Offset-paginated (offset + limit; limit defaults to 50, maximum 100; newest member first), so walk pages until one comes back short rather than treating the first page as the whole team. Each row carries organizationRole (ADMIN | MEMBER — ADMIN is the role every ADMIN-scoped operation requires of the key owner) and organizationMembershipStatus (ACTIVE | SUSPENDED). REMOVED MEMBERS ARE INCLUDED: a suspended person is still a row here, so filter on organizationMembershipStatus before reporting who is on the team, and never read a row's presence as "currently works here".
