Optional searchTerm is a SUBSTRING match on name and email for a plain term and on the id for a uuid; a phone number is matched ONLY when the term is a complete US number (a partial such as the last four digits is searched as a name/email substring and finds no phone — an empty page there is not evidence nobody has the number). Plain terms rank by similarity; a complete email, phone or uuid keeps newest-first and can also return members whose value contains it. Capabilities are not here: the key owner's own come from getMyCapabilities, and an admin reads a teammate's with getTeamMemberCapabilities. Use listTeammates instead when you only need to pick one active person by a partial name.
- `listTeams` (query, READ) — The organization's teams (groups of teammates a contact or form can be given to), newest first, with their members; `search` narrows by name.
- `publishGoalPlan` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Publish a DRAFT plan (planId from getGoalPlan): it becomes the month's active plan, the one Agent Performance tracks, and the previous active plan is archived. Confirm with the user first. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `publishTeammateGoalPlan` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): publishGoalPlan for them; confirm with the user first.
- `removeTeamMember` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Remove a teammate from the team, the team page's Remove from team. It is a SUSPENSION, not a delete: they lose access at once and stop using a seat, but stay on listTeamMembers as SUSPENDED and restoreTeamMember brings them back. On the way out their open tasks go to YOU (the key owner), their contacts' point-person seats are released (a contact left with no agent gets you), and they are taken out of the workflow steps and lead-routing forms that named them. Restoring does NOT hand any of that back; the person approves it on a card. Optional reason is kept on the member. You cannot remove yourself. Organization admins only. The result reports what the handover did: handover (NOT_NEEDED | REASSIGNED | REMOVED | FAILED), reassignedTaskCount, releasedContactSeatCount, handedOverContactCount, and openWorkTruncated / openWorkFailed when some work is still theirs; tell the user those.
- `resendTeamInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Re-send a team invitation by id (from listTeamInvites) — the same invitation email goes out again to the same address. The invitation itself is unchanged: same id and acceptUrl, so use this for "she never got the email" rather than creating a second invite. Only a LIVE invitation WITH A RECIPIENT can be re-sent (isAlive: true, email set): a spent or revoked one is refused — create a new one with createTeamInvite instead — and a PERMANENT link is refused too, because it has nobody to send to; email that one with emailPermanentTeamInvite.
- `restoreTeamMember` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Restore a removed (SUSPENDED) teammate to the team, the team page's Restore to team. They get access back and use a seat again; work handed over when they were removed stays where it went. Refused when the organization cannot take another member (its seat policy). A member who is already active is left as is. Organization admins only.
- `revokeTeamInvite` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Revoke a team invitation by id: the one this chat created, else match it in listTeamInvites. The permanent link only when named. The link stops working (isAlive false). Own organization only.
- `revokeTeamMemberCapability` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Turn ONE permission off for a teammate, the same switch and the same capabilities as grantTeamMemberCapability, which turns it back on. Their role does not change. An Admin holds every permission whatever is stored, so read getTeamMemberCapabilities first and never offer one for an Admin (their role changes first). Organization admins only; the person approves it on a card naming the teammate and the permission.
- `setTeamMembers` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Set a team's members. memberUserIds (active teammates, listTeamMembers) REPLACES the whole member list. Organization admins only.
- `updatePersonalGoalStatus` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Mark a personal goal ACTIVE, COMPLETED or ARCHIVED, on a draft or active plan (not an archived one). goalPlanId/goalId from getGoalPlan. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `updateTeam` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Edit a team (teamId from listTeams); omitted fields are untouched. memberUserIds (active teammates, listTeamMembers) REPLACES the whole member list. Organization admins only.
- `updateTeammatePersonalGoalStatus` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): updatePersonalGoalStatus for them; ids from getTeammateGoalPlan.
- `upsertCommissionGoal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set a commission target on a DRAFT plan: targetCents (> 0, cents), metric EARNED | TOTAL, pipelineId (null = all pipelines). Pass the goal's id to change it; without one a new goal is added. goalPlanId/goalId from getGoalPlan. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `upsertPersonalGoal` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add (no id) or edit (id) a personal goal on a DRAFT plan: title, optional description and displayOrder. goalPlanId/goalId from getGoalPlan. Your own plan; a teammate’s is the *Teammate* op (ADMIN).
- `upsertTeammateCommissionGoal` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): upsertCommissionGoal for them; ids from getTeammateGoalPlan.
- `upsertTeammatePersonalGoal` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — A teammate's plan (`userId`, ADMIN; the key owner must be an org admin who sees the team directory): upsertPersonalGoal for them; ids from getTeammateGoalPlan.

## workflows

- `addLibraryFileFromArtifact` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Add a file the person attached (or you made) to the content library by its artifactId, under a name, with an optional description and folderId (listContentTemplateFolders). Templates can then attach it.
- `applyTaskSet` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Run a whole TASK_SET against a contact: creates every step as a task in one call, all assigned to the acting user and linked to the contact (and any dealIds). Each step's due date is ITS OWN relative offset from one shared “now”, snapped to its own preferred time-of-day; the referenced template's timing is ignored inside a set. Steps run in due order and stop at the FIRST failure, KEEPING what was created: the payload carries the tasks that landed plus failedStep { index, taskTemplateId, message }, and it does NOT error, so read failedStep before reporting success. Rejects a template not of type TASK_SET. Set ids: listContentTemplates(type: TASK_SET).
- `applyTaskTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Run a TASK template against a contact: creates one task, assigned to the acting user, linked to the contact (and any dealIds). Title/description render the template's merge fields + spintax against that contact, and the RELATIVE dueOffset resolves from now, snapped to its preferred time-of-day. Rejects a template not of type TASK. overrides { title?, description?, endDate?, timezone?, taskType?, autoCompleteOnNoteAdded?, autoCompleteOnReassignment? } replace what the template would produce for this one apply: an endDate override skips the relative due date, and what is not overridable (origin, supporting-file links, the contact/deal links) still applies. Send timezone with any endDate override: the task is stored and read back in it, and without it keeps the TEMPLATE's zone, so an instant chosen in one zone can render as a different day. Template ids: listContentTemplates(type: TASK). A whole saved SOP is applyTaskSet, not this per step.
- `bulkPauseWorkflowRuns` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pause many runs at once by explicit id (cap 500). Ids that are ineligible or not visible to you are counted in skippedCount, not errored.
- `bulkResumeWorkflowRuns` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Resume many paused runs at once by explicit id (cap 500). Ineligible or not-visible ids are counted in skippedCount, not errored.
- `createContentTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a reusable template. type is EMAIL | SMS | NOTE | TASK | TASK_SET. The nested input carries name, bodyContent (merge fields and [a|b] spintax allowed) and subjectContent (email only). Its merge fields are the vocabulary of WHATEVER NODE renders it, since a template has no domain of its own: from a CONTACT node or applyTaskTemplate, the CONTACT vocabulary listed under updateWorkflowGraph ({{firstName}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{userFirstName}}, …); from an APPOINTMENT text node, that PLUS the appointment fields ({{appointmentStartTime}}, …). Quote merge fields to the person as [First name], not raw keys, unless they check spelling. Keys match EXACTLY and case-sensitively, with no dotted or snake_case form: {{merge_fields}} and {{contact.firstName}} send the literal braces. TASK (the checklist/SOP step under Automations → Templates) takes input.taskConfig; bodyContent holds the task description and the due date is RELATIVE, resolved when applied. TASK_SET is a whole SOP: bodyContent "", no taskConfig, and input.taskSetSteps of 1–25 steps (their rules are on the input shape), applied in one call with applyTaskSet.
- `createContentTemplateFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a template folder. Pass parentFolderId to nest it under another folder.
- `createOrReturnWorkflowDraft` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Idempotent "edit": return the existing DRAFT version under this workflow, or clone the live (or most recently paused) version into a fresh DRAFT. Use the returned id with updateWorkflowGraph. WEBHOOK SECRETS ARE REDACTED. A `send_webhook_action` step's `config.auth.secret` reads as the literal `__GOLIATH_WEBHOOK_SECRET_REDACTED__` — never the credential, never a value to quote or reason about. Send it BACK UNCHANGED in updateWorkflowGraph to keep the stored secret, and a different string only when the user is deliberately rotating it. Never invent, guess or complete a replacement: that overwrites a working credential. The sentinel on a step with no stored secret behind it (a step you just added, or a graph read so long ago its node ids rotated) is REFUSED: re-read the graph and carry it from the fresh copy. 
- `createWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a workflow automation: a new group plus its initial DRAFT version. workflowDomain is CONTACT | DEAL | PROPERTY | APPOINTMENT | EVENT. There is no workflowType (sending it is a 400 unknown_variable). Which channels a workflow messages on is not a property of the group: it is the union of the channels its communicationConfig configures with its own text_action / email_action steps, reported as `channels` on this response and on getWorkflow (listings carry `channelsAcrossVersions`). A create seeds NO communication config unless a templateId brings one; adding a text or email step with updateWorkflowGraph seeds that channel's editor defaults, and a sender must still be chosen before promoting. Optional templateId seeds the draft graph from a registered starter template. Edit the draft with updateWorkflowGraph, whose step vocabulary (listed there) is far more than texts and emails, then ship it with promoteWorkflowDraft. Optional sendWindow is the starting SENDING SCHEDULE (updateWorkflowSendWindow's shape); absent takes the template's when it has one, else the platform default. The graph never carries it: change it later with updateWorkflowSendWindow. THE SKIP-TRACE WORKFLOW (watches property signals in a buy-box and skip-traces each owner into a contact) is created with `workflowDomain: "PROPERTY"`, `systemCategory: "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE"` and `templateId: "property_signal_skip_trace"` together, as the onboarding package does. Its draft is a trigger, a create-contact step and an end. It is promoted only with TWO triggers: a MUTATION trigger whose filter names at least one property signal type (`propertySignalTypes`, in ONE flat OR group: a run starts when a property gets any of them), and a MATCH trigger whose filter is an AND root carrying a top-level `spicyLeadScore` minimum (the buy-box; places and property types are optional conditions beside it). Read the draft with getWorkflowVersionGraph, replace its trigger with those two through updateWorkflowGraph, then promoteWorkflowDraft; getWorkflow.draftValidation names whichever is missing. Each run spends a skip-trace credit. Its daily run limit is the ORGANIZATION's, shared by every skip-trace workflow: setSkipTraceDailyCap sets it, getWorkflowThrottleUsage reads it.
- `createWorkflowFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create an empty workflow folder, optionally nested under parentFolderId, and return its id.
- `deleteContentTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a template by id; returns the remaining templates. One that workflow steps or task sets still use is REFUSED without a dependencyResolution: call getDeletionImpact (targetKind CONTENT_TEMPLATE) first, then pass its impactVersion and one replacement template of the same type; every step and task set is repointed at it before the delete. Omit it for a template nothing references.
- `deleteContentTemplateFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a template folder by id. Subfolders inside it are also deleted; templates in the deleted folders become ungrouped rather than deleted. Returns the remaining folders.
- `deleteEventWorkflowPayloadSample` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete one pasted example payload for good (sampleId from listEventWorkflowPayloadSamples). A `run:` sample is NOT_FOUND.
- `deleteLibraryFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Take a file out of the library for good (its name and description go). The upload itself stays, and templates that attach it keep working.
- `deleteWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a workflow (the UI's "Delete"): archives the group, pauses any active version and PERMANENTLY stops its in-flight runs; everyone mid-sequence drops out and restoring the workflow does not bring them back. Confirm with the user first. The re-queried group shows archivedAt. restoreWorkflow undoes the archive (the workflow comes back paused).
- `deleteWorkflowFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Delete a workflow folder by folderId. Its direct workflows and child folders move to its parent; nothing inside is deleted.
- `deleteWorkflowTable` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Archive a Workflow Table. Refused while a workflow, message or form still names one of its columns; the refusal names them.
- `discardWorkflowDraft` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Discard the workflow's current DRAFT version, if any. Idempotent — a no-op when there is no draft.
- `duplicateWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Duplicate a workflow into a fresh group with the given name, as a paused/draft copy that never starts by itself. The copy inherits `systemCategory`, so a duplicated "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE" workflow is another one of those. Two are REFUSED: "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" (a copy would fire for the source reminder's appointments; create a new one with createAppointmentReminder) and "INTEGRATION_LEAD_HANDLING" (one per integration, and a copy binds to nothing; set it up from Integrations).
- `enrollInWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Enroll MANY contacts in one CONTACT workflow's ACTIVE version: the app's bulk "Add to workflow" on the Contacts table. ASYNC bulk task: returns a bulkTaskId before anything runs; poll getBulkTask. TWO selection forms, never combined. EXPLICIT: `contactIds`. FILTER-BACKED: `filterId` (a saved contact filter from listContactFilters; a teammate's private one is refused) OR `filterTree` (inline, saveFilter's CONTACT DSL, parsed STRICTLY) with `selectCount: N`, the first N matches in the filter's default order; `excludeIds` drops contacts from that window. NO select-all: a filter without selectCount is refused, so size the window with countContacts first. CAP: 20,000 contacts per call (the app's bulk-action limit, charged on the ids or selectCount); split a bigger audience with excludeIds or narrower filters. The workflow must be CONTACT with an ACTIVE version (PROPERTY or DEAL is refused; one record at a time is triggerWorkflowRun). Each enrolled contact starts a run that can TEXT or EMAIL them under the workflow's send window, daily caps and the org's sending safety. State the workflow and contact count to the user and get a go-ahead BEFORE submitting.
- `getContentTemplate` (query, READ) — Fetch one reusable template by id — name, type (EMAIL | SMS | NOTE | TASK), body, and folder. EMAIL/SMS/NOTE templates are the saved message content workflows reference; TASK templates are reusable checklist/SOP steps you instantiate with applyTaskTemplate.
- `getWorkflow` (query, READ) — Fetch one workflow automation by group id: status, versions, the live version, the pending draft and draft validation. `channels` reads ONE version, the most recently PUBLISHED whatever its status now (active, paused or suspended), else the pending draft; null when that graph could not be read, [] when the group has no version. `channelsAcrossVersions` reads every version not deleted, superseded ones and drafts included (never null), so the two differ whenever another version messages on a channel the published one does not. Both are CONFIGURED channels, not sending: a paused or suspended head answers its channels while sending nothing, so read `status` before calling a workflow actively texting or emailing. `draftValidation.carrierRisk` is the draft's text copy scored for carrier filtering, riskiest first (`isFallback`: the step's backup text). It never blocks the promote: reword a medium or high one with rewriteWorkflowDraftTextStep first. `sendWindow` is the workflow's live SENDING SCHEDULE (a graph `triggerWindow`'s shape plus `timezoneMode`, see updateWorkflowGraph), or null for the platform default (Mon–Fri 09:00–19:00 org time). It belongs to the workflow, not a version: every run reads it on its next send, whichever version it started on. Only updateWorkflowSendWindow changes it; no graph write can. `stepKinds` names step TYPES, not waits or copy: never say a pending draft matches or changes the published one before reading BOTH with getWorkflowVersionGraph (paused: the published one is in `versions`, not `currentVersion`). TRIGGERS ARE NOT THE ONLY WAY IN. Steps in OTHER workflows enroll records into this one: a PROPERTY `create_contact_action` (the contact it creates), a `trigger_contact_workflow_action` (start another workflow), and an EVENT `find_create_contact_action` / `event_find_property_action`. A workflow whose only trigger is {type: "manual"} is normal when it is fed that way: never call it idle or unreachable from its triggers alone. getDeletionImpact(targetKind: WORKFLOW_GROUP, targetId: <this group id>) says whether anything references it: its WORKFLOW_AUTOMATION group counts REFERENCES (each step, trigger or filter in each live version naming this one, so one workflow can count more than once), not names. To see WHICH workflows feed it, scan other workflows' graphs (getWorkflowVersionGraph) for a step naming this group id. TO CHANGE WHAT A WORKFLOW DOES (add a condition, change a trigger, narrow who it acts on), edit its graph: createOrReturnWorkflowDraft → updateWorkflowGraph → promoteWorkflowDraft, then resumeWorkflow if it was paused. Pausing only stops it. E.g. a PROPERTY workflow can require a motivation signal before it creates or texts anyone: a `conditional` step on the `hasSignal` or `propertySignalTypes` property filter fields (listFilterFieldNames lists them) ahead of the `create_contact_action` step. Never tell a user restricting outreach this way needs human review: it is a graph edit.
- `getWorkflowStats` (query, READ) — Performance summary for one workflow (by group id), lifetime, dry runs excluded: run counts by outcome (active/completed/paused/stopped/failed), messages sent, reply rate with its positive/negative split, bounce rate and last-run time. The headline "how is this automation doing" answer.
- `getWorkflowTable` (query, READ) — One Workflow Table with its rows, paged by `rowLimit` (default 100, at most 500) and `rowOffset` — keep reading while a page comes back full (`rowCount` excludes the DEFAULT row, which pages like any other): each row's key (`key`, `keyLabel`, the `keyLevel` of the fallback chain it sits on, and its `keyParts`), whether it is the DEFAULT row (used when nothing matches), and its cells by `columnId`. Rows need an org admin (the Tables editor's gate); null when the table is not in your org. Which row one record gets is previewWorkflowTableLookup's answer, never a key matched by eye.
- `getWorkflowThrottleUsage` (query, READ) — Daily send-limit usage for a throttle-backed workflow (by group id): usedToday vs dailyCap and a per-day history over the last `rangeDays` (1–90, clamped). Null for a workflow with no throttle (only skip-trace-category workflows have one). Answers "am I near my sending limit?".
- `getWorkflowVersionGraph` (query, READ) — Fetch one workflow VERSION by workflowAutomationId (from getWorkflow.versions/currentVersion/pendingDraft) with its full node/edge graph: the superjson-serialized WorkflowGraph updateWorkflowGraph writes back. Its `triggers` array shows what starts runs; updateWorkflowGraph documents the trigger shapes, how to add or remove them, and the FULL step vocabulary (far more than text steps). Read `graph.config` before answering about BEHAVIOUR rather than steps: exit conditions, sender selection and the trigger operator live there, not on a node. The SENDING schedule does not: it is getWorkflow.sendWindow. `inWords` states the triggers and the stop rules in words, and `inWords.names` names every tag, list, teammate or stage the graph holds by id (a tag and a list share names: read `kind`). Describe the workflow from these, never from its name or description; keep every stop rule unless the person asks to drop that one. TRIGGERS ARE NOT THE ONLY WAY IN. Steps in OTHER workflows enroll records into this one: a PROPERTY `create_contact_action` (the contact it creates), a `trigger_contact_workflow_action` (start another workflow), and an EVENT `find_create_contact_action` / `event_find_property_action`. A workflow whose only trigger is {type: "manual"} is normal when it is fed that way: never call it idle or unreachable from its triggers alone. getDeletionImpact(targetKind: WORKFLOW_GROUP, targetId: <this group id>) says whether anything references it: its WORKFLOW_AUTOMATION group counts REFERENCES (each step, trigger or filter in each live version naming this one, so one workflow can count more than once), not names. To see WHICH workflows feed it, scan other workflows' graphs (getWorkflowVersionGraph) for a step naming this group id. TO CHANGE WHAT A WORKFLOW DOES (add a condition, change a trigger, narrow who it acts on), edit its graph: createOrReturnWorkflowDraft → updateWorkflowGraph → promoteWorkflowDraft, then resumeWorkflow if it was paused. Pausing only stops it. E.g. a PROPERTY workflow can require a motivation signal before it creates or texts anyone: a `conditional` step on the `hasSignal` or `propertySignalTypes` property filter fields (listFilterFieldNames lists them) ahead of the `create_contact_action` step. Never tell a user restricting outreach this way needs human review: it is a graph edit. WEBHOOK SECRETS ARE REDACTED. A `send_webhook_action` step's `config.auth.secret` reads as the literal `__GOLIATH_WEBHOOK_SECRET_REDACTED__` — never the credential, never a value to quote or reason about. Send it BACK UNCHANGED in updateWorkflowGraph to keep the stored secret, and a different string only when the user is deliberately rotating it. Never invent, guess or complete a replacement: that overwrites a working credential. The sentinel on a step with no stored secret behind it (a step you just added, or a graph read so long ago its node ids rotated) is REFUSED: re-read the graph and carry it from the fresh copy. 
- `getWorkflowVersionStats` (query, READ) — Performance summary for one VERSION (by workflowAutomationId, from getWorkflow.versions), the shape of getWorkflowStats: compare a new version against the one it replaced. Also `sendingCapacity`: how many of its runs are queued behind sending capacity now (`queuedRuns`), the soonest `nextAttemptAt` and the main `reason` (DAILY_CAP | SEND_WINDOW | WINDOW_LIMIT | OUT_OF_SMS_CREDITS); null when nothing is queued. It tells a workflow that is PACING from one that has stopped.
- `listContentTemplateFolders` (query, READ) — List the organization's shared content-library folders (id, name, parentFolderId, displayOrder) with per-kind template counts and a file count. Counts are DIRECT — what is filed in that folder itself, not its subtree — so a parent's own counts do not include its children's.
- `listContentTemplates` (query, READ) — List the organization's reusable templates, optionally filtered by type (EMAIL | SMS | NOTE | TASK) or folderId. Pass type: TASK to find the saved checklist/SOP steps that applyTaskTemplate runs against a contact. Returns the template id to use in getContentTemplate / updateContentTemplate / applyTaskTemplate.
- `listEventWorkflowPayloadSamples` (query, READ) — The example payloads an EVENT workflow has received or been given (what its sender POSTs), to map trigger fields from. Empty for any other domain. A `run:` id belongs to a run and cannot be deleted.
- `listLibraryFiles` (query, READ) — List the content library's files (Automations → Templates → Files): id, name, description, folderId, contentType. Optional folderId (listContentTemplateFolders) and name search.
- `listWorkflowFolders` (query, READ) — List the organization's shared workflow-folder tree (id, name, parentFolderId, displayOrder, itemCount). The compatibility field `ready` is always true on current servers.
- `listWorkflowGraphRevisions` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — A workflow's save history, newest first: when, who (`source` HUMAN, AGENT or SYSTEM; `actorName`; `agentRunId` for an agent's save), the version it wrote, and `diff`: what changed against the save before (`summary`, edited steps and keys, settings, rename). A save through this API, the assistant's included, reads HUMAN under the person's name. When `diff.hasPredecessor` is false there is no earlier save to compare (its first save, or older history trimmed): go by `summary`, never the lists, as that save's change. `absorbedUnjournaledEdits` means it includes edits made outside the editor; say so.
- `listWorkflowPerformance` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — Scoreboard: the org's workflows (paginated, non-archived) each with headline stats — total/active/completed runs, reply rate, and last-run time. One call to answer "which of my automations are running and how are they doing". Drill into any with getWorkflowStats. Each row carries `channelsAcrossVersions`: the channels the workflow messages on (TEXT, EMAIL, both, or [] when it messages nobody; never null), the same answer the app's Channel filter gives, so read it to PICK workflows out of a list. It spans EVERY version not deleted: the published one, the ones it superseded and an unpublished draft. getWorkflow.`channels` reads ONE: the most recently PUBLISHED version whatever its status (active, paused or suspended), else the pending draft. NEITHER says it is SENDING: a paused or suspended head keeps its configured channels while sending nothing. Read `status` for that.
- `listWorkflowRuns` (query, READ) [max limit 34] — List runs of one workflow version (by workflowAutomationId), optionally by run status (PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | PAUSED | STOPPED | FAILED | NOT_ENROLLED). Run ids feed pauseWorkflowRun / resumeWorkflowRun / stopWorkflowRun. Report each run's reason rather than saying reasons are unavailable: a NOT_ENROLLED run was refused at the door and never entered, and its `stoppedReason` says why (a STOPPED run's says why it was withdrawn); a PAUSED run carries `pausedReason`, plus `sendFailureCode` (the carrier code, e.g. 30007) when a failed text paused it; a PENDING run whose next send waits carries `queuedSend.reason` (DAILY_CAP | SEND_WINDOW | WINDOW_LIMIT | OUT_OF_SMS_CREDITS, null when the wait has no nameable cause; current only on a PENDING run, so go by `pausedReason` on a PAUSED one) and `queuedSend.nextAttemptAt`. A FAILED run has no reason field and an older STOPPED run's `stoppedReason` can be null: say it is not recorded, never invent one. Reasons are raw codes.
- `listWorkflows` (query, READ) [max limit 50] — List the organization's workflow automations (paginated, non-archived by default). Returns the group id to use in getWorkflow and the other workflow operations. `status`, `domain`, `name` (a name search, any case) and `triggerType` (on a version of that status; hidden groups included) narrow rows and `total`. For a workflow the person named, pass their words as `name` and compare each row's `name` for the exact one, reading every page `total` counts before calling one row the only exact match (names are not unique). Each row carries `channelsAcrossVersions`: the channels the workflow messages on (TEXT, EMAIL, both, or [] when it messages nobody; never null), the same answer the app's Channel filter gives, so read it to PICK workflows out of a list. It spans EVERY version not deleted: the published one, the ones it superseded and an unpublished draft. getWorkflow.`channels` reads ONE: the most recently PUBLISHED version whatever its status (active, paused or suspended), else the pending draft. NEITHER says it is SENDING: a paused or suspended head keeps its configured channels while sending nothing. Read `status` for that.
- `listWorkflowTableChanges` (query, READ) [max limit 100] — A Workflow Table's change history, newest first: who saved what and when, how many columns and rows changed. `rowId` narrows it to one row. Page with `after` = `nextCursor`. Same gate as the rows.
- `listWorkflowTables` (query, READ) — The organization's Workflow Tables (not archived), by name: each table's key (what rows are matched on — `keyKind`, e.g. COUNTY_FIPS, STATE, ZIP, FIELD_PATH, and its fallback levels in `keyShape`), its columns (with each column's `tokenKey`, the merge field a message uses, and a SELECT column's options) and `rowCount`. No rows — read one table's rows with getWorkflowTable. Paged: `limit` (default 20) and `offset`; a page shorter than `limit` is the last.
- `moveAndResumeParkedRuns` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Restart the runs a publish paused on a workflow (getWorkflow runsParkedByPublish; mostly publishes before 2026-10-23, which paused everyone in flight): moves up to `limit` (at most 200) of them onto the live version, still paused, and once `remaining` is 0 resumes them all on the live version, so their messages go out again. A run on a step the live version no longer has is finished instead (`completed`). Call again while `remaining` is above 0, unless `stuck`: then those runs cannot be moved, so say how many and stop. Offer it only when the person asks about that workflow's paused runs, and say how many people will start getting messages again first. With no live version it does nothing and returns `notLive`: the workflow has to be turned back on first. A run whose contact replied while parked stays paused.
- `moveContentTemplateFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move a template folder under another, or pass parentFolderId null for the root. Not into its own subtree.
- `moveContentTemplateToFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move a template into a folder by id. Pass folderId null to ungroup it.
- `moveLibraryFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — File a library file into a folder (listContentTemplateFolders), or folderId null for the root.
- `moveWorkflowFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move a workflow folder under another folder, or pass parentFolderId null to move it to the root.
- `moveWorkflowToFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Move a workflow into a folder by folderId (from listWorkflowFolders), or folderId null to ungroup it. Creates nothing: an unknown id is NOT_FOUND, so make the folder with createWorkflowFolder first. Refuses a workflow the caller cannot edit, and one a campaign manages (its sequence belongs to the Campaigns editor).
- `patchWorkflowGraph` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Edit a workflow version's graph by sending ONLY THE CHANGE (updateWorkflowGraph writes a whole new graph). Ids come from getWorkflowVersionGraph and CHANGE ON EVERY SAVE: patch again from the response's `graph`. `graphPatch`: ops applied in order, all or nothing. Ops: {op:"updateNode", id, config?, edits?} | {op:"addNode", node:{type, config}, after?: nodeId, onEdge?: edgeId} | {op:"removeNode", id, keepChild?} | {op:"addEdge", edge:{parentNodeId, childNodeId, config?}} | {op:"updateEdge", id, parentNodeId?, childNodeId?, config?} | {op:"removeEdge", id} | {op:"updateConfig", config} (graph.config) | {op:"addTrigger", trigger:{config}} | {op:"updateTrigger", id, config} | {op:"removeTrigger", id}. A `config` is a JSON merge patch: objects merge, null deletes a key, other values (arrays too) replace; {op:"updateNode", id, config:{seconds:86400}} makes a wait one day. `edits`: [{field:"textBody", find, replace}], each find exactly once in that text. `after` inserts after a step with one path out, `onEdge` on a branch edge; with neither the step is unconnected. A new edge out of a condition sets its config (`eval`/`path`). removeNode rejoins the flow; a condition needs `keepChild` (its other paths go). New step types: updateWorkflowGraph's NODE VOCABULARY. Saves like updateWorkflowGraph (same refusals, flags, draftValidation); a no-op patch is refused.
- `pauseWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pause the ACTIVE version of a workflow — no new runs will start. pauseInFlightRuns=true also pauses runs already in flight; false lets them finish. No-op if nothing is active. TO CHANGE WHAT A WORKFLOW DOES (add a condition, change a trigger, narrow who it acts on), edit its graph: createOrReturnWorkflowDraft → updateWorkflowGraph → promoteWorkflowDraft, then resumeWorkflow if it was paused. Pausing only stops it. E.g. a PROPERTY workflow can require a motivation signal before it creates or texts anyone: a `conditional` step on the `hasSignal` or `propertySignalTypes` property filter fields (listFilterFieldNames lists them) ahead of the `create_contact_action` step. Never tell a user restricting outreach this way needs human review: it is a graph edit.
- `pauseWorkflowRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Pause one in-flight run (PENDING or RUNNING → PAUSED). Get run ids from listWorkflowRuns.
- `previewWorkflowAiText` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Preview what an AI text step with this systemPrompt would write to 1 to 5 contacts, through the real generation path. Sends nothing and saves nothing; one model call per contact. Each result has generatedText, or a declineReason (the prompt's own rules said not to text them, a valid no-send), or an errorMessage.
- `previewWorkflowTableLookup` (query, READ) — Call this before you say which row, or which value, a named contact, property, deal or appointment gets from a table: a county or key guessed from an address is not the answer. Which row of one Workflow Table a run on a record would use, and each column's value by `columnId` (names from getWorkflowTable): `input` takes `workflowTableId` and a `contactId`, `propertyId`, `dealId` or `appointmentId`, resolved exactly as a workflow run resolves it (fallback levels, ranges, composite keys). `match` DEFAULT means no key matched and the default row answered; NONE means nothing answered. `missingSubjects` names records the key needed and the record could not reach. Same gate as the rows.
- `promoteWorkflowDraft` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Ship it: promote the workflow's current DRAFT to ACTIVE (live). MIGRATE (default) moves in-flight runs to the new version: on a kept step they continue with the new copy, on a removed step they finish, held by a pause they wake. PAUSE keeps them on the old version, whose copy they send if resumed. Fails without a valid draft (see getWorkflow.draftValidation).
- `recordEventWorkflowPayloadSample` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Save an example payload (a JSON object, what the sender would POST) on an EVENT workflow, so its fields can be mapped before anything arrives. Starts no run, sends nothing, leaves the graph alone. Refused on a workflow the key owner cannot edit.
- `renameContentTemplateFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a template folder by id.
- `renameWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a workflow version (by workflowAutomationId) and optionally update its description. The workflow list shows the display version's name.
- `renameWorkflowFolder` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a workflow folder by folderId. Duplicate sibling names are rejected rather than merging subtrees.
- `reorderWorkflowFolders` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Persist the display order for one sibling set. Pass parentFolderId (null for root) and every folderId in that set.
- `restoreWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Undo deleteWorkflow: bring a deleted (archived) workflow back to the list, by group id, to edit again. Nothing turns on: every version stays paused until resumeWorkflow, and the runs the delete stopped stay stopped. Use it rather than a duplicate when a just-deleted draft is the one you need. A workflow not deleted comes back unchanged. Refused for an event workflow (its webhook address was retired) and an appointment reminder.
- `restoreWorkflowVersionAsDraft` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Roll back: copy an OLDER version (workflowAutomationId from getWorkflow.versions) into the DRAFT, then publish it with promoteWorkflowDraft. Only a PAUSED version a later-published one superseded (compare publishedAt); the most recently published one is refused (resume it with resumeWorkflowVersion). REPLACES the current draft and its edits, so confirm first when one exists. Nothing goes live.
- `resumeRunsPausedWithWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Wake the runs a workflow pause left parked (getWorkflow runsPausedWithWorkflow) on a workflow that is live again; each restarts at the step it reached and its messages go out. Never turns the workflow on: refused when it has no live version. Runs paused for any other reason stay paused. Say how many runs first.
- `resumeWorkflow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Resume the most-recently-paused version of a workflow, and wake the runs the workflow pause parked (getWorkflow.runsPausedWithWorkflow counts them): each continues at the step it had reached, and runs paused for any other reason (by hand, a publish, a failed send, a reply) stay paused. With a version already active it flips nothing but still wakes that version's workflow-paused runs; no-op if none is paused.
- `resumeWorkflowRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Resume one paused run (PAUSED → PENDING) and kick its executor.
- `resumeWorkflowVersion` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Resume a specific PAUSED version (by workflowAutomationId), pausing the active sibling first. Promotion is ONE-WAY, so this is NOT a roll-back: it REJECTS a version that is not PAUSED, and it REJECTS a SUPERSEDED version (one with a later-published sibling) with "Only the most recently published version can be resumed." So it can only activate the most recently PUBLISHED paused version. Do not treat resumeWorkflow as an equivalent fallback: it picks the most recently PAUSED version (a different ordering: a version paused later may have been published earlier) and NO-OPS when an active sibling exists, where this op pauses that sibling first. To bring an OLDER version back, use restoreWorkflowVersionAsDraft, never a retry of this op.
- `rewriteWorkflowDraftTextStep` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — The publish dialog's "Rewrite for me": reword one DRAFT text step to lower its carrier-filter risk, saved on the draft. Pass a getWorkflow.draftValidation.carrierRisk row's nodeId, and its body as expectedBody; only for a medium or high `band`. A row with a templateId is the template's copy: reword it with updateContentTemplate instead (here it is refused). status REWRITTEN (body saved), else NO_BETTER_REWRITE or STEP_CHANGED (it no longer carries expectedBody), the step unchanged. Never publishes.
- `saveWorkflowTable` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create a Workflow Table (`workflowTableId` omitted) or replace an existing one's name, description and columns. The key (`keyKind`, `keyFieldPath`) is fixed at creation; fallback levels may be added later. A column left out of an update is DELETED, with its value in every row — permanent, so this needs the person's approval. Rows are written with saveWorkflowTableRows. Returns the table's shape.
- `saveWorkflowTableRows` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Create or replace rows (`rows` — a row is replaced WHOLE, never merged) and delete rows (`deleteRowIds`) of one table in a single write; a deleted row or a replaced cell is gone for good, so this needs the person's approval. Pass `expectedUpdatedAt` = the table's `updatedAt` from getWorkflowTable so a save over someone else's newer edit is refused (CONFLICT) instead of overwriting it. Returns the table's shape and `rowCount`; read rows back with getWorkflowTable.
- `setSkipTraceDailyCap` (mutation, ADMIN) [idempotent] — Set the ORGANIZATION's daily cap on property-signal skip-trace workflow runs: the `dailyCap` getWorkflowThrottleUsage reports, shared by every PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE workflow in the org. Each run spends a skip-trace credit, so this arms real spend: ADMIN scope, and the key owner must be an org admin. A whole number, 1 to 1,000,000,000; a raise reaches an org already capped today within minutes. Returns the new cap. State the old cap (getWorkflowThrottleUsage on a skip-trace workflow) and the new one first; when it already is that cap, change nothing. Run it as a write code task whose approvedLive names it: that draws the person's yes/no card showing both caps, and only that yes sets it, so never ask a yes of your own. Never lower it unless asked: a lower cap throttles every skip-trace workflow.
- `stopWorkflowRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Permanently stop one run — PENDING, RUNNING or PAUSED (terminal: a stopped run cannot be resumed). A no-op on a run already STOPPED; an error on one that already COMPLETED, FAILED or was NOT_ENROLLED.
- `triggerWorkflowRun` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Manually start one run of a workflow's ACTIVE version against a record. recordId must match the workflow's domain: a contactId for CONTACT workflows, propertyId for PROPERTY, dealId for DEAL, taskId for APPOINTMENT.
- `updateContentTemplate` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Update a template by id (name, body, subject). The id is nested in the input object.
- `updateLibraryFile` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Rename a library file or change its description (fileId from listLibraryFiles); description null clears it.
- `updateWorkflowGraph` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Replace a workflow version's node/edge graph AND its triggers (to edit, patchWorkflowGraph). Edit the DRAFT (createOrReturnWorkflowDraft). A PAUSED version is writable too, off the normal path. workflowGraph is the superjson-serialized WorkflowGraph shape returned by getWorkflowVersionGraph; send back a modified copy of the existing graph, same serialized field names (node/edge ids are caller-minted strings). An OMITTED top-level key keeps its stored value ({nodes, edges} alone is valid); a trigger needs only {config}; a text/email step lacking its channel's communicationConfig gets the editor default. A valid graph needs at least a trigger node and an end node joined by an edge; every node is {id, type, config} and every edge is {id, config, parentNodeId, childNodeId} (edge config is {} except conditional branches, below; a Wait until signed step: {path}). NODE VOCABULARY — every authorable step type, generated from the registry the writer validates against. STRUCTURAL STEPS — the same in every domain. "trigger" (The graph entry point. Every valid graph has exactly one, and every run starts here. It does not decide WHEN the workflow fires — the graph-level `triggers` array does. config {} — no settings); "conditional" (A two-way fork decided by a filter. Skipped once signed or closed. config {reason});THAT FilterGroup IS THE FULL SAVED-FILTER VOCABULARY FOR THE DOMAIN, not an automation-only subset. For CONTACT, PROPERTY and DEAL that vocabulary is enumerable: listFilterFieldNames returns it complete, and any field it lists a conditional can evaluate. NEVER tell a user an automation cannot consider some attribute without reading that list for the workflow DOMAIN first — "it cannot see it" is usually a domain mismatch (last sold date, year built, estimated value are PROPERTY fields, not contact fields). APPOINTMENT conditionals take their own full filter group, but listFilterFieldNames and listFilterFields do not accept APPOINTMENT. That is a gap in DISCOVERY, never evidence about the capability: copy a conditional already in the graph; if you cannot confirm a field, say so rather than that it cannot be done. AI CONDITION CONTEXT — an "ai_conditional" step's `context` is a Context Layer SELECTION, not a list of ids: an object keyed by any of contact | deal | property | appointment | organization, each mapping to that source's slice flags (e.g. {contact:{includeTextMessages:true, includeNotes:false}}). A key's PRESENCE includes it; {} means that source with its defaults. Only sources the RUN carries an id for resolve (a CONTACT run has a contact), so one the domain never carries renders nothing. The step is available on APPOINTMENT graphs although "conditional" is not. A sixth key `event` is EVENT-only, and on an EVENT graph the ONE source that renders (an EVENT run carries no record): {mode:"whole"} sends the whole webhook body, {mode:"fields",paths:["call.outcome"]} only the named accessor paths (1-25, none reading the whole payload; use whole for that). `{event:{}}` is refused, and `event` on any other domain is a publish error. EVENT MAPPINGS — two rules mapping rows are REJECTED for. (1) EXACTLY ONE destination and EXACTLY ONE value source per row: a customFieldMappings row names either a customFieldId or an attributionKey (one of the org's reserved, listing-hidden attribution fields: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, gclid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, li_fat_id, landingUrl, referrerUrl), and either an accessor or a literalValue. A row naming two of either is dropped and counted at execution, never resolved by precedence. (2) A tagMappings row resolves its value to a tag or list BY NAME and CREATES one when the org has none, bounded at 25 distinct values per row and refusing values that are obviously not category names (a uuid, an email, a url, a long-digit platform id, over 80 characters); tags and lists share one org-wide namespace, so a name a list holds cannot become a tag and that row is dropped. Both counts ride the run's FIND_CREATE_CONTACT_RESOLVED audit event as tagsWritten/tagsDropped. MERGE FIELDS — the COMPLETE per-domain vocabulary a body may draw on. Substituted at run time: textBody, textBodies, emailBody, emailSubject, a Slack block's text and a Slack button's url, plus a deal node's title and a task node's name and description. NOT substituted, so braces there are left alone: a generative node's systemPrompt (an instruction to a model, not a template) and a deal node's description. Keys are matched EXACTLY, case-sensitively. There is NO dotted record namespace: {{contact.address1}}, {{contact.firstName}} and {{deal.title}} are not merge fields (the SLACK keys below are literal dotted names, not a namespace you may extend). Do not infer a key from another domain's spelling either — the shapes differ (CONTACT has contactPropertyAddress, PROPERTY has full_address); use a key off this list or none. An unknown token is NOT a missing variable and does NOT render blank: braces reach the reader verbatim (except a notify step on OMIT_BLANKS, which blanks them). promoteWorkflowDraft REFUSES a draft carrying one in a SCANNED FIELD — textBody, textBodies, emailBody (including one stored as emailBodyFormat "TIPTAP_JSON", whose merge fields are document pills rather than braces and are read as such), the WORKFLOW-LEVEL email subject on communicationConfig and a NODE'S OWN one, a fallbackTextBody under SEND_FALLBACK, an email step's fallbackEmailSubject and fallbackEmailBody, under SEND_FALLBACK and only where a PRIMARY can miss a variable (the EFFECTIVE subject — the workflow's unless sendInSameThread is false — or a body the graph carries), a Slack block's text or its button url, a deal node's title and fallbackDealTitle on a CONTACT or DEAL graph, and an inline task node's name and description — and updateWorkflowGraph returns that same judgement as workflowGroup.draftValidation on every write — a reading of the GROUP'S DRAFT, which is the version you just wrote whenever you followed the normal path and edited the draft. Edit a PAUSED version instead and the field still answers about the draft, so it is null when there is none and about a DIFFERENT version when there is: it is not a verdict on your write in that case, and nothing in the response says so ({isValid, errors}, each unrenderable token named with the field it sits in and the supported key it most likely meant). READ IT on the response to the write and fix what it names, rather than discovering it when activation fails. THAT LIST OF SCANNED FIELDS IS CLOSED, and it is still SHORTER than the list of fields that are substituted. Anything substituted at run time but absent from it is checked by nothing, so a clean draftValidation is not evidence about it — check those against the vocabulary below yourself. What remains unscanned, and NOT an exhaustive list: a PROPERTY create-contact step's deal title and fallback title (substituted against the NEW CONTACT and the workflow user, not against the PROPERTY graph's own vocabulary, so the gate has no single vocabulary to judge them by and deliberately does not try); a Slack reply node's message; and any body that lives in a referenced templateId rather than in the graph — the graph then carries no body for the scan to look at. In every one of them a wrong key promotes clean. What the recipient sees differs by path: most render through the token renderer and arrive as LITERAL BRACES, but a Slack reply node's message is interpolated by its own function, which replaces any {{slack.<field>}} it does not recognise with an EMPTY STRING — so a typo there shows as missing text, not a broken template. PROPERTY: {{line1}}, {{line2}}, {{propertyCity}}, {{state}}, {{zip}}, {{full_address}}, {{property_url}}, {{beds}}, {{baths}}, {{sqft}}. CONTACT: {{fullName}}, {{firstName}}, {{lastName}}, {{contactUrl}}, {{contactPhoneNumber}}, {{contactEmail}}, {{contactPropertyAddress}}, {{contactPropertyStreet}}, {{contactPropertyFullAddress}}, {{contactPropertyCity}}, {{contactPropertyZipcode}}, {{contactPropertyAuctionDate}}, {{contactPropertyForeclosureStage}}, {{contactPropertyAmountOwed}}, {{userFullName}}, {{userFirstName}}, {{userLastName}}, {{userPhoneNumber}}, {{userEmail}}, {{userOrganizationName}}. DEAL: {{dealTitle}}, {{dealUrl}}, {{dealPipelineName}}, {{dealStageName}}, {{dealPrice}}, {{dealCloseDate}}, {{dealPropertyLine1}}, {{dealPropertyLine2}}, {{dealPropertyCity}}, {{dealPropertyState}}, {{dealPropertyZip}}, {{dealPropertyFullAddress}}, {{dealPropertyCounty}}, {{dealPropertyApn}}, {{dealPropertyLegalDescription}}, {{dealContactFullName}}, {{dealContactFirstName}}, {{dealContactLastName}}. APPOINTMENT: {{appointmentStartTime}}, {{appointmentEndTime}}, {{appointmentMeetingLink}}, {{appointmentLocation}}, {{appointmentDurationMinutes}}, every CONTACT key above. EVENT: no merge fields at all — a {{...}} in an EVENT body is an ACCESSOR PATH into the inbound webhook payload (see the EVENT actions above), not a merge field, and is never validated against this vocabulary. SLACK: {{slack.text}}, {{slack.userName}}, {{slack.channelName}}, {{slack.permalink}}. CONTRACT: {{contractName}}, {{contractSigningLink}}, {{contractUrl}}, {{contractSignedPdfUrl}}, {{contractDeclineReason}}, every CONTACT key above, every DEAL key above.  Two conditional keys, and neither is legal on every graph: {{agentName}} resolves ONLY where the graph's TEXT sender is a marketing campaign, and a contact CUSTOM FIELD — addressable as {{ContactTag_<uuid>}}, where the uuid is a CUSTOM-FIELD id from listContactCustomFields and NOT a tag id from searchContactTags, however much the prefix suggests otherwise (ContactTag is the table that stores tags, lists and custom fields alike, so the GRN is named for the table rather than for the thing; a real tag id passes the shape check, is accepted by promote, and renders empty) — resolves ONLY on CONTACT and APPOINTMENT and CONTRACT graphs, the ones a send loads contact context for — and on an APPOINTMENT graph only from the TEXT REMINDER, which renders with the task, the contact and the user. An appointment Slack post loads the task alone, so every CONTACT key there, tags included, renders literally even though promote accepts it: the gate judges per DOMAIN, and this is the one place a domain is wider than one of its own nodes. Used outside its condition either one is unrenderable and blocks promote exactly like an unknown key.Triggers are managed through the `triggers` array: each entry is upserted by its id (mint a UUID to add one) and omitted entries are detached; only `config` syncs (`name` is cosmetic). Trigger config shapes: {type: "manual"}, {type: "created"}, {type: "mutation", filter: <FilterGroup>}, {type: "match", filter: <FilterGroup>}; a CONTACT match whose root AND holds one lastActivityAt or lastNoteTakenAt {comparison:"MORE_THAN", number, timeUnit} and no other relative date is the "no activity for N days" trigger: an hourly sweep enrolls each contact as it crosses N; CONTACT-only: {type: "inbound_text"|"inbound_call", twilioPhoneNumberIds: [...]}, {type: "inbound_email", connectedAccountIds?: [...]}; EVENT workflows have exactly one trigger shape, {type: "event_received"} — the workflow's minted webhook URL is the trigger. Minimal valid drip example (node/edge shape): nodes: [{id:"n1",type:"trigger",config:{}}, {id:"n2",type:"text_action",config:{mode:"single",textBody:"Hi {{firstName}}"}}, {id:"n3",type:"wait",config:{mode:"fixed",seconds:172800,interruptEnabled:false,interruptFilter:{id:"f1",operator:"AND",conditions:[],groups:[]}}}, {id:"n4",type:"end",config:{}}], edges: [{id:"e1",config:{},parentNodeId:"n1",childNodeId:"n2"}, {id:"e2",config:{},parentNodeId:"n2",childNodeId:"n3"}, {id:"e3",config:{},parentNodeId:"n3",childNodeId:"n4"}]. PROMOTE GOTCHA: promoteWorkflowDraft rejects the default UNSET sender (SenderNotChosen): set a real one (e.g. {type: "POINT_PERSON"}) first; getWorkflow.draftValidation lists every blocker. GRAPH CONFIG — `graph.config`, beside `nodes`/`edges`/`triggers`, NOT per-node. Every domain: `triggerOperator` "AND"|"OR" (several triggers: all or any); `triggerWindow`, which limits when ENROLLMENT may happen; `exclusiveEnrollment` true STOPS the record's runs in every OTHER workflow (not prior versions of this one) when it enters this one — "only one campaign at a time per lead"; inert on EVENT graphs. `activation.triggerEligibleRecordsNow` is RETIRED: parsed, read by nothing, enrolls nobody — do not write it. CONTACT graphs add `exitConditions.exitConditionTypes` — any of "any_inbound_communication", "inbound_text", "inbound_email", "contact_archived", "deals_closed", "outbound_from_human", "outbound_from_ai_employee", "outbound_from_other_workflow", "contact_signed_contract", "property_listed", "property_off_market", "property_sold"; there is no per-node way. The "outbound_from_*" three end the run when somebody ELSE messages the contact, never on its own workflow group's message. On APPOINTMENT omit `exitConditions`: any value, even {}, is rejected. `communicationConfig` is NOT contact-only: APPOINTMENT graphs take it too, for a reminder's quiet hours and sender. SEND WINDOW — the sending schedule is not in the graph: getWorkflow.sendWindow, set by updateWorkflowSendWindow. It and `triggerWindow` share the shape {timezone, days:[{day:"MON".."SUN", intervals:[{start:{hour,minute}, end:{hour,minute}}]}], timezoneMode?}. Each day has its OWN intervals ("weekdays 9-5, Sundays 12-4" is one window); an absent day is CLOSED, an interval never passes midnight (end after start), and an end of {hour:0,minute:0} is midnight at the END of the day. The older {daysOfWeek?, startTime?, endTime?} (same hours each listed day) is still ACCEPTED, but `days` is what is stored and read back. `hour` AND `minute` are BOTH REQUIRED on each time ({hour:9} alone is rejected). Clock times, not offsets: "weekdays 9-6" is one `days` entry per MON..FRI with {start:{hour:9,minute:0}, end:{hour:18,minute:0}}. No sending schedule falls back to MON-FRI 09:00-19:00 org time, so no weekends. `timezoneMode` is WHOSE clock the times are read on: "BUSINESS" the ORGANISATION's timezone, read live (New York when unset), and what an OMITTED `sendWindow.timezoneMode` reads as; "RECIPIENT" each recipient's zone from their phone's area code (toll-free, non-NANP numbers and EMAIL fall back to the organisation's); "CONFIGURED" the window's own `timezone`, fixed. `triggerWindow.timezoneMode` accepts only "RECIPIENT"|"CONFIGURED" ("BUSINESS" there is REJECTED by the graph parser) and is inert: its times are always read in its own `timezone`. The window is final: no quiet hours are added on top, for TEXT or EMAIL. SENDER — `communicationConfig.text.sender` / `.email.sender`, both allowed at once. A mode name alone is not a valid sender: most modes carry required fields. TEXT: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"MEETING_OWNER"} (appointment graphs) | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]} | {type:"LOCAL_PRESENCE", scope, fallback} — LOCAL_PRESENCE picks a team number whose area code matches the recipient, and BOTH scope and fallback are required: scope is {kind:"ALL_TEAM"} | {kind:"SPECIFIC", fromPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"EXCLUDE", excludedPhoneNumberIds}, and fallback is {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]}. EMAIL: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"IDENTITY", fromEmail, fromClientId} | {type:"RANDOM_IDENTITY", identities:[...]}. UNSET is the creation default and activation is GATED on replacing it. A text_action or email_action step may carry its OWN `config.senderOverride` for that step alone (absent inherits): the same TEXT/EMAIL arms above except MEETING_OWNER and LOCAL_PRESENCE. SYSTEM CATEGORY — createWorkflow's separate `systemCategory` variable, not in the graph. All domains allow CUSTOM workflows, PROPERTY included, so `null` is right unless creating from a category's template. PROPERTY's one category, "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE", is the skip-trace template with a daily cap; a `null` PROPERTY workflow is blank, started manually, by a property signal or by a custom data pipeline. A non-null `systemCategory` requires a `templateId` on the same create ("A system-category workflow needs a template id" does NOT mean property workflows are unsupported). NO domain offers "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" or "INTEGRATION_LEAD_HANDLING" at create (READ-only): a reminder is createAppointmentReminder (isGlobal: true for every appointment); the second is minted on integration connect, then LOCKED against adding, deleting or rewiring a step.
- `updateWorkflowPriority` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set a workflow's priority, which orders its runs and sends against the org's other workflows (higher wins): 1.25 Low, 1.5 Normal (the default), 1.75 High; any other value is refused. Takes a version id (getWorkflow currentVersion.id); applies to the whole workflow at once, live included, and re-orders sends already queued.
- `updateWorkflowSendWindow` (mutation, WRITE) [idempotent] — Set the workflow's SENDING SCHEDULE, the hours its messages may go out. It belongs to the workflow (group id), not a version, so it applies to the LIVE workflow at once: every run reads it on its next send, whichever version it started on, with no draft or promote. A run already waiting for the old schedule's next opening keeps that wait and re-checks when it wakes. `sendWindow` is {timezone, days:[{day:"MON".."SUN", intervals:[{start:{hour,minute}, end:{hour,minute}}]}], timezoneMode?}, with the rules updateWorkflowGraph gives under SEND WINDOW; an absent day is CLOSED, and a window naming no days or hours is refused. null clears it to the platform default (Mon–Fri 09:00–19:00 org time). Read it from getWorkflow.sendWindow. The ONLY way to change it: updateWorkflowGraph refuses a graph carrying a different one.
